analysis.name: Andrew Dell'Antonio
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easiest and best class ever. Professor is so sweet and very understanding that students have other commitments outside of his class. Attendance is not mandatory and all assignments are self-paced and can be completed by yourself. Lowkey can finish class within the first 2 weeks of semester with the exception of concert report and reflection.

The class isn't marked as async, but you can complete all of the assignments  asynchronously for full credit. His Zoom lectures aren't mandatory, nor do you need to watch them to complete any assignments. This all makes an A extremely easy. Dr. Dell'Antonio is also clearly very passionate, and the assignments are interesting and quick to complete.

Intro to Western Music was an incredibly easy class, almost all of your grade consists of self-paced assignments that are just a completion grade, and the rest requires you to write a couple short reflections, but those are graded very leniently and with clear instructions. highly recommend
Easiest A in all of UT. Everything is online, self-paced. Just ready to be spammed by hella canvas notifications.

Dr. Dell Antonio is the best! I took him and Dr. Gabrillo for Music and Culture and they were both amazing together. Learned so much and you can really see how they care about us as freshmen.  Yeah there were lots of small assignments every week but they're so easy to do, like took me 10min per task. Music and Culture is an easy A tbh. Super fun.

analysis.name: Richard Albert
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Albert is one of my favorite professors at UT. This lectures are mostly discussion discussion based, so be sure to participate! Tests make up 80% of your grade make sure you know the material or go to office hours. His lectures are very interesting and makes you think about stuff you normally wouldn't care to think about.

Dr Albert has been the best teacher I have had at the university. He is very passionate about his work, and you can tell through his lectures. At first, the three-grade criteria was scary, but engaging in class and creating a study group helped me succeed. I cannot recommend this class enough!

I highly enjoyed this class, the lectures were engaging and small group discussions were always fruitful. Note taking is simple and Albert loves to talk to students as long as you put in effort to talk to him. This class is graded on few things however. Your final is 50% of your grade, so prepare wisely (the exams and essays are all open note).

There is a lot of reading in the class, but come on, it is a law professor. This guy is helping write the constitutions of Jamaica & US Virgin Islands. Even if you don't want to pursue a career in law, it is important to know how we can change the course of our nation through formal and informal amendments. If you want to pursue law PLEASE TAKE IT!

Professor Albert is one of the most knowledgeable people I have ever met. I started off not liking him, but the more I was in his class the more I began to enjoy it. You are graded on 3 exams and 1 essay, which are graded pretty harsh, but its not impossible. The content is a little boring, but its worth it because you will feel so smart after.

analysis.name: Ishraq Al-Awamleh
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is the best professor I have had at UT. I did poorly in Calc 1 and she made this class a breeze. She's exceptionally nice and her teaching skills are excellent. She gives us tips and tricks, which are SO HELPFUL. She takes notes with us in class, making it easy to follow along. I could rave about her forever. Go to class and do the work, easy A

Dr. Ishraq was truly one of the best professors I have had at UT. I came into this class with no prior knowledge of calculus, but she made the topics easy to understand and was always ready to help if someone didn't understand something. Tests are fairly easy if you take notes and DO THE REVIEWS. Homework wasn't bad and she drops the lowest one.

Dr. Al-Awamleh Is a great professor and if you have the option to take her please do! The class is definitely difficult but she makes it really easy and goes over the concepts in depth to make sure everyone is able to understand. The exams are tough but not too hard at all. As long as you study, go to class, and participate you'll be good!

Dr. Al-Awamleh is the most caring, nurturing, and kind-hearted professor I've ever had. She makes confusing concepts very understandable, really cares about individual students' success, and gives a lot of time for office hours, etc... Her exams and quizzes are straightforward and very similar to lecture notes. Hard to find a prof like this.

Very nice, caring professor, but definitely the hardest among all the biz calc profs. This is the only M408Q class where attendance is mandatory, where you have to show your work on the worksheets, and you are forced to take the final. The class is still an easy A, and the professor is a great teacher, but it is more work than the other sections.

analysis.name: Anita Latham
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 183 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Latham is the nicest professor ever. She always asked all of us how our day was, "Too much for a Monday (her catchphrase)"? She lectures over the main ideas, not so much the details. But that's Biology. We have to read! If you don't like to read, I'd suggest you take another Bio prof. Overall, you'll enjoy being her class. She's great.

Don't make the same mistake I did. I devoted all my energy to past material and it cost me. The final is mostly cellular respiration, photosynthesis, energy/enzymes, and biotechnology. Focus mostly on these topics! The final is alright. The thing that makes it different from past exams is that it's mostly application. In conclusion, study 3 weeks!

Dr. Latham is so funny and nice. I love the fact that she's the only professor that asks us often how our day was. Don't go to her office hours. She say's that the CA's are better than her. Go to CSS! They don't gave you the answers but make you think. This prepares you greatly for the test. All in all, her test can be challenging. So, study alot!!

DONT take this 1st semester if you can avoid it!!! Keep track of due dates b/c they aren't consistently on one day and for example Latham will say it's due in 5 days when its due in 2 days. Just check canvas, youll be good. For exams learn the ws objectives like the back of your hand, know discussion ws and you can get an A. She gives candy!!!!!!

I love Dr. Latham and her whole team of TA, CA! Came with little biology background but succeeded in this course thanks to how amazing she is. She's so caring, funny, and an amazing lecturer. I have hard time focus during class and it was fast paced too, but there is recorded video lectures that is super helpful! SHES THE MOST CARING PROFESSOR EVER

analysis.name: Megan Allen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Yes, I know I got a C+; however, Professor Allen is truly a sweetheart! She cares about her students and her teachings and is always willing to help during office hours! I feel like just going to the office for hours helped because I received extra credit for it! I highly recommend taking Professor Allen!

Tax is just a difficult class, but Professor Allen made it relatively straightforward. There's a lot of assignments, so it can feel overwhelming at times, but compared to the other tax professors, I've heard her exams are much easier. Definitely a doable class if you put in the work.

The professor is very nice, gives a lot of extra credit, and is very easy to follow. The first half of the class is fast paced, but you'll get used to it quickly. There's not really any pop quizzes but the assignments you work on in class can get taken for a quiz grade. Exams can be tough but extra credit covers it and there can also be a curve.

Tax is hard itself but her lectures and notes make it a lot better. She explains things well and does alot of examples in class so the concepts are understood. There is alot of material and it does become dense but her exams generally use practice exam questions and test on the easier of materials for any unit. She also does alot of extra credit.

It was a tough class, but shes the GOAT. Class was fun and engaging, I know how to do some taxes, how to evade them while avoiding detection from the service, and how to make that money clean through investments in restaurants or laundromats. she provides plenty of resources to prepare for exams, answers any questions, and is just great! recommend!

analysis.name: Ahmad Agbaria
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He was the worst professor I ever had. He changed the rubric on the tests with no clear direction on anything on paper. Avoid at all costs if trying to find a good government class as the GOV366T label for this class is misleading due to this class being solely a history class. He is terrible with technology and does not respond to emails.

The professor is nice and willing to help answer some questions, but wow, his class is extremely unorganized. He posts nothing but the readings on canvas. He goes very fast during lectures and doesnt post the lecture slides on canvas. Doesnt do reviews for the midterm/final. You wont really know your grade until after the semester is over.

Worst class I've taken at UT. "Lectures" are unorganized and rushed slideshows with dense slides that aren't even shared. No Canvas use. Expectations for writing assignments are unclear. Grades rely heavily on the exam and final (no final review guide either). Avoid unless you have prior knowledge on the topic or grad-level writing.

AVOID. While he held office hours, he lied about pretty much anything he said regarding the course format. My grade was up in the air until the final week of the class so that was a bummer too. Sure he was nice but did not teach properly. His lectures were all over the place and for a history class there was no chronological order.

Terrible professor due to his constant rants during the lectures which causes him to rush his lectures. He constantly changes the class format and rubrics verbally and does not post lecture slides or a final review despite rushing. Office hours do not help at all as he constantly changes what he says so cannot trust office hours.

analysis.name: Kiril Avramov
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing and engaging lectures. Clearly an expert on the topic. Truly cares about students, however it was too easy to succeed. I loved the content but wasn't meaningfully tested on it, so I did not grasp itwell. His lecture style works best in smaller class sizes. First prof I would ever say needed to give more assignments to reinforce the content.

Dr. Avramov is one of the best professors I have taken at this school. This class is interesting at times but can often be boring and he kept everyone engaged. There is a lot of reading but quizzes and tests are open note/book so you don't have to do it all the time, but it helps. Other assignments are short discussion posts. Take this class!

Avramov is one of the greats! Engaging lectures, fascinating material, really genuine guy. My only critique is that the class allows students to succeed without learning the material. Ex- tests are online, hw only covers part of the reading. Bc of this, his class ended up on the back-burner. I wish he demanded more, bc I know I had more to give!

Professor Avramov is super awesome, the lectures are very engaging and this class is super relevant to current events. Discussions are lively and students are super welcomed to share their opinions. Would hundred percent recommend for everyone to take it - one of my favorite classes and professors here at UT!

Dr. Avramov is definitely one of the best professors at UT!! He is the most caring and passionate professor I've had. Cares more about the students actually learning than the grades. There were three exams and two discussions a month based on readings. However, he is pretty lenient and doesn't want to add stress to his students. Take his class

analysis.name: Avi Blitz
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Avi Blitz is an outstanding teacher. His lectures are incredibly engaging, and you can really tell he cares about his students. Homework is graded fairly, and quizzes are given every other week. As long as you show up to class, participate, and do homework, you will get an A. If you are genuinely interested in learning Hebrew, take this class!!

Dr. Blitz is one of the best professors I've ever had, hands down. He will go out of his way to help you, and he cares tremendously for his students. Loved the atmosphere of his class. I am shocked to see that others claim to have not liked his class: I have a feeling they weren't expecting Hebrew to be so difficult. Take him, you'll learn so much!

Avi is an absolute GEM of a professor. His classroom feels like home. He's so kind and welcoming, and he TAILORS THE CLASS MATERIAL TO THE CLASS based on our interests in subject material. He's also accessible out of class at Schulchan Ivrit or by email. He will improve your Hebrew drastically, and you'll have fun learning!

Avi is the best Hebrew teacher I've ever had. He knows everything there about the culture and language and presents in an engaging and meaningful way. As long as you come to class and participate, you will get a good grade. Take this class if it's open you won't regret it

TAKE AVI!!! I absolutely loved his class. He crafted slideshows just for us and according to the topics that WE wanted to learn about. He's so kind and funny and cares so much for his students' success.

analysis.name: Alex Macedo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: LITERALLY THE GOAT! Didn't show up to class for a whole month or two but still end up with an A. The exam is basically what is covered during exam review session, and final is not cumulative. 3 quizzes drops, 2-4 HW drops. THIS IS FOR M 427L.

This man is NOT accessible outside of class, doesn't answer emails, and isn't clear in his lectures. He rambles about easy concepts and speeds through the difficult stuff. His exams are only 3 q's. If you take this class DON'T FORGET THE QUEST HW he won't mention it in class or put it on Canvas. The material itself seems easy, he makes it hard.

DO NOT TAKE if no experience in calc. 2 exams, 3 questions each all purely based on bad lectures. notes and lectures not posted, does not respond to emails, must rely on your own notes to study. discussion and HW not what is related to exams. there are better calc teachers. avoid or get ready to get a C for getting 1 question on the exam wrong.

Horrible teaching style, boring lectures, and unclear grading. Grades everything last minute so you don't know your actual standing until the end of the semester. Class time with the TA every other day gets you nowhere-- it's all busy work with a group you're randomly assigned to and nobody pulls any weight.
Doesn't answer emails, disorganized, and does everything last minute.

analysis.name: Katie Bradford
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed this course! Dr. Bradford's lectures were engaging and made me excited to come to class. While there was more work than a typical communications course, I genuinely enjoyed the assignments. She made an effort to connect with students, which I appreciated, and the group projects were positive thanks to great teammates.

I love Bradford so much. She is such a pleasant professor who has a true passion for teaching. Her lectures were easily comprehensible and engaging. She fostered such a fantastic community within the course. Yes, there is a lot of reading, but the content was genuinely interesting and assignments were easy!

Learned so much from this conflict res course! There's lots of homework and multiple things due at similar times, which can be overwhelming, but it's all pretty doable stuff. Dr. B was a bright energetic spirit, and she genuinely cared about us. Loved the groups projects; be prepared to talk to lots of people!!

Dr. Bradford is by far one of my favorite professors. She wants you to succeed, teaches in a variety of ways, has engaging lectures, and takes feedback seriously. The class itself is fascinating and has practical applications in everyday life. Since taking this class, I have handled conflicts much better in both my personal and professional lives.

Dr. Katie Bradford is one of the most caring and loving professors I've had while at UT. She would always print out the assignments for us, so that we knew exactly what to do for the next class. She brought in donuts one day as a sign of appreciation for us. She really cares and is really like a mom for you in the class.

analysis.name: Andrei Straumanis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 380 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Grades tough and tends to lose his bike.

Two words: F.U STRAUMANIS! This class was insanely hard, no help from the professor and quizzes were 5 minutes in length while it took this wannabe marine biologist 20 to explain the whole thing. No reviews for exams and you sure bet the exams were hard! Lots of fun to fail every test!

eh. this year's material was ridiculously hard compared to last year's, so exams and quizzes were hard to prepare for bc we were NEVER given accurate practice material. I saw a diff prof's midterm and it was exactly like our DAILY quizzes so take that as you will. if you gave a victorian child our 2nd midterm, they would probably have an aneurysm

I used to be chill with him until he dropped an email telling us ways to get bonus points on our final, only to send another one 40 minutes later saying that it was actually an email from last year and didn't apply to us. That's honestly the tip of the iceberg though the 5 minutes quizzes every class really took it all from me.

worst professor i have ever experienced he dropped my gpa and made me question everything. o chem is already a difficult subject and he made it 1000 times worse BY NOT TEACHING he single-handedly ruined my college experience.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Richmond-Garza
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: RGs a good lecturer. But the assigned TA made this the worst course Ive ever taken. Showing an extreme inability to convey the grading criteria or to help connect our concerns to the professor, sordid behavior, just not enough characters to truly do them justice. Also an attendance policy thats oddly strict, wouldnt recommend for any non-majors

i never went to lecture, just do the instapolls for attendance, discussions were mandatory and boring but if you show up to all its automatic 100 for attendance. 100 word responses for every reading which were interesting for the most part. stay on top of the work bc it is really easy to forget about this class. 2 easy essays and easy asf project.

Dr. RG is a good professor but does not properly prepare you for her exams. She uses far too much time going around the stories plot and background than actually talking about it. Once she showed us a movie clip of 007 that had no relation to the story??? Heavily controlled by TAs so youll be lucky to get a good one. Never on the same page as TAs

The timing of the assignments wasn't great; once I had gotten feedback, it was too late to change anything and it had already brought my grade down. There's a lot of reading in this class, but it's worth doing to keep up with the lectures and discussion sections. Overall, if I had to take English again, I would probably try another professor.

Dr. RG's lectures are very interesting/engaging & she covers a lot of interesting topics! The one thing that I'd note is that we're required to read a lot for hw & you'll have to write two large papers (1 has 13 prompts and the other has 10) & you have to write 100 words per prompt (1000-1300 words total). The plus side is there's no midterm/final!

analysis.name: Mark Bradshaw
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Takes an interesting topic and makes you dislike it. Almost 80% of classes are guest speakers, which may sound great, until exam time, when you realize he has taught nothing. Very lecture-heavy with little class participation. Exams are all written and make you teach the textbook to yourself.

He does NOT care about you learning the material. You will have to study slideshows 40-70+ slides long per chapter but maybe talks about 2-10 of those in class. He fully skips chapters when guest speakers come. The material is interesting he just doesn't teach it or gives long winded explanations. Be ready to stress for tests.

good luck yall boys, if you're reading this and youre in his class, its too late for you. every test will absolutely push the limits of the human mind. every case is a arduous process. the roughest part, though, is having to sit through his class without sleeping. He doesnt respond to any questions or hands raised, and is a yapatronic. runaway.

He insists on testing us all the materials although some of them weren't covered in class. Offers no help prior the exam, no review session, no practice questions. His condensed slides for exams are almost 350 pages + extra readings. If you want to spend more time in class with the guest speakers, then don't put that much of a weight on the exams.

I have taken multiple courses with this professor and he manages to make the most interesting classes such as fraud analysis sound super boring. 15 minutes will feel like the longest hour of your class. Not only does he only stare at his feet and outside the window while teaching, but he offers no help or additional learning opportunies.

analysis.name: David Birdsong
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I literally love this guy. He is so kind and he is very accessible if you miss a quiz or a test. He is extremely knowledgeable and receives questions well. He also does review sessions and goes over your exam 1:1 with you which is reallllyyy useful. The class itself is straightforward and the exams are just like the review.

Joy of French truly was joyful. He cares about the content he is teaching, and it is fun to learn about French curse words, common sayings, and other aspects of the language that typical classes do not teach you. He is passionate and understanding, so this is the 3rd class I have taken with him because he's simply the best. I highly recommend him!
Took for Power of Words UGS. Such a fun class and insanely easy. Professor does tend to go on random tangents/talk about nothing. Very little work and it is hard not to get an A.
He is hilarious and you really get to know him! Classes are simple and lots of interactive discussions!

Birdsong is a very enthusiastic & fun teacher- gets you excited about what he's teaching. He was not originally supposed to teach 317C, so he did not create the material and tests. Prepared us well w/ handouts, practice quizzes, & told us where to find the study material. Pretty generous with grading. Attendance points are self grading after class

analysis.name: Zoltan Barany
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The lectures are interesting and the content of the class itself, including the readings, are pretty cool. Dr. Barany is funny. That being said, his TAs are a total nightmare. They grade extremely inconsistently. They make the exams easy except for four-five random questions that absolutely do not test your knowledge about the class. Rude too.

My favorite professor at UT by far. I have learned the most in his class and he genuinely cares. Don't let him scare you off. He is knowledgable and caring, and has the coolest experiences in his research. His humility is astounding. Class is not easy, but it is so rewarding and prepares you for grad school type work. Could not recommend more.

I took GOV365G Military in Politics with Barany. The class was fun and Prof Barany is genuinely passionate about the topic and discussing it with students. Pay attention in class, review lecture slides and do the readings! There are pop quizzes that are pass or fail so make sure you read. He's really one of UT's gems so take advantage!

The course material is super interesting, and Barany is such a fun lecturer. The class is pretty seminar-based, but it isn't intimidating at all. You are graded by very few things; however, I think he's a pretty fair grader. He's also super approachable and funny, so I never felt too afraid to ask for help. Take this class!!

Everything based off 3 tests, and test wording can lowkey be confusing. Had to study a ridiclous amount for the tests just to not even get a 100, I had nothing else to do tho. If your course is alr loaded take a diff one. He's really funny.

analysis.name: Brett McKinney
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor McKinney's class was incredibly straightforward, well taught, and was always a great person to talk to. Very knowledgeable and passionate lectures. No tests, a couple projects/assignments, mandatory attendance (as part of grade), plenty of extra credit opportunities. Overall, great class and great professor.

He is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. The class is very useful, and he is willing to answer any questions after class or over email. A few short assignments every week or so, you just have to show up to class once a week and participate.

Brett was a very caring guy and he's definitely the type to genuinely care about his students. I've learned a lot on this class and I would say I developed some professional skills as well. It can be a bit work heavy since you only meet once a week but overall very easy.

Brett really wants to help everyone in the class, and teaches the course in a way that your resume writing and communication skills really improve by the time you are done. I didn't like the course because there was so much work, and had to do extra credit events to keep my grade up, but nothing against Brett. Very well spoken and great guy.

He is very engaging even at 8 am classes. A lot of homework but all is useful for your career-building process! Gets you familiar with facilities around campus and career coaches. So much extra credit is offered by participating in McCombs events, which can replace your lack of attendance if needed. Easy A!

analysis.name: Sarah Collins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor was nice and seemed to want to help in the classroom, however she is incredibly disorganized and at several points pushed back due dates from the ones listed on the syllabus without announcing it. she took over 2 months to grade our 10 point multiple choice quiz and almost never replied to emails and if she did it took over 2/3 days.

Dr. Collins is a super accommodating, caring, and relatable prof. She drops a HW and quiz, no exams, and the quizzes are open-note. Most of the HW can be found online to check your work. Very low-stress class and I highly recommend her if you need to take 321. My only critique would be I wish she and the TA were more active on Piazza.

Professor Collins is nice, but it's the grading that really gets you, especially the quizzes. Lectures are super fast (messy notes, hardly any examples), and on your 13 quizzes (60% of your grade), there's only 5-8 questions. Get one wrong and you're cooked— once there were 25 points to a single question. Super picky about anything you write, too.

Dr Collins stats class is one many CS majors will take. Weekly homework is doable. Lecture slides help a lot with exams, and practice problems are similar. You get a cheat sheet for formulas/notes. The class is fully online except for exams, offering flexibility. Exams are generously graded with partial credit and usually include a bonus question.

Dr. Collins was incredibly sweet. She would pause for questions and created a folder for practice problems. She would also post the notes from each lecture with examples, however they might be difficult to understand if you did not attend class. She wanted to remember everyone's name + leave feeling confident in their understanding of statistics.

analysis.name: Charles Carson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Gave a huge curve on a test, giving many people well over a 100. One midterm and one final, not multiple choice but not difficult if you study. Hilarious lectures that can be off topic sometimes but interesting. Readings about once a week from the textbook with a reading guide. Doesn't take attendance but most of the test info is learned in class.

Carson is a great *lecturer* -- his lectures are interesting and his personality is great. The course itself, however, is pretty bad - if you're looking for sudden homework assignments assigned the NIGHT before the due date, late grades, and overly difficult quizzes, take this class (difficulty still is OK). Way too much effort for a VAPA class.

Don't take this professor. He causes unnecessary stress and is snarky and rude. The quizzes are super hard, and there are long readings and reading guides due before every single lecture. He is funny at times and if you really enjoy hip hop go for it, but I came expecting a fun, interesting vapa and left with a bad grade and a bunch of stress.

BY FAR, the best professor at UT. He is literally so chill. Go to cyphers, trust me. I was able to build a really personal, mentor-mentee type thing with him by doing that and dude, he gave advice on everything from finance to relationship stuff. Absolutely chill, talks a lot, but it's honestly a good thing. Just don't slack.

Most enjoyable summer class I've taken. Lectures were very engaging and fun while not being too long either. Graded by instapolls (don't have to get them right), weekly discussions that are completion, and weekly open note quizzes. An easy A for the VAPA credit and a great professor. Definitely take this class if you need the credit.

analysis.name: Cesar Martinez Espinosa
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: A very nice and kind professor - but the class is SO boring and monotonous and he isn't really great at getting the content across to students especially when it comes to teaching how to use R for our statistical methods. you have to pretty much self-teach everything and hope for the best despite the fact the tests aren't super easy or super hard.

The class was easy as the homeworks, midterm, and final (written by chatGPT) were very easy. He was brought in as a last min replacement and I think he tried his best, but he is a very unengaging lecturer imo. His grading is also very ambiguous and he screwed a lot of ppl on the project. Overall easy class and you can do well with minimal effort

The professor was a last-minute addition and new to this specific course. While the homework and exams were manageable, the reading workload was extremely heavy. I think most of the class just didn't read them and it was fine. The group project felt a bit rushed due to the timing, but the professor was understanding and fair with the grading.

His lectures are extremely boring, making an already dry subject even more unbearable. His project grading was quite arbitrary, and he honestly struggles to communicate to his students. BHP will probably  replace him, so hopefully future students have a better experience with the class.

This class is not engaging and is organized poorly. Lectures are mostly discussion and vague which isn't very effective for learning and retaining information. I have to teach myself everything. When I asked for help, he laughed in my face.

analysis.name: Cynthia Cabrera
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cabrera is obviously very passionate about teaching. But she consistently gets practice problems wrong and explains concepts in overly complex ways. If you can do well with this teacher that means you already took calculus or you completely learned the course on your own time. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Just horrible at teaching, nice person and passionate at math, but she makes so many little mistakes while teaching it makes someone who already took calculus worse at calculus. Would not recommend. If you get this teacher I would recommend self teaching and tutors. Good luck.

She is a lovely person who cares about her work, however, she is not a good professor. She overcomplicates simple concepts and underexplains the more difficult ones. Exams are weighted heavily making the other assignments seem unimportant even when they take a lot of time. I would recommend avoiding her and taking calculus with another professor.

Getting in contact with her is very hard. She overcomplicates subjects, and her lectures are very hard to understand. Many of the assignments you do seem unrelated to what you are learning. In addition, on the tests, there is a lot of material that you will feel like you never learned. Take calculus with someone else.

She's incredibly sweet and you can tell she loves her job. However, she's not a good teacher. About 1/5 or of her students actually go to lectures because they're unhelpful, she's a confusing lecturer. Time is spent super inefficiently. If you reach out to her personally, she'll try her best but you'll have better luck self-teaching in this class.

analysis.name: Chad Landis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Chad Landis? More like DAD Landis. This guy was awesome. The material was presented in an interesting and engaging manner, making it a pleasure to show up to class everyday. Tests are fair and pertain to what you learn in class. Homework is optional, but helps you with quizzes and further understanding. I HIGHLY recommend my dad.

I struggled a lot in Statics, but Landis' grading scale really helped. A C was around a 65, so even low exam scores counted. The class isn't easy, but many still got A's and B's. He provides lots of past exams and quizzes. He seemed grumpy a lot times due to cheating scandals in our class and sending attendance codes.., but overall he's fair.

He is really good at teaching and provides plenty of resources to study with. I had him for statics and solids and liked him for both. The tests can be difficult, so prepare in advance. He takes "cheating" on attendance very seriously. There are weekly quizzes with two drops and 4 exams with scaled weighting.

Take Landis! His class is very well organized & he provides all the material you need to succeed. dont take early semester warnings lightly-- falsely filling the attendance form is -5 pts off overall grade. exams are fair, study at least 4 most recent past exams and you'll be set. but expect to put a little more effort in for exam 3. quizzes are ez

THE GOATTT. As someone who barely passed eng physics 1, I learned so much from this class and did surprisingly well despite being worried. Loved this class so much I signed up for his solids class next semester, and super excited. The material is difficult sometimes, but he provides an ABUNDANCE of HWs, past quizzes, and past exams.

analysis.name: Carlos Torres-Verdin
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor really cares about teaching. He has a binder full of practical examples that he uses to teach. He writes summaries for each lecture. Exams are aligned with homework. Great TAs. Excellent solution sets. Field trip included.

Great instructor and very well organized. He teaches practical knowledge and designs the homework and exams to be complementary. Nice person. Very helpful. Optional field trip and visit to core facilities. Cares about students.

Hes a great professor that really wants the entire class to engage and learn. Exams are hard, but if you understand the material you will be fine! Go to office hours, he is even better explaining one-on-one. He is accesible after class, super funny in lectures and tries his best to be as resourceful as possible to optimize students learning!
Wow, one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. You learn so much from this professor, but he is an all around great person. This class kicked my ass, but is extremely relevant to our major.

Overall great instructor and very well organized course with lots and lots of practical examples. Very good solution sets. Subject matter is hard but it is what we expect in a professional setting. The instructor organizes a field trip. Highly recommended

analysis.name: Terry Chapman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: this professor is one of the nicest professor I have ever had. he cracks some jokes every once in a while, he grades quickly and on time. great hair and jawline
Such a lovely course. I loved his Politics and Science Fiction class, the readings were phenomenal and he really cared. Take this UGS! It's so much better than any other.

The subject of the class was fascinating to me, but I thought the book was not always clear and the quizzes and exams had ambiguous questions. I also think the professor could gain from improving his lectures by paying attention to the flow of his speech for a more natural and smooth delivery: get meditation/massage to create relaxed recordings.

Professor Chapman is a very standard professor. His class on global governance consisted of reading a module, watching a lecture, taking a quiz. Then three exams were based on the modules, lectures, and quizzes. This is going to sound obvious, but it is especially true in this class. Do the modules and the readings and you will do well.

Prof. Chapman made this upper division government class worthwhile. He was very interested in the subject matter and related it well to his students. Although attendance isn't necessary, he will learn everyone's names. He is always available for office hours. This course has a lot of readings from the textbook and outside articles.

analysis.name: Laura de Castro Quaglia
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lecture heavy and get ready, they are monotonous. She's so intellectually dry that I had trouble not falling asleep during her courses.

As long as you keep up with the work, it's an easy A. If you miss a few tho, it's hard ot get back up on your feet. There was like 2-3 assignments a week and then tests every 4 weeks. Overall great experience for a summer class.
Took this course online over the summer and was extremely easy. Not much homework and very few quizzes which is all your grade is accumulated with.
Easiest government credit. You watch lecture videos from O'Brien. Exams are so straightforward. Never used the textbook.
The average of every assignment was failing or close and her feedback was terrible

analysis.name: Emily Caudill
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 210 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Don't take under any circumstances. She knows the material, but does not know how to teach. She jumps from slide to slide and has in class quizzes every week. These quizzes go over the same material learned from that same day. She uses other professors materials to "try" and "teach." SHE DOES NOT DROP EXAMS ANYMORE. Expect to do 6+ hours every week

Professor Caudill is the most unlikeable chemistry professor. Her voice tells you she doesn't want to be there. I found the lectures to be disengaging and hard to follow. The exam proctoring and academic integrity process was handled unfairly in my case, but the dean cleared me. She does NOT want the best for you. Do NOT take her.

slides were so unorganized, if you were to download it from canvas it will not match with what shes showing during lecture. its hard to pay attention to her, so many hw/quizzes due before class, doesnt drop exams or retest, had to drop the class because it was mentally draining trying to teach myself the material. take her or not, just be mindful

Some how my previous rating on here disappeared. Somewhat sketchy, but I will not allow my voice to be silenced, and I will exercise my first amendment right. She is monotone and boring. The only saving grace of this class is the review notes and organization of the class, but all other chem professors use it too, so it is somewhat irrelevant.

This teacher does not teach. In addition to not teaching, she somehow manages to blame the students for her lack of ability to teach. She gets distracted so easily in lecture and ends up wasting a good portion of lecture time asking students to be quiet even if they were whispering. She once yelled at her TA for helping a student.

analysis.name: Douglas Dempster
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was amazing! Coming in, I thought I knew what creativity was, but this class allowed me to reflect on and challenge my views. Prof Dempster taught us through a lot of fun activities, from scavenger hunts to movement labs. There are 10-minute talks that require you to give a presentation during your lab section, but they're not too hard.

1st class he said that TTH lecture was optional, and Fri discussion wasn't. Then 1/3 through the semester he did class grades and quizzes TTH. It was so much work for UGS. Locked our grade so you couldn't see how you were doing, and didnt allow devices, claiming he would "get us out of class early for trade off" and we never got out early since.

The class was decent enough, though I feel the grading criteria is somewhat unclear. Once, I received a B on one of my assignments for “appearing to be stressed”. Additionally, Professor Dempster rarely got back to me when I asked for feedback. The course is simple enough, however, if you're in need of a UGS, I wouldn't take it with him.

His lectures are engaging, and he incorporates many interesting activities. However, he couldn't understand my paper, and the A threshold is 95, not 93. Ultimately, due to my final paper, I received an A- with a final grade of 94.7.

such a good professor. cancelled friday lectures for the last two months of class. easy readings and fun labs. great professor literally nothing bad to say. the creative notebooks are fun and easy to do and count as a big portion of the grade- he also encourages students to work on them during class. super interesting and engaging. HIGHLY RECOMMEND

analysis.name: Dan Puperi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
He's an alright professor. Makes odd comments about current society standards at times. The course itself is built willy-nilly. Don't believe the "love him!" if you can think critically. Do work hard and be on his good side, he teaches 3+ required BME courses. Also grades preferentially, so make a good impression.

TLDR: ok class, ok professor.

Relatively easy A if you don't procrastinate on larger assignments, all lectures are recorded but there will be in class assignments that are not noted beforehand so you prob need to show up to class. the small individual grades accumulate to effect your grade in the end even if it doesn't seem like it matters at the time.

Much more interesting than 303L, but it's also much more work and can be overwhelming at times. Your grade is going to depend on your group, so prioritize forming relationships with them. 

Dr. Dan is fair and provides very clear expectations and instructions. If you show up and don't procrastinate, this class is very manageable.

Very unwelcoming environment makes it intolerable. Easy class subject matter with SO many busy work assignments. Lecture is required but not relevant to the assignments. Did not learn anything. Disappointed at best.

Not understanding, not accommodating, his labs are unnecessary difficult and time consuming due to his own poorly written instructions, and he is extremely condescending and will publicly shame your work to later classes. He doesn't contribute to UT at all so I don't understand the power trip he has.

analysis.name: Lydia CdeBaca-Cruz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 111 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I've never left bad reviews on RMP, but this was the most demotivating class I've taken at UT. I spent several hours working on reading journals and annotating readings. But my journals were sent back anyways. Feedback mostly nitpicked my answers' organization into their "CRIT" style rather than correcting content of responses themselves. :(

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IN THE SUMMER! It was very frustrating, especially for students who also have other commitments, like other classes or jobs, which the professor called out in a very passive-aggressive tone. The grading was very slow and it took longer than the advertised 1-2 days, and many times, the assignments would have to be redone.

The structure of this course, as a summer class, is rigorous to the point where it's stress-inducing. Very lengthy journals. Grading takes a very long time (>2 days). You can try to stay ahead & turn assignments in early, but the stressful part is if you pass to "unlock" the next module, and if you don't, expect another 2 days after you resubmit.

Do not take this professor under any circumstance. She does not clearly communicate the timing and goals required for the class and when asked to make reasonable adjustments to rectify issues, she immediately hid behind "you signed an agreement." A lot of people in the class are getting way worse grades they otherwise would because of her.

I took this class over the summer, which was a lot more complicated than it should've been. The TAs take a long time to grade journals, leading to you falling behind, especially if you need them to regrade them. Readings and lectures are very lengthy, so if you are taking this class with any other classes or jobs, expect to have a heavy workload.

analysis.name: John Deigh
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Unbelievably impolite and disrespectful. Two essays constitute the entire grade and you won't receive your grade back in the first essay until after the deadline to drop a class. You'll have no idea of your standing. He simply wants your essay to regurgitate his exact opinion stated in class. Otherwise, he'll refuse to even grade it.

Took him for Plan II philosophy. The entire class was graded on 3 tests (25% for each midterm and 50% for the final) and it was really hard to follow along with his lectures. Does not give makeup tests for any reason no matter how far in advance you contact him. If you're taking Plan II philosophy, take literally anyone else.

Lectures for an hour and a half with no slides or handouts. Very boring, which makes it incredibly hard to pay attention. Even if you write your papers using verbatim notes, he'll say you misunderstood the prompt. Submitted grades extremely late to the point where I was forced to use my OTE drop to save my GPA.

I took Deigh for Plan II Philosophy, and it was boring. I definitely think it's possible to get an A in his class if you work hard, but he's not a very engaging lecturer. However, he does explain well!

Kinda boring lectures, it is the end of the semester and I still don't even really know who he is despite showing up everyday. But Deigh is very helpful during office hours, also a fair grader who will explain if you lose points or need help. I finally figured out what I was supposed to learn from Dr. Deigh, don't be a  snob and you will too.

analysis.name: Donald Winget
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is the easiest class you will take at UT. No exams or projects. 45% of your grade is from quizzes at the end of every class. One Instapoll at the end of each class (completion grades). There are 7 hw assignments, but they are multiple-choice Canvas assignments, around 20 q each. TAs are very sweet. Lots of EC (you won't need it).

Don was an awesome professor who actually cared about his students. His class is structured differently than most classes I've had at UT as he does 8 exams, 1 every 2 weeks, but he drops your two lowest scores and will drop your next two lowest scores and replace them with an optional project grade if you want.

Don is a fantastic professor. His lectures were consistently interesting and entertaining. You can tell he loves being an astrophysicist and a lecturer. His homework is very easy, and the exams are very similar to the practice tests he gives. If you have to take a science class, take his.

Awesome guy. His class was super easy so I never really talked to him, but even though the topic was outside of my major he did get my attention a lot. Super passionate and you can tell he really cares. Loves engagement during class and always super willing to answer questions. Instapolls for attendance and quizzes + homework, no exams.

Professor Winget was amazing! His class was easy and offered a low-stress environment to learn about astronomy. It honestly helped me learn better, as I wasn't having to worry about cramming information. No tests, just weekly assignments and quizzes. His lectures are fun and will have you engaged. One of my favorite classes!

analysis.name: David Leal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Your grade relies on only three tests (and a paper that is only 5% of your grade and is easy to get a 100) and you better get ready to know every single detail about us gov because some of the questions get pretty involved. The final is cumulative and made me a broken woman. But he is knowledgeable and nice! Why does he love squirrels so much?

US Congress. His exams are so packed full of stuff that you have to race through the exam to get everything done on time, leaving you to turn in a steaming pile of garbage. exams consisted of 15 term identifications, an essay, and 10 multiple choice questions. Boring material, boring guy, wouldn't touch this class again.

He was alright... I guess. Really boring lecturer he kind of just reads of slides. The essays are super easy basically just completion grades. His exams are kinda hard, you are expected to remember a lot of things that are very inconsequential, which is fine, they are just hard to remember because his lectures are so boring.

The majority of the grade is made up of two pretty easy exams --- you just have to make sure to read all the slides super carefully and take detailed notes from them. I attended probably less than 50% of the lectures, but I still did fine when I dedicatedly studied for the 5 days before the two exams. Attend his pre-exam review sessions!

Professor Leal is very accommodating and kind, but his lectures can get lengthy or tangential. Not super heavy reading load, but keep up with notes as exams can get detailed; make sure you understand concepts and key events/figures. 10 short response essays (33%), 2 Exams (66%). Attendance optional.

analysis.name: Dana Moshkovitz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: very simple, straightforward format. 1 problem set a week, 3 tests total with cheat sheets. Challenging class but basically impossible to fail given the grading scheme, allowing you to focus on the content rather than the grade. Would def take her again over other profs

She's an AMAZING professor who's extremely talented and caring. She teaches the material clearly and is very fair with grading. I was so nervous for this class initially, but I thoroughly enjoyed her class!

Moshkovitz is a great lecturer with a lot of experience in the field. She was accessible and always willing to answer questions. Weekly homeworks are usually not too difficult (1-2 questions each). Exams are not too difficult but have a strict time limit. All problems are graded on an A-B-C-F scale. TA discussion section is helpful.

Great professor. Algorithms is an inherently difficult course by idea, but her lectures make it much more fun and approachable (great lecturer tbh, except writes 1 like i). I think she delivered the content very well. Psets helps with content understanding. Exam is difficult (by nature) but very fair. (provides textbook but lecture is sufficient)

Very solid algorithms class. Lectures require careful attention to follow fully. Homework and exams are very fair. They can be tough (given the course). Shafik was an excellent TA. Moshkovitz explains things well, but be sure to phrase your question clearly so she understands how to best answer.

analysis.name: David Quintanilla
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 129 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Quintanilla is an amazing prof!!! He has super clear lectures and is such a cool and laid back guy. He really cares about his students and wants you to succeed. I would take him again if I could!

Prof Quintanilla is the best lecturer I've ever had. He makes every complex law topic easy to understand. TAKE HIM IN PERSON!!!! and always go to class, it's not mandatory, but participation is part of your grade and really all you need to do well in this class is take good notes during lectures. One of the few classes I actually loved going to!

Prof Q. is very passionate about teaching, and that passion shows in his lectures. He made the online class engaging and explained complex topics in a practical manner. He rewards your participation - by answering questions and attending lectures, the assignments and exams are very doable. Enjoyed the class a lot; he taught very useful concepts!

TAKE THIS PROF! GO TO CLASS! Prof Q is so amazing. This class changed my life no joke. You MUST go to lecture to do well on tests (which can be somewhat tricky but not horrible). Homeworks & group proj are easy. Review sessions are incredibly beneficial. Prof Q is incredibly engaging, passionate, & caring. I looked forward to class every day.

Professor Q is the best. Attendance is not technically mandatory but participation is a chunk of your grade, so make sure you stay on top of that. Honestly, I would just go as much as you can. He is a great lecturer and the tests are easier if you're in class. I highly recommend this class and any you can take with him

analysis.name: Michael Endl
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 85 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Super easy and interesting course. Information on tests is easy to learn but very specific so attendance and good listening and note taking are important (we're in college this isn't hard). As long as you take notes this is a free A.

Dr. Endl is really funny, and his lectures can be really interesting. I didn't pay all that much attention in class, which is my own fault, but half of your grade comes from just showing up. The tests aren't that difficult, but if you don't come/don't pay attention, you may get stuck. Overall, this was a great course to take for science credit.

Take this class. Light work, easy A. Prof cares about what he teaches. 4 pretty easy midterms, no final, instapolls for attendance (always at the same time+70% attendance gets you full credit), light hw to prep for the exam. some extra credit, and two xtra cred questions every exam. if u need a science req class this ones pretty cool.

Dr. Endl is very passionate about what he teaches, and it shows. There are 4 major tests in the class, and they are HARD — be prepared to know every single topic he covers in lecture. He does instapolls during class for attendance, and if you miss one or get it wrong, your grade will drop significantly, unfortunately.

Good professor. Class has 4 Tests and 4HWs and that is it for your grade. Tests were usually chill; you can find flashcards online. There is extra credit if needed. I found the class pretty intresting. Definitely made me think of the universe in ways I had never before, and it's really cool if you are interested in space and possibilities of life.

analysis.name: Peter English
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 232 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Disrespectful and dismissive. Will take off points arbitrarily without chance of refutation and is more concerned with weeding out lazy students than rewarding good ones. Tried to ask him a question when entire group was confused, he assumed I had not even attempted to engage with peers, and refused to even listen to circumstances.

From my experience, the material for this class was not difficult to learn, but his wording on exams can be very tricky to interpret. It feels like I am not just about learning Bio in this class, but rather trying to play word games with this professor at times.

This class is honestly a take at your own risk class. It's very clear what he wants you to know as it's 100% lecture based, despite him saying you need to read. The first half of each lecture is the EXACT same as the second half of the lecture before, so it does help you review stuff. Tests are manageable, the grading criteria will get you. Hard A.

By far the worst educational experience of my life. I made an account just to post a review because Dr. English has such a disdain for the students in his class. Unorganized, rude, and we have to argue back on grading criteria on a weekly basis. TAs are clueless, and the professor faults the students for everything. At this point it feels personal.
It costs nothing to be genuinely helpful, but Pete makes it a goal to make every student miserable. No wonder his lab is underfunded—even basic kindness must be too expensive

analysis.name: Eric Staron
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 291 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Eric Staron is a legend. He is a great lecturer and amazing at math. The homework through Quest is pretty normal stuff. The exams were not very difficult, you just have to know the subject and have good algebra skills. Warning, his Final was a  very hard, make sure that you study well and expect him to put some challenging questions .

extremely passive aggressive, twice he posted the wrong hw and corrected it AFTER everyone did the wrong version already. have to email him at 11pm the night before an exam for the "practice exam" key (10 times easier than the actual exam) because he ALWAYS forgets (1 time the key was half wrong hello??) the tests are harder than other professors

Staron's great at teaching, but he posts his notes online. Quest is due every Monday, and there are usually 20+ problems. Cut off for an A is a 93, and tests are multiple choice with 2-3 short answers. The final was pretty hard and it's worth 30%. Built-in curves in midterms and final. The max on each test was usually around 106. Class isn't easy!

Don't get me wrong, this class is hard, but Staron is easily the best math professor at UT. He gives you exactly what you need to do well. The problems on the exams are the exact same steps as problems from lecture or homework, there are no curveballs. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you better go if you want to know the example test problems.

Won't respond to emails. Practice/quiz problems offered by Dr. Staron do NOT reflect what is on the exam material and are instead based on material vaguely reviewed in lectures, in addition to an infuriating 1-2 trick questions on each exam. Was recommended by former classmates and friends and am HEAVILY disappointed. Avoid if you can.

analysis.name: Pamela Elias
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is a very nice person, but I found it frustrating that she talked like we were children and over simplified math terms so much. Not the best preparation for intense calculus courses, but if this is the only math you have to take then you're good. Not much homework and you get cheat sheets on the exams

If you ever have the chance to take Pam as your professor, please do!!!! I just completed my first semester at the UT Austin, and she was without a doubt my favorite professor of the entire semester. Pam is so energetic, and she teaches the material in a way that helps you understand no matter what your math background is. She is the absolute best!

My GOAT. She gives you test reviews for the midterms and the final that match the test exactly and you get a one page cheat sheet (front and back). Attendance isn't required but the daily homeworks match what she does in class so it's best if you go. TAs are very helpful and reachable. Easiest class ever if you listen in lecture and put the work in

I loved Pam, she is sweet,kind,& smart. She truly loves teaching, and you can tell. Attendance is not required (but you should definitely go because it helps a lot!). She builds in no-class days before and after holidays. Her office hours (along with the TA) are helpful. No matter how much math you have going in,she'll make sure you understand.

I had Pam for pre-cal in my first semester, and she was one of the best teachers I have had. She is so funny and creates an inclusive learning environment that encourages questions. She always has opportunities outside of class to meet with her if you need extra help. What is on the exams is clearly communicated by word or the Canvas reviews.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Klingbeil
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Really easy lab. Work was pretty much all group, but easy to do. The TA is super nice and Dr. K is very understanding if you have any issues. The lectures can be boring but overall not too bad.

Absolutely loved her! She genuinely wants everyone to succeed and makes it a goal to not work outside of class since it is only a 1 hour credit course. This is a very easy A as long as you go to all the labs and understand the purpose of each lab. There are midterm and final lab practicals but they are fairly easy with an extra credit question.

New lab thoughtfully designed, not just busywork. Feels like you're contributing to real scientific research. Not too much work 1 credit. Wet lab meets 3 hours per week, but often get out at least an hour early. Midterm is tough with no multiple choice. You need to really know and explain concepts. Final is not harder than the midterm.

she's WONDERFUL. this whole class is just writing one mini-systematic review on a nutrition topic of your choice. she guides you, assignment by assignment, and then you're all done about a month before finals. 10/10 i learned so much and wasn't even that stressed out about it. she's great, take her!

final + midterm are doable, but she makes them seem so much easier than they were. other than that, there's one in-person lecture per week plus the lab, which is TA-based. you learn a lot for sure, and they make sure you're never doing too much work outside of class. overall worth it for sure!

analysis.name: Morgan Fong
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Well-structured class, reasonable workload, and fair exams. However, Dr Fong is the most exasperating professor I have ever had. Her grading is picky to a fault and she is not understanding at all. Truly feels like she goes out of her way to make her class as annoying as possible. $100 mandatory textbook btw.

cheating reports aside, she's not a good professor. i self taught for EVERYTHING in this course - her lectures are around 20 minutes long and then you have to answer questions that are 10x harder than the practice for attendance. coding assignments have nothing to do with the class lectures. you're better off with ANYONE else, not worth the risk.

I've never felt so hateful in my 20 years as I have since Fong. Her lectures are useless, the workload is absurdly difficult for the single resource she requires.
