A cutoff is 90, which is huge. Didn't read a single text all semester, and got an A. Going to lecture isn't required, but gets a decent amount of extra credit on exams. I was dreading humanities, but I feel like I got out of this awful requirement with Dr. Garcia's class. If you hate reading but need a Lit credit, I promise this is the best one.

I don't understand why she's been getting so many negative reviews as of late when she was at a near 5 star score when I registered for her class for the spring semester. Her lectures can be a bit boring and long, but overall, the class was really simple and easy, with the tests being pretty easy if you attend lecture. Plus, 90 and above is an A.

Garcia's lectures are quite interesting and in depth and hit the main points that are on the frequent quizzes. Exams (4) consist of objective, short answer, and an essay question. There were 2 standalone extra credit opportunities and another on a close reading installment (4 CRITs total, 16%). We also went to the HRC for to see original books.

Im guessing (could be wrong) that she has tenure because she literally does not care about anything. So many arbitrary rules. She doesn't respond to emails on weekends (fine), needs two business days to respond (okay), then doesn't respond. But she said she "saw it though". She also changes her office hours all the time so you can really attend it.

analysis.name: H.W. Perry Jr.
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Everyone should take this class. No tech, no AI. You have to use your brain, you must think critically, and you cannot choose to not read, as the class operates in a Socratic format, so you will get cold called. The class is hard, but if you work hard it should be manageable. Prioritize your readings; it is really not an option to get behind.

I was in one of his early (first?) classes at WashU. I took his ConLaw class and loved it. We loved the content and his teaching style.  Discussions were lively and as noted if you say anything silly he will use the Socratic method to make you realize your mistake, why you made it, and how to think to avoid a similar mistake down the line.

Professor Perry's course was a transformative journey through constitutional law, akin to time travel to a bygone era of profound intelligence. His lectures challenged beliefs, offering life-saving legal insights. Despite the intense workload, his passion for law made learning immensely rewarding, marking him as a favorite among students. Take him.

Perry's a great professor if you buy into his teaching style. Know the facts of the case before you come to class, decide whether you agree with how cases were decided and come up with justifications for your opinion. If you don't like talking in class, don't register. He has some frustrating habits and there's a lot of reading, but it's worth it.

I cannot fit enough characters into this review to describe how wonderful Perry is. With that said, do not take this course if you aren't willing to put in the work. It is difficult because the content is very vast, but it's interesting and made me realize that I love con law. Keep up with the reading and go to office hours if you are confused.

analysis.name: Yahaya Halidu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I had this TA for US History and overall the experience was pretty solid. He clearly understood the material well and did a good job breaking down complex concepts into something more manageable during discussions and office hours. I especially appreciated how patient he was when answering questions- never made anyone feel rushed for asking

This SI Leader is absolutely exceptional. He explains concepts clearly, breaks down difficult material in a way that actually makes sense, and always makes sure everyone is comfortable asking questions. You can tell he genuinely cares about student success and puts real effort into every session. His teaching style is engaging, organized, and 100%.

Such an organized, and supportive TA who creates a positive learning environment that makes challenging material feel manageable. Truly an outstanding SI Leader and a huge reason I did well in this class during our just ended quiz. I have huge respect for this man. Thank you Mr. Halidu. I recommend going to his sessions if you want to do well.

Grading was fair and mostly consistent, though sometimes I wanted MORE verbal feedback during office than I got from the scripts and could've been a bit more detailed to help improve on future assignments. Yahaya was also approachable outside of class, which made it easier to get help when needed.

The class is definitely challenging, but the Instructor is great and leads really meaningful discussions. He  proofread all my essay drafts before submissions, held office hours, offered comments and suggested areas of improvements. I got an A+ in the end. I was in his Intro to Africa class too. Worth taking again if he has another class next year.

analysis.name: Neal Hall
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Dr. Hall is the professor you want to have for a course like this. His lectures are worth their weight in gold, they take the dense book chapters and dumb them down. 
Exam grading emphasizes precision. Go to OH to do the homework. Get good with complex numbers, transform tables, and conceptual understanding of applications (sampling, filters).

Great lectures. All notes are posted to canvas. HW is essentially a completion grade. Weekly quizzes in class aren't hard and lowest 2 dropped. Asinine exam grading policy. Questions were not difficult but very harshly graded with minimal partial credit. One exam had no calculators allowed. Final grade cutoffs are very generous (40 = C-)

One of the better EE professors in the department. Very clear and covers all the information without going too much into proofs. First class I've taken in a while where going to class REALLY does help, because he does cover all the material that will show up on homework/tests. Would definitely recommend him for future classes.

Homeworks were completion grades, but grading on test was extremely harsh, taking off many points even for just simple arithmetic errors. The cutoffs for letter grades were adjusted to account for this, but it's not super clear what cutoffs were used in the end. Lectures and notes are also not that clear, would recommend just reading the textbook.
I don't usually write reviews, but Hall really knows how to abstract really complex ideas to be digestible. This class is very effort = reward, no tricks. Plus Hall is just fun to listen to.

analysis.name: Hannah Walker
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr Walker feels more like a researcher who is teaching as a side gig, but he class was great. I love research so it was definitely the class for me. She doesn't grade very hard, and the workload was very manageable. She is extremely knowledgeable in her field so she is a great resource if you want to get into political science research.

I really enjoy her teaching style as it is a balance between lecture and discussion. The readings are required but you can usually skim them to get full points. She is very passionate and makes the content engaging.

Nice lady, but the amount of reading assigned is crazy. A 20-40 page paper every other day— and you really need to read them to participate. Participation is 20% of the grade, class is entirely discussion based. She focuses way too much on statistical methods used in research for an intro level mandatory class. Tests are open book but not easy.

Dr. Walker's class was relatively easy; however, she reads off of her notes and does not pause for students to take notes, so you have to type really fast to get good notes. You have to get good notes though because the three exams are entirely based on the lectures and readings. Your grade rests on the three opennote exams and two group projects.

Dr. Walker does speak fast; however, I found her lectures and her field of research very interesting, and the class was very. engaging with many group discussions. Your grade does rely only rely on two group projects and three tests, but she doesn't grade too harshly on the projects, and the tests questions come directly from the lecture slides.

analysis.name: Ryan Hannigan
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Proffessor Hannigan is a blessing to any engineering student. He makes material very accessible and does not even make you need a textbook since he suggests just the free open stacks one and then covers the materials as they will be used in his class. The exams are incredibly fair.

Ryan is honestly the best professor I have had at UT. Physics is very challenging and overwhelming, I spoke to him about my concerns before starting the class and he was super nice and helped me out so much. Going to his class was always so fun! He wants his students to succeed! He offers retakes for exams, and homework is on quest.

He was an amazing professor and really wanted his students to learn the material. Physics at its core is a little challenging if that's not your forte, but he has so many opportunities to get extra help. So many opportunities to get extra credit and he wants everyone to get an A. If you go to class and do your homework you will do good.

Ryan was one of my favorite professors I've had at UT! He is so understanding and is a very engaging lecturer. I thoroughly enjoyed this class even though I thought I wouldn't like physics. He made me love the subject and ensures you have all the tools and resources to succeed. Highly recommend taking him if you have the chance!!

Easily one of the best professors I've had at UT. He genuinely cares about each student and wants everyone to succeed. His lectures are engaging, and he's actually able to make physics enjoyable (shocking, I know). Attendance does make a difference in his class, but he provides exam retakes for full credit and exam reviews before each test.

analysis.name: David Harwath
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Really chill professor, he made all the lecture slides available online, assignments were manageable, and exams where very fair.

Personally, didn't like some lectures (signal processing, spectrograms) and found the slides very dense and a bit uninteresting. Exams are computational, similar to the practice, and graded leniently. Occasionally a q focuses on a small detail, so make sure to memorize the slides. He gave a lot of EC: 2% from ECIS and 1% for everyone at the end.

Dr. Harwath is an incredible lecturer, he is engaging and always stops to ask people if they have questions. He is also very accessible after and outside of class. His exams are also very fair as long as you study and engage with the slides during class. The projects themselves are quite challenging at times but he also guides you through it!

One of the best professors I had. Amazing classes, learnt so much. Makes you feel very safe to ask questions and learn. Makes you want to study hard. Classes are very interesting and technical. Such a sweet professor.

Dr. Harwath is one of the best CS professors. He is passionate about what he is teaching. The class material itself can be a little bit hard, but he tries his best to help students out. He always stops and asks if everyone is clear with what he is teaching, if anyone has questions he would stop and explains again. A great professor! Take him!

analysis.name: Zoya Heidari
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Her course is not really hers but the guy who wrote the book. Just buy the book and you won't have to attend. She is a textbook communicator lol

Professor Heidari is the GOAT of PGE professors at UT Austin. She is great at lecturing and handling examples you will see on homework and tests. I am not a morning person yet I was able to remember what she taught more than the other professor who taught this class. She is easily a 10/10 professor and I can't praise her enough.
She was teaching Advanced Petrophysics for the first time. She is well equipped with the topic and always helpful inside and outside of the class. During the classes, she was very student-friendly.

analysis.name: Mary Ibarrola
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I can't remember where I read this, I had written it down a while ago, but it really reminds me of Dr. Ibarrola: "Every subject, however dull they had seemed in the hands of others, became animated in hers." Would take her class again, it seems like most do.

I love Liz. I took Ethics with her first and then MF (current). She is what I would say the ideal lecturer. Her slides aren't overwhelming with text (though some are just pictures so attending lectures is important). I will say there are ALOT of readings (all interesting) but they can be overwhelming. She is also understanding when communicated w/

Professor Ibarrola is AMAZING!!! I had her for ANT304, and I HIGHLY recommend you take her. She loves what she teaches and made me truly interested in Archaeology, having no prior knowledge or interest. There is no homework, just a weekly lab that is easy. The exams are easy as long as you study. Easy A and truly amazing professor.

Dr Ibarrola is so sweet, supper engaging, and very passionate. Her class is interesting and not difficult if you pay attention. I liked her lectures a lot so I never skipped class, but if you use her study guide and memorize the slides then you can get a good grade on the tests! Would recommend for intro to Arch.

Prof. Ibarrola is caring and attentive to her students. Her lectures are interesting, and she kept the class entertaining and active. She was understanding and easy to communicate with. There's a bit of assigned reading, but it was fine. Be sure to participate and attend lectures, as a big chunk of your grade is dependent on participation.

analysis.name: Brent Iverson
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 153 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've had at UT! He records his lectures, but I highly recommend going to class because the vibes he gives off are great and he's an amazing lecturer. He has old exams posted which help a lot when it comes to studying for exams. His tests are a challenge, but definitely doable. He is the best ochem professor.

MUST TAKE HIS CLASS! You'll not only acquire more than enough knowledge to tackle subsequent UT courses (& MCAT) but he also imbues his class w/ wholesome lessons in life. In brief, Dr. Iverson is a prof who enjoys pointing out how smoothly he segues from one topic to the next, providing his class with "time capsules," & advocating to run run run!

Iverson is AMAZING. People always look forward to his lectures- he knows how to explain the same topic in a million different ways so every kind of student will understand. He works tirelessly to make sure every student has the opportunity to do extremely well in his class, and the head TA (Chris) is great too. You will love this class!!!!
Dr. Iverson, if you read this. You made me love a class I once used to hate. I was having anxiety over Ochem, but you changed that. Thank you for being there for your students, thank you for caring.

You are LUCKY if you have the chance to take him. I was so scared to take Ochem bc I'm an average student and I loved his class and he is hands down my fav prof. He is super accessible outside class despite corona. He goes above and beyond to help you learn and keep you interested in lecture. He also provides a ton helpful materials and practices.

analysis.name: Ivan Martinez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Like other comments, he does care about attendance, which he manages by having pop quizzez but does offer enough pop quizzes over the semester to receive full credit if you miss any. He is honestly a very nice teacher and cares about what he is teaching. Overall, a really nice teacher who cares about literacy and tries his best to show it.

He was okay but if you're not into film at all it might be a lot to take his class... def not just an easy english class I would just take the big one. You have to show up to every class because there are pop quizzes over the readings that are sometimes NOT fair. But you have a grade negotiation at the end which is nice!
The class is very small (20 ish people) and there is readings every week. You do have random pop quizes but you have the opportunity to make up points if you miss them.

analysis.name: Vishy Iyer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Gives vague instructions and grades far too harshly for such little guidance. Even when you reach out for help/clarification, he either tells you to figure it out on your own or talks to you like you should already know the answer. He spends far too much time talking about things we already know and not enough on things actually affecting grades

Dr.Iyer gives extremely hard homework that is barely covered in lecture, he spends 75 minutes talking about pure nonsense, that is due in 3 days after he opens it. Whole class asked for ,ore time and he wouldn't give it. He doesn't answer questions and his questions on the homework's don't make sense half the time. Take any other professor! RIH
Iyer is the worst professor I ever had in my four years here!!!!!!!! His homework's are extremely long, he does not explain anything or give good feedback to do better on other assignments.
Hard homeworks with no feedback

Dr. Iyer is a great choice if you're needing to take genetics. You can tell that he actually cares about his students and is knowledgeable about the content he's teaching. On most days during lecture there was a QOTD which you turn in, an instapoll, and random zoom polls which counted only towards participation. Relatively easy to do for credit.

analysis.name: Isabella Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's the best; she helped me survive waves. Would 100% take again.
Great Professor, Finally understand Maxwell's equations, and found the last digit of Pi!
Dr. Zhang is an amazing professor and really cares about students and wants everyone to succeed
Great person with very energetic personality and very intelligent!

analysis.name: Ian Molineux
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Molineux has been my favorite professor at UT!! The class is really intimidating at first (graded only on FRQ exams, a presentation, and some in-class participation points) but prof is super sweet and knowledgeable. Lectures are very dense with important details, so utilize his office hours+textbook as much as you can! Logic > pure memorization

His tests were difficult, but he curves at the end of the semester so everyone ended up doing fine. The class is graded just be 3 in class exams, all free response. For us they consisted of 10 questions and you had to pick 8 to answer. Overall I don't think the class is bad at all.

He is a sweet guy but is so educated that I fear there is a gap of knowledge that he has a hard time bridging with his undergraduate students. His tests are some of the hardest I have ever taken, but he curves a lot. Pretty inaccessible and not very technologically savvy. His lectures were very boring and he talks so quiet its hard to hear him.

Dr. Molineux is a nice guy in person and he really just wants his students to get something out of the class. That being said, his lectures are sometimes hard to follow and at times the class feels like a survey course. His exam setup is really nice as it allows for you to drop questions you have no hope of answering. Grades are curved immensely.

Dr. Molineux is nice, but he tends to mumble during lecture so unless you sit towards the front you can't really hear him. His tests are all free response, but you get to pick which 8/10 you answer. However, he wants very specific answers, so the class average on the tests was always low (but he curves the whole class at the end so you're fine).

analysis.name: Irving Dai
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He overcomplicates a lot of things and goes into irrelevant detail about it. Obviously good if you love calculus but for the sake of doing good on exams and quizzes it's just easier to learn the steps to do it through youtube and homeworks as opposed to trying to understand the minuscule details about how something relates to something not covered.

Dai was overall a caring and intelligent professor. The exams are structured based on the quizzes, although it was a little harder. No practice exams only reviews that are harder than the exam. 2 midterms and 1 final. TA was goated tho, shoutout to Nathan. Just be a little "clever" and you can do well in this class.

Good lecturer and definitely knows what he's talking about. Often times proves all concepts in his lectures, which can be irritating for students with AP credit who couldn't get out of the course. Gives plenty of in-class examples. Textbook not mandatory. Quizzes & HW are harder than tests, but final was harder than all midterms.

Dr. Dai explained things really clearly, mainly from a mathematical proof perspective, which I liked but may not be the best for others. He allowed us to use a notecard on all tests, which was really nice, and the quizzes are fine as long as you look at the practice quiz. My only complaint is that he sometimes explains too quickly.

Super nice professor but not the best at explaining. If you took BC Calc in high school and did well, class will be sooo easy. Does not fully explain concepts in class and will have to learn at TA sessions. Exams are exactly like weekly quizzes and he allows a notecard to write anything for exams.

analysis.name: Ilya Finkelstein
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Wow, well I should really have listened to all the warnings and rumors. He is an awful professor, rude and a gotcha artist. He has made several cry. He clearly loves flexing on his students - he clearly knows a lot, but just doesn't teach it and he gives the feeling that he is too good to teach. way too much work for so little pay off.
It's hilarious this guy is still allowed to teach. Avoid at all costs. Even his graduate students are afraid of him
why did i take this class? first time a teacher has made me cry.
do not take his course under any circumstances. awful human in a position of power.

The worst Biochem class & professor I've ever taken. Smart guy, but terrible at teaching. Hardly anything from the lectures or office hours are actually on the exams. You study so much material to get tested on none of it. Test averages were in the 60s, yet he barely curves; a 66 to 69 is a C. What a joke. Oh, & he's not caring at all whatsoever.

analysis.name: John Osborn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Everything (including some exams) is collaborative, essays are not bad, and the content is very manageable. If you can look at definitions/theorems and apply them, you can do the proofs in this class. He's a nice guy but particular about notation and formalities. Be respectful and you'll be fine. Probably the easiest class in the department.

GOAT! Tests are identical to assigned study problems (or similar methods to solve). 6 quizzes, 2 dropped. GO TO DISCUSSION!! HELPS A LOT FOR PREPARING FOR TESTS AND QUIZZES. No graded homework, but they were useful as practice for exams. 

I personally didn't think he was the best lecturer, but he makes the class easy if you put in a little effort.

Gives you almost, if not the exact questions that will be on the midterm. Midterms are five questions and he gives you 12 to study, which is extremely manageable. TA was fantastic and explained solutions very clearly. Lecture is a little theory heavy, but solutions to every homework are posted in a timely manner. Take him if you want an A.

Super unhelpful and very condescending. I would take any other professor but him. Before the 3rd exam, half of the entire class q dropped because everyone was failing. Only 8 questions on the exam and no partial credit.

Lectures are useless, but TA sections are GREAT. I didn't go to any lectures beyond the first week of class.

Prof gives a study guide before every exam, and the problems on the exam will typically be drawn straight from the study guide.

analysis.name: Jonathan Valvano
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Labs are very time consuming and frustrating, the second exam is an assembly program which you have to write, and debug on the fly in an hour. Worth 25%.. Either it works, or it doesn't.. Needless to say, it ruined my chance at A. 319K is just a weed out class you have to go through and there's no way around it. Start on the labs EARLY!!

The only real gripe I have with this guy is that he is EXTREMELY disorganized. One look at his office will tell you everything you'll ever need to know about him. Do NOT rely on him to make announcements about things or help you meaningfully, he can probably clarify some stuff but you might just end up the butt of a bad joke.

Took both 319k and 445l. Tough professor, tough labs, tough exams. Lots of work. Valvano is willing to bend over backwards to pass his students. He has office hours every weekday and picks excellent TA's. Lectures are scattered but very helpful. 445l is more structured than 319k. Heavy emphasis on debugging, hirerability, and maintaining your job.

EE 319K is the worst class I have ever taken. The labs are unworldly time consuming and difficult, and lab check-out is very stressful and the TA's ask you ridiculous, irrelevant questions. Absolutely HATED this class. Valvano is really unorganized and so is the class. If you're like me and need structure, you won't get it from this class.

valvano is a really funny person and an absolutely horrendous lecturer which is a bit unfortunate cause the class is actually very interesting, but you're able to learn most of the material from labs and practice exams. if it were a harder course he would've been worse but the class structure makes his class just alright

analysis.name: John (jack) Stoney
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Synonyms for quirky is a place to start, I guess. Eccentric, interesting, funny, talks about things that don't always seem relevant. But in the grand scheme of life maybe everything is relevant. At times he seems condescending. Hard to know if I'm reading him right. I almost wish he expected/asked/demanded more of students. He might be surprised.

For sure a character; for intro he has great projects that lets you learn a lot of mediums. Lots of demos. Read through an insufferable book on modern sculpture and had group discussion. Does not post anything on canvas but you can text him any questions, anytime. Hilarious and caring. Donuts for crit, and random weird snacks occasionally

Had such a good semester in Stoney's class! The projects in intro are material based and help you gain a confidence with the different mediums and applying them to sculpture. We had a presentation project where we had to research two artists and present them to the class, super easy and very educational. Overall, I would recommend him to everyone!

His projects involve lots of experimentation. He wants you to learn through your mistakes, and will often leave you to your own devices. He will grade you on the time and thought you put into your work, and you'll find his class to be casually cerebral.

Had him for Degree Track Perspc Studio. Class is sculpture based b/c he's that kind of artist. Lots of readings for HW, discussions about readings in class, must get a different sculpture library book every week, site visits are often, a single group project/presentation, watched videos often. Easy A if you show up and participate. He's so funny!!

analysis.name: John Rumrich
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I learned absolutely nothing. You really will not be getting your money's worth here. If you care about learning, do not take this class with this professor. If you want an easy A, go for it, but you'll be bored to death.

He will waste your time and money. You won't learn anything about Crime Fiction. He's a pleasant, intelligent man, but puts no effort into teaching. He will waste a lot of class time talking about John Milton. If you're looking for an easy "A," then you won't mind. I had hoped to learn.

chill and interesting class. attendance isn't mandatory, but DO ATTEND bc the exams are just things he talks about during class. pretty easy class, just pay attention during lectures and take notes. i suggest having a few friends on a shared note doc so you can catch up when you miss stuff (his powerpoints don't help).

If you need a UGS I 1000000% recommend this class. It was so much fun! There are 4 or 5 quizzes the entire semester but as long as you pay attention and take notes in class, you genuinely don't even need to study. There were 3 other assignments in the entire year that were so easy and graded really lightly. Rumrich is the best prof ever fr.

best professor i have ever had. prof rumrich is a master at his craft, is well-knowledgeable, and encouraging to his students. his lectures feel like a conversation, and as long as you do the readings they are easy to follow. SHOW UP TO CLASS!! and ask questions!! i can't stress enough how awesome this guy is.

analysis.name: Jay Whitehead
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Mr. Jay is very caring and you can tell he loves calc. Explains concepts well, and I personally thought his lectures were very helpful. He does spend a lot of time on warmups, but they're often relevant + help you learn how to do different problems. Office hours were also very accessible to me! Tests were not bad at all; gives back a lot of points.

The professor can be difficult to contact. The professor will spend 30+ minutes on the warm-up and skim through the content covered on the test. There are no extra-credit opportunities. Test reviews can be long and don't reflect the test. Be ready to learn on your own if you take this class, and be an expert in algebra and trig.

Best professor I have had while at UT. Very passionate about his work and makes sure all students understand before moving on. Speak up if you have a question he will answer it to the best of his abilities. Good review sessions and good TA. Highly recommend taking a course with Whitehead if possible.

Professor is a very kind man. However, his lectures are very disorganized. He spends more than 30 minutes on warmups which are sometimes helpful. TA isn't much help either, often gets many things wrong and is just as lost as the students sometimes. Exams make up most of your grade so be ready for that. Be ready to study and to have a hard time.

Jay is decent, but the math department truly is awful. The lectures are fine, but he typically solves halfway and then you have to wait and ask later for help. The practice exams do not help, they are old exams and don't match at all. Several Homeworks a week that require office hours since the questions aren't answered in Lecture.

analysis.name: Jesse Johnson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's nice and a great lecturer, however be prepared to cram for exams as grades are only three exams, and a policy memo, so you genuinley only have four shots to make an A so dont slack, go to class--his lectures arent recorded so being there genuinley matters. Test is over textbook chapters and slides.

Prof. Johnson is an excellent professor. He does his best to make a sometimes-bland area of study into an engaging and exciting lesson, though his lectures are quite dense. There are not many assignments that factor into the grade, but the workload is manageable. Highly recommend for an overview of the field of IR.

One of the best classes I've taken at UT. Professor Johnson is passionate and very knowledgeable about international relations and makes the lectures interesting and interactive. The class and material is straightforward as long as you go to class and read the textbook. There are only a few grades but grading tends to be in your favor.

He was an amazing professor, you can tell he his passionate about the subject and makes the lectures interesting and fun. Be aware there is very few grades in this class 3 exams, a paper and in class activities. However along as you pay attention during lectures and read the books the test are pretty simple. I would take again and learned a lot !

One of my favorite professors so far! He is extremely knowledgeable, and that is reflected in his lectures. He takes questions and actually cares about what is said. There are in-class activities usually every class, but missing one or two is okay. Tests are also easy if you pay attention and do readings.I highly recommend this class and professor.

analysis.name: Debra Hansen
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 327 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are very boring and very confusing. She's very patronizing and will look down upon you if you ask questions she deems stupid. She will rarely directly answer a question, instead she'll pose a new question that'll confuse you even more. You'll basically have to fuse with your textbook in order to do well.I highly regret taking this course.

I'm sitting in hansen's class right now and I wish I hadn't come. She has an incredible ability to not answer a single question, even when asked directly. On top of this, her lectures are confusing and not relevant to the tests. Study the textbooks, go to the TAs (not gustavo), and really know your stuff and you'll be fine, but don't expect help.

This woman ruined my mental state for a solid 8 months. She was a boring lecturer with immensely unfair tests. Do the learning objectives, know them back and forth and hope for the best with the tests. She would overlook huge topics in tests while pinpointing dumb facts. Study more than you need to, and study the lectures before book. Good luck.

Dr. Hansen makes biology very unbearable. It's almost as if she doesn't even know the material herself.  She asks lots of questions in class, and never provides the correct answer, leaving her students very confused.  Not worth your time-- I would honestly recommend taking Bio another semester if she is your only choice.

Worst professor I've ever had at UT. She is HORRIBLE. Her lectures are irrelevant to the tests and she is impossible to please. The tests are filled with mediocre facts that were never mentioned in the reading or lecture. It's impossible to know what to study. Sweet lady, horrible professor.

analysis.name: Martin Kevorkian
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I like Dr. Kevorkian! I was kind of bored with the material but found myself engaging anyway because he had a good lecturing style. He was a fairly easy grader on essays and he highlights student accomplishment. Wish the class had more variety in the readings though. I got tired of the after a while.

He seems to be a chill guy, but is not really the most understanding person when it comes to situations and is very strict for some reason as an English teacher. Also he looks at his rate my professor a lot, and keeps flagging the ones that make him look not good.

This guy clearly doesn't pay attention to attendance cause he'll deduct points for attendance for no reason. But they he'll give it fully to people who don't show up. He's past his prime in terms of teaching and it's showing
He's not very good at giving feedback and not fast at grading. This takes away from improving as a writer. He is also very poor at using technology.

Class discussion was mostly student-led. There were three essays and a short response about once a week. Readings could be somewhat heavy if you're not in the mood, but I thought they were very reasonable and well-paced. Dr. Kevorkian is a really nice professor with a passion for the subject and enthusiasm for student thoughts. Great guy.

analysis.name: Spyros Kinnas
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's so funny and passionate. Love the professor, dislike the class. The exams are extremely difficult, and the homework is very long. My TA was awesome for the lab (best TA I've ever had), so they were bearable. He gives points to students who answer his questions, so make sure to speak up; you will need the extra points.

I love Dr. Kinnas. He is funny, his lecture is very easy to focus. The material itself is hard but he tries his best to help us out. The homeworks are challenging but if you really try in class, you can do good. The lab is easy and if you focus during lab, you will understand the lecture better.

The lab sessions were fascinating, with assignments that were easy to complete. The homework, on the other hand, was tedious, often taking several hours each. However, this is slightly offset by the generous partial credit given. The professor also does his best to know and check in with each student, ensuring their well-being and participation.

I didn't expect this class to be so math/theory based. It's essentially a hardcore math class with ocean and wave influence. Weekly homeworks are quite long and tedious. Can use a notes sheet on exams but they are difficult. He does give partial credit. Dr. Kinnas is clearly passionate and knowledgeable but the course is just hard. Project no Final

Difficult material but a great class. Long weekly homeworks that were kinda tough, but he very clearly explains how to do everything in well-planned and descriptive lectures. Tough exams. Capped off with a term design project that was super interesting and just the right amount of work. Overall it's a tough class but well worth the effort

analysis.name: Daniel Kahozi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall, the class was very fun and definitely improved my french skills. If you aren't consistently keeping up with your french then the class will be considered more difficult. However, Prof Kahozi is always available, willing to meet with his students, & he wants them improve their french skills. He's easy to talk to and he's very understanding!

He is very nice, but sometimes the class was confusing. You usually just review textbook material with a partner in class. The tests and quizzes are difficult, but he is an easy grader for other assignments. There are two essays, which is 30% of your grade; he values effort, not accuracy. Lots of out-of-class assignments, but manageable.

Took him for FR322E and wish I could have taken him for FR320. Show up to class because participation is mandatory, and things covered in class go on the exams. Quizzes were probably the hardest aspect of the class, but still an easy A if you put in the time and some effort. Merci Daniel!

I took both 320 and 322 with Professor Kahozi, and I really enjoyed his classes. I definitely struggled with some parts of these classes, but overall, Kahozi gives lots of opportunities to improve your grade, so that was never something that concerned me.

This class definitely reduced my love for French. The average on most of the quizzes was close to a 40, and people were not given their accommodations even after asking for them multiple times. We had to rely on the book to teach us majority of the material. Super difficult for me despite learning French for years. Would not take him again.

analysis.name: Jason Brownlee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 123 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: It's almost like the professor is trying to make lectures incomprehensible. There's no reason "America's prudence eclipsed its swagger" is a phrase that should be used. On a positive note, quizzes and exam questions are largely derived from the weekly comprehension checks; however, they have been changed to a closed-book, lockdown browser format.

I took this online class to get a breather from all my in person upper division classes, i needed a break. Little did I know this would be my hardest class I have. The lectures are long and you HAVE to take notes on every miniscule topic because the most random note WILL be on an exam or quiz. Overall, horrible experience so far and I might Q drop.

The questions asked on tests are WAY too specific, having to remember specific dates of events and names of bills or acts, while also needing to memorize the names of leaders of countries at different points in time, is ridiculous. Apparently this class used to be open note, it isn't now, which would make it possible to do well in class.

Getting too much info each week. So many details for the test/quiz to be about 1 specific thing he said 24 minutes 39 seconds into a 45-minute video. 

This class used to be open note, which I think is fair for the amount of information he is giving, but now that it's not, you have to spend way more time than suggested to do well.

I do not understand where the bad reviews from this semester are coming from. I am a STEM major and this class was a cake walk. Not only that, but it was interesting. It really doesn't get better then this for the government credit at UT. Take if able.

analysis.name: Kirsten Bradbury
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 165 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: She is so awesome, I loved having her an have taken several classes with her - I wish I could take every class with her. She's so accommodating and lenient and cares about her students more than anything else.

This class is one of the easiest but most enjoyable courses I've taken this year. You have to genuinely try not to get an A, because the entire course is online and open-note. Dr. Bradbury is really funny, and her lectures can be super interesting. I recommend taking this class if you need something easy and fun to fill up your schedule.

Clinical psych with Bradbury is one of the best classes in the psych major. TAKE IT. Her lectures are super interesting and easy to understand and readings aren't too heavy. Quizzes could sometimes be hyper-specific but as an online asynch course I get that. She was very nice and helpful over email too!

This course was very well organized and Dr. Bradbury is clearly interested in the work which makes participation easier and the curriculum more digestible. Expectations and grading strategy were clear and simple. Highly recommend.

This class was a much needed easy a in my schedule. The lectures and supplemental material are interesting but easy to comprehend. There are no late grades until the end of the semester, so there's really no excuse for failing.

analysis.name: Amrita Kaur
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 112 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The situation is that the professor is great but the class is extremely difficult, likely in an effort to prepare us for computer architecture. While her quick pace might be difficult for some, I personally had little issue following along. On top of that, Professor Kaur is literally reading books on kindness, like she clearly cares about students.

As a CS major, this class made me want to change majors. The coding assignments were fun but the lectures and tests were NOT IT. Her tests are heavy on "can you do this? what will error out?" and her lectures just go on and on about syntax and stuff. She seems like a nice person and office hours helped a lot but I will try not to take her again.

read all of this. I'll start by saying she is an amazing teacher, just not a good professor. She's really fun in class, but she loves handing out zeros on her homework assignments, which is hard to come back from. I enjoyed the class before we were given back our homework grades (1 month after submitting!), but she was not helpful after that.

I personally enjoyed the HWs even though they were challenging because they were quite enjoyable to code up. However, I feel like most of my effort went into doing good style and docstrings. Sometimes we don't know about certain style requirements until after it was graded, especially at the end unless you asked the TAs. Final was hard, but curved

Professor Kaur has really good lectures. The programming assignments are long and you can lose a lot of points because of poor style (especially at the semester start), but since there's so much lecture/feedback form extra credit it's easy to get full credit. Tests are really hard and worth a ton but there are practice tests posted, so study a lot!

analysis.name: Kate Pounders
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Pounders is, so far, my favorite professor at UT. The material is actually very interesting and lectures are entertaining to listen to. She provides a lot of cool examples of ads so that the class can understand the content more. She did cancel class a few times, but I wouldn't call that a downfall. Textbook is necessary for online quizzes.

Ethics was a great class! I enjoyed the balance between lectures and group work. Lectures were engaging, and group work days were chill but interesting to dissect with peers. The topics we discuss are relevant to the modern world while still acknowledging the history of ethics in advertising. Overall, loved it!

It was my worst class by far. Murphy's tests were easier than her quizzes, because you were getting grades for what you know. In Pounders' class doesn't matter if you study or not. She's confusing as hell. She should take some class at ACC to get better with computers, because boy... she's damn slow with anything what has buttons. Take Drumwright.

I loved this prof and class! Your grade consists of 3 out of class writing assignments, random in class activities for participation, 10 question timed online quizzes for each chapter, 3 exams and an optional final (if you didn't miss any of the 3 exams). Cancelled class a few times but there's nothing on the exam that we didn't go over in class.

Not too difficult, engaging, relevant discussions, multiple case studies that can be done before class ends. There are guest speakers towards the end of the semester, which are also interesting, and grading isn't too tough. There's room for open-minded discussion.

analysis.name: Lara Latimer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Latimer is the best. She's very open minded and has interesting discussions with her students in class. Awesome guest speakers. She gave extra credit which was awesome because we got to go to a yoga studio all semester for free. She also gives extra credit for just coming to class. She'll tell you exactly what is on the test during lecture!!!

Even though her many assignments were not particularly the "hardest", you better get ready to read cause either wise you'll find yourself losing points for not being "thoughtful" enough or "specific" enough in your writing responses. You may read a lot of comments that she is very nice but she is very self-center and has zero original thoughts.

Dr. Latimer is super kind and genuinely cares about each student. She always opens up discussions with insightful feedback and makes the classroom feel like a safe space. I have learned a lot in this class and it was very a cool structure. There are a lot of readings and the assignments definitely pile on at the end of the year, but still chill.

Literally my favorite prof this semester. Discussion-based lectures. 12 modules, 1 assignment and knowledge check per mod, and 4 quizzes (over 3 mods each). Was witty and funny while covering info which kept me engaged. Need 10 participation points which are assigned at random to lecture days. TAKE HER CLASS!

Dr. Latimer can be strict about some things but ultimately an easy class. There's 1 assignment and quiz per unit that you do outside of class, and all were pretty easy. You only need 10 attendance points so you really don't have to show up much. Lots of good topics covered! If you take her class she brings in therapy dogs so I 100% recommend lol!

analysis.name: Linda Reichl
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: I'm going to lock in and learn every physics principle, concept, thoroughly study every idea Albert Einstein had on relativity so that I can grow up, invent a time-machine to time travel back and not take this class.

Dr. Reichl is very accomplished in physics, but when teaching, it's mediocre at best. Unless you are already REALLY comfortable in physics, you will be struggling to understand anything the whole semester because the pacing is lightning speed. Granted, physics at Ut is already difficult as it is, so Reichl isn't the worst if you learn on your own.

Professor Reichl is a sweet lady, but she is past her years of teaching. Linda read incoherent lecture notes word for word that she had written down, and many times got herself confused. This is the worst class I have taken at UT, and avoid her at all costs.

Linda does not teach. She genuinely just writes over printed notes making them completely illegible. I pulled up to class but never bothered to take out my notebook because attempting to take notes is useless. If you ask her questions, she will proceed to answer a different question that you didn't ask. The only saving grace is the online midterms.

She is a wonderfully kind human. Lectures are kind of useless but mandatory, however you can zoom them. Homework's are long but doable, tests and quizzes are on quest. The worst part about this class is the TA. If you end up with Peter,  he judges you instead of helping you, and makes the mandatory discussion miserable. Hand to God I hope he quits.

analysis.name: Lauren Mitchell
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 121 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Mitchell gives STEM baddie, she's a good lecturer and very transparent when it comes to due dates and preparing for what exactly will be on exams. You have the opportunity to retake 2 exams for full credit, and she gives a generous amount of extra credit and dropped classes. UT did their big one by hiring her, looking forward to CH302 with her!

A great professor who gives so many resources to succeed. She gives lots of extra credit, her lectures are amazing, and has plenty of study resources. Daily quizzes in class which are surprisingly helpful and helped me from procrastinating for tests. The learning modules and review notes are the only things I used to study.

Professor Mitchell is a great lecturer and very communicative from the beginning about what to expect from her course. There are two quizzes a week over what was covered in the previous lecture, and four exams which make up most of your grade. Plenty of extra credit opportunities and the ability to retake two exams make it very easy to succeed.

Professor Mitchell is a wonderful professor! I had her for CH301 and CH302 because I loved her teaching style and class format. Yes, there are daily quizzes, but I found them to be more beneficial for ingesting material one quiz at a time; for me, I'd rather have more quizzes with fewer topics than fewer quizzes with more topics. Take her for chem!

her course is so organized! quizzes are daily so attendance is mandatory. i personally found her canvas course more helpful than lectures. she has a lot of opportunities to reach her outside of class and a lot of resources to study for tests. provides enough extra credit to bump you up a letter grade. i struggle w chem but 301 wasn't so bad!

analysis.name: Leonard Moore
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 253 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He relies a lot on rhetoric to persuade people of his arguments. He is quite intimidating. He says he wants people to talk and give opinions, he doesn't listen when you give an opinion and argues it before he understands it. He is almost impossible to meet outside class. However, he does get his students thinking by discussing taboo topics.

funny and engaging professor opened my eyes to other perspectives STRONG political bias (welcome to atx) required books were interesting discussion session with assigned TA for 1 hour a week pop quizzes given in lecture & in discussion section write 2 timed essays for midterm & final topics easy to predict you get study guides

He changed up the class to have group projects that rely on random student evaluations so can get a bad grade (25% of your grade) by a judgy student. T.A's are disorganized and make last minute changes that get lost in canvas notfications. Its an intersting class but be ready for disorganization.

Very few assignments (2 exams, 1 individual project, 1 group project). Exams are BlueBook essays, tough if you're not good at on-the-spot writing. Huge grading differences across TAs. Attendance isn't taken, but no slides posted so you'll be lost if you skip. Lectures are funny but can feel like a waste of time on a Monday night. Not an easy A.

DON'T take this course if you want to learn about college football. The class was on the history of African Americans and college football-yes interesting, but not what I signed up for. He is also impossible to get in contact with and tests consist solely of free response essays. Lectures are funny but not worth it.

analysis.name: Michael Sailors
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 99 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Super easy VAPA if you just do the work. About 1, 5 question quiz a week and all the answers can be found word for word in the previous lecture. Majority of your grade comes from Cerego Homework which is so easy as long as you just do it. You are required to go to two jazz concerts a semester and write a 500 word paper but its graded super easy.

Cerego is a bit annoying but easy to complete. Lectures are 15- 30-ish minutes have 6-8 instapolls and there's like 6 per module and 4 modules per week. great guy, DO CEREGO AND LISTENING QUIZZES. Those will TANK your grade if you forget. Easy class jsut keep up

Honestly ended up finding the content very interesting, despite not really enjoying jazz prior to taking this class. Now, I really can appreciate jazz whenever I hear it! The lectures are great and interesting, and the Cerego sets are totally manageable as long as you don't start late. Really easy class that I really enjoyed.

Dr. Sailors was a great professor and made jazz fun and exciting. The part of going to concerts for a grade and writing about them was fun. Make sure you show up to every class for your instapolls there's a lot (100, graded for 90). Overall the class was very enjoyable.

Girl. Just take this class. You don't need to love jazz, but it's definitely an easy class. That said, it does come with work but it's nothing that should be giving you a headache. Only thing that may be bothersome to some people is to actually go out to a concert. I went to the free UT Jazz Combo nights at Mozarts and loved it.

analysis.name: Patrick McDonald
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 154 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are boring and it's never clear on what you need to understand. The textbook assignments are so long and boring as well and it is one of the worst things ever. So many assignments due every week, take so long and overall DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

McDonald is a good professor. Watching him and Moser interact was always funny. Course material can be a bit difficult to understand and goes pretty fast at times. I always had a relatively hard time on the test, as they seemed a little hard for an intro course like this. Lots of outside the class modules and readings. Overall, I enjoyed the course

This class's exams were way harder than they needed to be for a core class. The modules were easy, it's fine, but they don't really provide you with any study materials for exams. The exams had like "A and B" and "A, B, and C" options that made it confusing and just harder than it needed to be. Idk, easy lectures, tough exams.

Overall, this class is very easy. Him and Professor Moser do an amazing job of breaking down the material, and use bullet points/power points to highlight the topics of the lectures online. I do wish that there were more study guides provided for exams. It's also important to note that they use HonorLock, so there's no cheating/no using A.I.

Exam grades make 75% of the grade in the class. Even if you take care of your assignments that covers only 25% of your grade. If you mess up one exam really bad then you are pretty much screwed for the class. I suggest that if you take this class you should be ready to block out multiple hours of your day outside of your main classes to study gov

analysis.name: Robert Moser
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 235 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Moser literally reads off a teleprompter for all of the required lecture videos, but stutters on every other word. He is a bad lecturer and is unclear in both his slides and module videos. Overall, the class is a lot of work but not too bad. The professor, on the other hand is pretty god awful. Exams have poor word choice and bad grammar.

Lectures are sooo horrible because they literally read a teleprompter and stutter and struggle with their own words. It's hard to learn because of this. My eyes glaze over. Class/quiz is online only ONCE a week but there's a lot of videos you have to watch outside of class. Required readings are long but you don't actually need to read them.

Grades tough. If you do not put specifically what they want you to put then you might as well pencil yourself in as a B. Tests are way harder than they should be. TAs grade like you have to quote the textbook. Would not recommend. Should have taken community college Gov.

His online GOV 312L class is pretty awesome. I didn't pay attention sometimes, but for the most part his lectures are interesting, he includes current events and talks about debatable issues and we get to see where we are on the spectrum compared to the rest of the class. 2 tests and 1 paper. Pretty easy overall. Just go over the powerpoints.

Moser is an alright professor, sometimes the modules can be very dry and he stumbles on his words often. The class really wasn't that bad; as long as you keep up with the module videos and read the class google docs before a test, you will be fine. The people saying this is the hardest class they have taken haven't taken a STEM course at UT.

analysis.name: Nicola Tisato
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very nice, funny, and approachable. In class lectures were kind of difficult to follow because they weren't very organized. Not much given to help you study for exams but only a few assignments the whole semester was nice to have

This was the first coding class I took and I'm really glad it was with Dr. Tisato. His lessons were clear and easy to follow. If you haven't taken coding before, it's hard at the beginning, but don't worry, you will get it eventually. Be patient. And don't worry, he will curve. Great professor. He's relaxed and has a good sense of humor.

I took him for the coding class and I did not enjoy it at all. Tisato himself was completely adorable - so funny and kind and patient. Unfortunately, that did not make the content any more understandable. His teaching is not clear and the class is very difficult, especially if you have no previous coding experience.

analysis.name: Martha Maas
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 224 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Biology lab is the most useless class you could take. Dr. Maas uses this class in a way to make herself feel more important than she is. The material you are supposed to learn is very simple and is already learned in class, and Maas makes the tests and analyses very convoluted. I loved my LI, but this class killed any love for lab I had before.

My least favorite class at UT by FAR. I found organic chemistry easier than this class because she was so unclear on what we needed to know for exams. Rather than covering larger important concepts, we needed to know the length of a nematode and specific crayfish parts. She seems to really enjoy power and exercising it over students.

This class can be super stressful. There is 2 exams and a practical. No final! Also, there is lab prep hw, lab analysis, lecture questions, and peer review for every lab (12). Some labs are boring such as the plant one. Cool labs were the chick embryo and the crayfish one. Exams are hard because each exam are over 6 labs. But they're fair!

I've done research for three years, aced every biology class I've taken here, and sincerely love science and biology. Despite all of that this class seriously made me consider dropping my BIO major, picking up BCH instead. Boring, tedious, and none of the material is even close to real science. Essentially a high school class.

Since it's a lab, your experience is highly dependent on the TA. Nonetheless, I did not enjoy the professor. Her lectures are random and boring. You don't really know what to expect for the tests and some of the questions are ridiculously specific. This class was unnecessarily difficult considering how the concepts covered were not advanced.

analysis.name: Nicole Smith
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
A caring prof but is lowkey carried by her course topic. The topics are very  
current making engagement easy and natural however her lectures are very cyclical. She more often than not sounds like she is struggling to express what she is trying to say and doesn't word her writing coherently. I did however love both my discussion section and my TA.

Professor Smith teaches a very easy class. As long as you sort of pay attention in lecture, you'll get an A. Readings are insightful if you actually care about the content. Their lectures often stray away from the ideas being discussed and end up addressing the thoughts and objections of a single imaginary strawman.

Prof Smith is nice but spends a lot of lectures rambling off-topic instead of better explaining some complex concepts. They are a very easy grader if you get everything done and put in a little effort. No electronics unless you have accommodations, they went on multiple rants about this because people would do it anyway. Pretty simple intro class

Dr. Smith was a really enjoyable professor. Her course was not graded by many assignments, which felt pretty intimidating, but overall, she was pretty forgiving with grades. She lectured each class and was great at separating personal beliefs from the content. Overall, you get what you put into it, so if you do the readings, it's worthwhile.

Dr. Smith is the best professor I have had the pleasure of learning from. They are really good at explaining complex concepts more simply and covering all of the ethical considerations of a concept. I am so glad I took PHL 304 as my first philosophy course because it set me up really well for my other ethics courses. Best. Professor. Ever.

analysis.name: Nicholas Snashall-Woodhams
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is nice and means well but his teaching style is so ineffective. You end up having to teach yourself everything because he just lectures on and on about theory and doesn't do actual problems during class that reflect what's on the actual exam. This makes lectures annoying and a waste of time. He has a cool Australian accent tho
He's there to help; the class content can be confusing. If you pay attention to class, he does a good job of explaining the theories. Go to office hours if you are confused!!!

Woodhams has the unique ability of turning a simple and intuitive concept into something utterly unintelligible. He loves to teach by using variables and keeping things "theoretical" instead of just using real numbers or examples to explain things like a regular human being. If you enjoy vague math concepts, he's the guy. If not, stay away from him

His lectures are very boring, and it becomes your job to sit through it and filter what is actually important. Spoiler alert: it's not very much. This guy will spend 90% of the time deriving things that don't matter and aren't tested and maybe 10% of the time talking about how things are actually used to answer questions. Good luck yall

He is a really good professor who knows what he's teaching. Lecture and content heavy class - so make sure you attend + take good notes. Exam heavy, but as long as you do the practice exams and problems, you should be fine. Attend his OH for the problem sets for help - they're difficult. Overall chill guy.

analysis.name: Nik Palomares
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
