review_highlights.comment: I had Nik for CMS 367 and it was purely a class I'd go to to talk. Discussions on readings, personal experiences, etc. You just needed to talk at least once a week for credit. He's pretty chill if your open minded and participate you'll do fine.
Never prepared, no lectures, just random spiels, talks about his divorce in class, certainly no expert on his field, rude to students. Genuinely don't know how this guy is a professor.

Idk what the reviews here are on about, they're one of the best professors I've ever had. They made Quantitative Research Methods fun. The class is based mostly on lectures that feel like casual conversations. Assignments are short with very clear directions. There is plenty of opportunities for extra credit on their exams. Nik is SO chill

Honestly they were really chill and this class changed my perspective on how arbitrary gender is. They say there's required readings but I feel that they're not really required. This class is definitely not a lecture and is entirely discussion based. One paper and one presentation about whatever you want, no exams. Can get kind of boring at times.

unorganized class. expects us to write a research paper on research he conducted years ago and doesn't know how to perform the research. counts students absent when they're 5 minutes late when attendance is mandatory/for a grade. expects students to get notes from other students since lectures are not posted. mumbles a lot and goes on tangents.

analysis.name: Nicolas Reyes
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are all over the place and there is little effort into them, Nicky is clearly passionate about math but it doesn't translate well in a teaching environment. To make matters even worse there is close to zero resources for self instruction outside of class, which would be okay if the lectures were great but they are abysmal. 0/10 course.

Professor Reyes seems nice, but struggles with expert bias and explains concepts poorly, making lectures hard to follow. The class is quiz and test-heavy with little review material, and the few questions make it easy to get low grades. There's also little communication with TAs, so support feels limited. I'd avoid if possible.

Had some of the best reviews for a calc prof but his switch from online exams to in person broke this class. Quizzes are two questions completely free response and weighted almost identically to the midterms. They are super difficult and they are NOT curved. I finished 408C with a 98 and am struggling to do well on his quizzes.

The professor described the quiz on proofs of reductions as “easy,” many students who don't work with this material found it quite challenging. The topic was not clearly explained during the TA discussion, which made the quiz harder to prepare. I would not be surprised if the scores were curved. lectures are sporadic and are not clear.

Reyes style of teaching, syllabus, and just general vibes from him have changed. Maybe something having to do with new math department guidelines as he mentioned on our first day. The main issues are homework not correlating to lectures, discussions being overly hard, and just in general no synchronization between the many parts of the course.

analysis.name: Shannon O'Brien
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 98 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lets just throw together 2 tests worth most of your grade while giving a study guide each with 300 terms then calling it a day. The tests are written as if they're open note and with 300+ terms in each test, pray youre lucky and get easy ones, every mistake is costly and getting 2-3 more wrong is a letter grade difference. Terrible grading system

Anything you heard before Fall 2025 about this class IT HAS CHANGED!!! Tests are honorlock and you are expected to know over 300+ vocab terms for each test. In retrospect if you have the time every week to listen to 10 lecture vids each being 45 min you should be okay in the class but If you're looking for an easy A+ I wouldn't take this class.

She is very passionate & can be funny at times, but nothing is funny when you're given 300 terms (without definitions/examples/context) a week before the exam and expected to deeply understand all of those terms. This class is definitely not treated like an introductory course for non-majors.

She's funny... But that's all I really got. The each test is 27% of your grade. Involves memorizing over 300 words, CLOSED BOOK/NOTE. In my opinion, the exams seem to be formatted like they're open book/note (like they were previously), but the percentage it takes up in the class does not reflect the increased difficulty for students.
Tests are implemented so students suffer and make sure your grade stays down. Interesting lectures ig

analysis.name: Tolga Ozyurtcu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O is an incredible professor who delivers thought provoking and interesting lectures every class. Attendance isn't required, but you will actually want to come to class just for the interactive discussions and lectures. You can absolutely make an A with reasonable effort, and he is one of my absolute favorite professors I have had so far!

Dr. O is fantastic. Just took his UGS 303 "Sports and Innovation" and it was a major win. Lectures were engaging and work was easy. 3 exams which are all basically the same that are graded very easily. All discussions are used working towards singular group project, not to difficult. Definitely the best UGS available at UT.

He is honestly the best professor I've had. His lectures aren't mandatory, but I found them to be super interesting and helpful. The class is very interactive, which helps lectures not be so boring. The exams are in blue books, but he tells you what is going to be on them, so just go to class. Amazing professor, I would definitely take him again!

Definitely one of the chillest professor that I have ever had. This course is very interesting to learn but attendance is not mandatory. As long as you come the class before the test, he tells you what is on it and has online notes posted on canvas which is super straightforward. He also gives extra credit as well!

Loved Dr. O! I didn't realize this was more of a baseline introductory class, as I took it for my minor, but it was still enjoyable. Just come to class as often as you can, take notes, and follow his instructions, and you'll be good to go! I appreciate his engaging teaching style and how he provides solid, real-life examples.

analysis.name: Olla Al-Shalchi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ustadha Olla is an awesome teacher; she definitely can make things harder, but honestly, they're all with the best of intentions. When you come out of the class, you have a greater understanding of Arabic, and if I didn't have a weed out the next semester, I definitely would have taken Arabic 2. Awesome Ustadha, and a caring one

If you're taking Arabic at UT, one of the best programs in the country, you take Olla. This isn't a contention. You'll have to work, show up, and do the readings, but she gives extra resources that actually help you learn, when other professors dont. She's available, flexible, and supportive. Get ready to work, but take Olla first. ⬆️⬆️⬆️⬆️⬆️⬆️

Unless you're heritage, this class will not be easy. But if you want to learn Arabic, then you should absolutely take Olla.
She is a very warm and friendly professor, and the class is very rewarding. Homework EVERY day, and lots of participation, 2 hours 3x a week. Like $200 on textbooks, but the books apply to 611C and 621K.
Highly recommend!

The BEST! I wasn't able to take her classes in the spring but she still met with me and helped me with anything I wasn't understanding. I passed my Arabic class in the Spring thanks to Olla making the time to help me out. I wish more professors were as caring as her. Don't hesitate to take her class and always ask for help if you need it. She's #1.

Dr Olla is an amazing professor who loves building connections and being relatable with her students. This was her first year teaching Gateway to Middle East so she was very flexible with our cohort when it came to quizzes and final exam and even grading the biweekly synopses. There is hefty amount of textbook weekly readings tho.

analysis.name: Ofodike Ezekoye
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ezekoye is simply a fabulous human being, easy-going, generous, and caring.  He's not always as organized in class, and some concepts could bear better explanation.  He connects well with his classroom, focuses on the most important concepts, and really cares that his students get something out of his class.

This is hands-down the worst professor I have taken thus far. Weekly quizzes worth 50% of our grade that are supposed to be based off weekly homework, but he always finds a way to screw everyone over by putting something that is completely irrelevant to the homework or "lectures" that we only found out existed about halfway through the semester.

Was a nice prof but literally taught us nothing. I learned nothing in the class and he never had ACTUAL lectures. Had to drop $$$ on the textbook. Our class averages on quizzes were in the 30s. Did not know how to properly teach in the online format. Disappointed because I know I'll need this info for future classes and I have no clue what we did.

Pretty much based the entire class (quizzes, homework, reading assignments, final) on the online textbook, besides his lectures. He switched up the quiz policy, causing a failing quiz average almost every week. The professor was nice and wanted to solve the issue, but he never really did. He started grading partial credit halfway into the semester

The other reviews cover everything you need to know. The lectures were too broad and not specific and although he is a nice guy, he was honestly the worst professor I've ever had at UT. He did his best to try to understand why we were not prepared, but by the time the final rolled around, we were woefully unprepared. Thank god for pass-fail.

analysis.name: Oscar Chaidez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: If you're looking at taking SPN601D, take Oscar. Oscar is very funny and wants his students to succeed. He makes learning simple and has a relaxed teaching style that encourages you to speak. If you weren't able to understand something in lecture he almost always has time to discuss with you after class.

TAKE SPANISH WITH OSCAR! He genuinely was the best teacher I have ever had and that says a lot! He made our entire 8am class engaged and laughing. Our entire class was lucky to be taught by Oscar, he cared for every one of us, and it showed by our attendance and participation in his class. Would take his class forever if I could!

The best professor! So caring, funny, and made a mandatory 2 hour lecture 3 times a week enjoyable. There is a lot of HW but it is not hard at all and the textbook is mandatory. Take Oscar for Spanish!!

Fantastic professor. Made a mandatory 8am class a class I WANTED to go to (that says a lot)! The textbook is absolutely 100% mandatory for this class - you can't get around it. I've progressed a lot through taking his class - highly recommend Prof. Chaidez!

AMAZING professor! Learning Spanish is hard, but he made it enjoyable. Extremely kind and teaches so you actually learn. Follows general Spanish department course structure. If you have to take this class, take this professor if you can!

analysis.name: Diana Orozco-Lapray

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O was such an amazing professor. At first, the exams can seem very daunting and the lectures seem fast paced. However, you get used to it and her lectures are very engaging. There are many extra credit opportunities and a chance to replace your lowest exam grade. Dr. O is so kind and understanding, and most of all deeply knowledgeable. TAKE HER

Dr.O is an amazing professor! Her class is one of the few that I made sure I attended despite her not taking attendance most days. Her lectures were engaging, fun, and interesting. Your grade is exam heavy, but she offers extra credit at the end of the year. Exams were tough but mostly everything is covered in lecture.

This professor is AMAZING. She is kind, loving, and treats her students like her own kids. Her class is normally paced, and the lab is one of my favorite things I've done in college. If you have the opportunity to, TAKE HER. SHE IS BEYOND INCREDIBLE!!!!

She is a very knowledgeable and kind professor. Her class is attendance optional. Test material comes entirely from lectures/recording. Other assignments are weekly quizzes/written assignments/activity. No test review but easy to study for just review notes/lecture recordings. She is very approachable for questions or office hours. I recommend her.

I loved Dr. O's class! So much wonderful info and very relevant to the world. She hasn't taught 313 in a while, so the class is still changing. 3-4 Exams + Lab portion with 2 easy papers! Lab grade is separate. Tests are open-note + online, but I would study for them. I learned a lot in this class! She wants you to do well! Incredibly knowledgeable

analysis.name: Tatem  Oldham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Oldham is so kind and sweet, and she's incredibly skilled at what she does. This class seems like a standard LAH requirement, but it can actually be really helpful if you use the resources provided. If I could go back, I'd attend the career events earlier in the semester instead of putting them off. Overall, such an easy and useful class.

Tatem is such a genuine and caring person. She's also one of the best possible connections to have on campus, and will connect you to so many resources if you make the effort to meet with her. The class is super light; just submit your assignments on time and make sure to attend events to reflect on for your final reflection paper.
Easiest seminar ever, and she's so sweet. There has to be something genuinely wrong for you to get less than an A in this class.

This class was ridiculously easy. There were quite literally one to two assignments due every month. As long as you don't forget to attend three events throughout the semester to write your final reflection paper and turn in your work on time, you should be fine.

analysis.name: Rachel Ozanne
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 141 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ozanne is a very nice professor and a good lecturer. I had a kind TA, so my grade was potentially higher than it should have been. I really enjoyed this class. The group projects are annoying, but Dr. Ozanne and the TAs are understanding if group members don't hold up their end of the project; it didn't reflect on my grade. Would recommend!

Easy class; the professor is really nice. You don't need the lectures to do good in class, and if you want you can watch the recordings on Canvas. There is a Canvas quiz every week, but they are really easy, and there is the occasional group timeline project, which is really manageable. Definitely take this class to fulfill the history requirement.

No tests or final, attendance not required with lecture recordings available + slides posted online which is really helpful Homework covers the bulk of the content anyway, so it's pretty easy to just set aside an hour or two to get the classes work out of the way for the week. There are a few papers and group projects, so just plan ur time for that

Prof Ozanne gives very engaging lectures and made history somewhat bearable for someone who really doesn't like history. Her class is fairly easy with minimal work outside of the 2 group projects, 2 essays, and the weekly chapter quizzes. However, some TAs grade harsher than others (like mine), but lots of EC is available.

Sometimes provides decent amount of extra credit if you go to her lectures. A lot is left up to the TA's so if you get a bad TA they will mess your grade up. Grades are carried by two projects and two essays which are grades harsh. Also sucks if you have a bad team. Professor can be a little passive aggressive also

analysis.name: Stephanie Osbakken
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took this course in person. Lectures weren't all mandatory but there were pop quizzes ( heavy at the end of the semester). All lectures were recorded. 10 pop quizzes but only 6 are graded. Lectures are kind of boring but there is a lot of resources for help. Test are all different ( free response, multiple choice, T or F). One group project.

She's wonderful- she's an engaging lecturer who really cares about both her subject material and her students and is really such a proponent for their success. Her tests are a little weird because she asks if multiple answers are correct are not, but the information is definitely relayed in class and in your readings.

Professor O is so passionate about her subject and is a very clear communicator. There are random pop quizzes, but you get a 100 for writing your name down, so they're more for attendance. My only issue was a group project worth 10% of your grade, where you are assigned a random group (and only given Canvas to find them in a class of 300+).

Loved this class! The lectures weren't always engaging but often very interesting. The content was easy to grasp and the tests were easy. You get a cheat sheet for 2/4 exams and 1 exam gets dropped. Attendance measured by group quizzes graded on participation. Only thing that was unenjoyable was the group project.

Amazing prof + TAs. Super interesting topics, a lot of it is pretty obvious/common sense topics being taught so it's not crazy hard. The free response exams are graded a little harshly and getting even a few half-points off can kind of tank your grade. Very charismatic teacher & had amazing guest speakers. Love her.

analysis.name: Dan Pryor
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT take Pryor if you have public speaking anxiety. Spoke to him about my anxiety disorder so that he could better help me improve, berated me in front of the whole class for no reason and made me cry. Truly enjoys picking on the quieter students, even when you show up to every class and put effort into assignments. Would never take again.

If you don't care much about your grade, he's fine. Fun class, but if you want any sort of A, good luck. Grades are based on random stuff, you will never understand why someone got 5 points higher or lower than you. There's little to no instruction on anything and points are taken off randomly.

DP tells a lot of stories and loves to make people laugh. He truly is a sweet old man and wants you to be friends with your class. A lot of people ended with an A-, but you can get an A if you go to office hours every time. All the TAs grade harshly without much reasoning. Don't be afraid of the A-; take Pryor's class and you'll learn something.

Great guy, hilarious, and he actually connects with the students. By the end of the semester, he makes sure you know the rest of your class, too.
Embrace the A-. There's basically no leeway to get an A, and the TA's grading is ridiculously harsh. So you'll almost definitely end with an A-, but it's a fun class, and Pryor is a really good professor.

Although, he is a tough grader on group presentations, Pryor is a nice and understanding professor. The grade you get is almost entirely dependent on your TAs. Double check writing guidelines to not lose points. Presentation grading is subjective, but is not hard to get an A if you put some effort. I didn't like the random 50 mcq tests at all.

analysis.name: Michelann Quimby
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: An easy class that satisfies the core writing requirement (previously writing flag, idk what they're calling it these days). Weekly assignments that can be finished quickly. She is a very understanding and accommodating professor, but lectures were quite boring and the class is not very interesting.

Avoid taking this class if you can. The majority of lectures devolve into her chatting with a few students about her politics. Constantly tries to push her own agenda, and asks loaded questions on canvas. Doesn't seem to have a very strong background in computer science and most issues discussed are generic tech issues. Lenient on late submissions.
The class is very easy but not particularly interesting. Take if you want a simple upper div CS class.

I took HDF 306 with Professor Quimby. She was very accommodating during my time in this course when it came to online vs. in-person attendance and sick days. While the concepts were certainly important, they could have been explained in 1/5th of the time. Easy class -- prepare for two simple essays total, and weekly discussions posts. You got this!

Took her for HDF340. While her lectures are politically charged, she encouraged open discussion and was very honest with her own experiences. She constantly stressed the importance of mental health days and rest. We had to do a discussion post, presentation, and occasional paper per week, very low effort class but the information was invaluable.

analysis.name: Robert Quigley
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Quigley is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable in the field of journalism, as he spent many years working as an editor and a few years as a reporter. His approach to the class is very hands-on, having groups go through the reporting process step by step. Overall, it was a fun class, and if you want to be a reporter, it will be useful!

Quigley is an amazing professor and a gem of UT. Assignments are really straightforward as long as you follow the rubric. He also invited alumni like Pulitzer winners and reporters to give unique Q&As. There is an overarching group project with a low-stakes presentation at the end, but it's easily manageable unless you're stuck with an awful group.

Had Quigley for 301F and it was a great experience! The whole class is basically step-by-step instructions of the journalistic process with a short, low-stakes presentation at the end. He also gets some very interesting and accomplished people to give guest lectures. Overall, Quigley wants the best for his students and creates a solid foundation.

For his first time teaching 301, Professor Quigley did amazing. The homework and group projects were easy to complete and content was well taught and easy to understand, especially if you have a journalism background. Quigley is funny and kind and wants the best for his students. Choose your group wisely, you'll be working with them all semester.

Quigley is by far one of the best professors I have had at UT. He keeps the class fun and light while lecturing on the core pillars of journalism. Will try to take more classes with him before I graduate.

analysis.name: Lili Qiu

review_highlights.comment: I found Lili's lectures very inspiring. It really highlighted how essential wireless is during the age of AI. The breadth of topics she covers went well beyond what I expected. Thanks to her engaging teaching, I've developed strong interest in wireless.
Lili is a fantastic professor. She is very knowledgeable, and her lectures are thought-provoking. I learned a lot from her. She is genuinely caring toward her students.

Qiu is a great professor. Her accent is definitely there, but not enough to detract from understanding (unless perhaps if you sit at the far back). Furthermore, she genuinely takes an interest in the class, promotes class discussion and participation, and makes sense of the material. She's an excellent professor.

Personally I think the prof is very generous. Like someone said she will reschedule a few lectures that she can't attend, but attendance is never mandatory so it's your choice. Also, she ended up starting the test that person mentioned at 9am instead of 8:45 and extended the test for a total of extra 75 min! I justcan't complain more about the prof

Worst professor I had in UT by far. People would regularly fail quizzes and homework. Test was insane with most people failing it. She didn't curve. Instead she gave a make up exam that was harder than the actual exam. She would go through 100 slides in one day or two if you were lucky. She was a nice person though, but the class itself was hard.

I don't even know who the "professor" was but I do know that chem lab is annoying af. Dry lab is confusing but you'll make it through, wet lab as well. I think it's pretty TA and pod dependant which sucks. You'll be fine just stay on task, theres little outside of class work, just communicate with your pod and ask the TA's questions.

i mean you'll live... probably the most annoying and boring class ever but there's no way you'll fail chem lab lmfao. just do not sign up for an 8:30 or a 4-6 it'll be the bane of ur existence (arguably it might be no matter when you have it!)

We never actually met Dr. Sotelo; everything is run by the TAs and your lab experience completely depends on what TA and lab pod you get. The work isn't hard and you get the chance to fix any worksheet mistakes for full credit. Lab makeup is a pain so attendance is basically required

analysis.name: Qiang Liu

Took ML2 Hon and was a great class. HW and exams were directly related to course content and were similar to practice problems. Lectures were good as well.

analysis.name: Quoc Nguyen

review_highlights.comment: He grades very haphazardly,and the course material is not very useful.

Nguyen is honestly the sweetest professor I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and treats us like his own kids. He's definitely one of my favorite professors ever

Dr Nguyen is truly a once in a lifetime professor who genuinely cares about his students. If he thinks you are putting in ample effort, he will be flexible about your test grades and will give points back where he can. Quoc is genuinely a good and caring professor but the class itself is very hard with the final being the hardest exam by far.

analysis.name: Emily Que

Dr. Que is extremely hard to follow in lectures. She doesn't completely work out problems and expects us to follow unfinished messy work. She jumps from topic to topic with confusing explanations, does not simplify any concepts. Tests are too long, which she acknowledges but does not change. Can only understand material by teaching yourself.

Can't even solve her own questions, even relying on students to help her. When she make mistakes (pretty often), she just smiles through it and laughs it off. Embarrassing for her honestly. Lectures are essentially pointless because she just reads off of the slides without ever explaining anything. Might as well be a biology major and take Laude.

Dr. Que is talented in her work and is very nice; however, this does not translate to her skills as a teacher. Que is the worst professor I had. First time teaching gen chem and it shows. Exams are long, heavy weight, no curve, rushed. If you lacked strong high school chem, this class is a struggle.

analysis.name: Emily Quigley
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload

review_highlights.comment: Quigley is absolutely my all time favorite professor at UT. She is one of the most kind and understanding professors here. Prof Quigley was one of the best professors I ever had. She truly cares so much about her students and helps them with everything to succeed in journalism. She was always avaliable to help. Participation is also a huge part of this class.
Professor Quigley is great. She gives great feedback and really cares about student's success. If you go to her office hours, you will get an easy A. One of my favorite professors at UT.

chose professor Quigley as your reporting words teacher. She's my favorite professor at UT by far and truly wants you to succeed. She's chill and laid back but also pushes you to be the best. She's someone you can go to for more than just class and understands reporting words is difficult so she's awesome
EQ is amazing. My writing improved so much because her feedback is so detailed. She is also a cool person overall. Labs are fun. Take her if you can!!!

analysis.name: Qixing Huang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very dry lecturer. Did not provide a syllabus and never gave out a clear grading scheme. Tons of generous extra credit (A total of 24 extra points towards our final grade). Thought a lot of complex topics were trivial and did not explain them correctly. Often brushed over topics necessary to complete assignments. Hard tests but graded generously.

Covers difficult concepts, some of which are not explained in depth. Exams are very challenging but graded leniently. Assignments are challenging, but you get 12 slip days, extra credit opportunities, and they're not graded too harshly either. Uses MATLAB which is not ideal, but u have the option for python for later assignments iirc.

Dr. Huang is a nice guy. You go through a lot of material and a bunch of math derivations in lecture. But, projects were not too hard w/ a bunch of extra credit. Exams were pretty hard but graded leniently. I think this was his first semester teaching generative visual computing, but it was pretty good.

Topics are very dense, both for good and bad. Concepts often feel somewhat overwhelming, but you will doubtlessly learn a great deal about a great deal. Exams are very rough, but graded leniently. Assignments are moderately rough, but have plenty of extra credit. Brush up on your math and be prepared for slow lectures.

Class was graded off of 6 projects and 2 exams (tons of EC tho). Exams were difficult (mostly theory that was covered in slides) but graded very leniently. Projects (choice of matlab or python) were time consuming but covered really cool topics. Lectures that didn't involve linear algebra were pretty good, but the ones that did were a struggle.

analysis.name: Thais Rutledge
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took Dr. Rutledge for RHE306, and she was amazing. I loved her. She creates an open and learning space for her students and is easily accessible. Her class has back-to-back essays, 5-7 pages, and uses around 3-5 resources, so essays are doable and easy to write! If you put in effort, she'll put in effort on you. I would take her again!

Professor Rutledge is a wonderful and caring professor. Her lectures are engaging, and she creates a comfortable environment for everyone. She is also very accessible outside of class for any questions. I would take this class again!

I had Dr. Rutledge for RHE 306. She is an amazing teacher who really cares about her students. She is very passionate about the material she teaches and is adamant about helping her students absorb it. If you put effort into this class, Dr. Rutledge will put effort back into you. I highly recommend this professor.

I had Professor Rutledge for Rhetoric of Inclusion. She was passionate about the subject and genuinely cares about her students' success. The lectures were engaging and clear, and she was always available to help outside of class. I learned so much, and I would definitely take another class with her. Highly recommend!

Professor Rutledge is amazing! I took RHE 306 and I learned so much in her class. She creates a fantastic learning environment where everyone feels comfortable sharing their ideas. Her feedback is really helpful, and she makes writing and critical thinking fun and engaging. Highly recommend her class!

analysis.name: Rohitash Rao
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I would not recommend this course, especially if you actually care about graphic design. It is easy to get an A, but the lectures are not productive. Professor Rao spends each lecture giving "feedback," but he often gets sidetracked, and the feedback is rarely constructive. You don't get any lessons on programs or software.

He offers subjective feedback to everyone in class based on his own opinions, but it can sometimes be helpful. He is a very qualified creative, but extremely disorganized as a professor. Assignment instructions and overall organization of the course changed too frequently. I got an A, but this class could be unnecessarily stressful.

Took this class thinking I would learn how to use Adobe, but I've been pretty disappointed. We have cool assignments, but he just tells us what he wants to see, without explaining how to get there. In class he just goes through everyone's submissions. I took this so I wouldn't have to learn outside of class, which is exactly what I've had to do.

Professor Rao is a really nice guy! He is a little all over the place sometimes, but that's just how creatives are sometimes. He's really smart and wants to help you succeed in the creative industry! Make sure you take his constructive feedback and use them to improve your work, he really appreciates that.

Perfect balance of easiness and wanting to rip your hair out. If you're stuck with a dormant group, good luck. BUT Rao is a very approachable person and is always down to help you with campaigns. The class overall really helps you develop your creative muscles. Attendance is required but lectures are just going over all the groups work.

analysis.name: Silvia Ramirez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: take this class! she's so sweet. the class was easy, as long as you do the homework that doesn't take long and isn't very difficult. I will say that my class was tiny so we all got more individualized feedback on how to improve, so it might be harder to manage all the random cold calls she does in a larger class. my spanish improved so much

Contrary to some reviews on here, I found her to be an amazing professor that really cares about her students and helped me improve my Spanish. Yes, it can be intimidating to be cold called but I am by no means a great Spanish speaker and I never found it to be as bad as everyone says, it actually helped me improve. Advice: always do your homework.

Profesora Ramirez can definitely be the kind of professor not many people are used to having, but personally, I enjoyed the challenge. As long as you do the homework and actively participate in class you will definitely pass. Take advantage of her office hours as she provides valuable feedback and is also an easy person to connect with.

Profesora Ramirez is a great teacher. You get what you put into the class. Participation matters and she makes you interact with other students. In turn, this makes speaking Spanish more comfortable. She is a bit stubborn with the grading but is not too bad. I would not recommend this class if you do not speak Spanish well or have never written it.

It's her way or the high-way. It doesn't matter if you're a good writer, you have to write exactly how she wants it (hint: she doesn't understand what a thesis is). She also gives 0 feedback. She never tells you what she wants then you go to her office hours and all she says is "this wasn't what I wanted." Doesn't help you improve before next paper

analysis.name: Scott Myers
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I didn't really like this guy. His lectures are pretty boring, and he is a really weird grader. He often has taken points off and I really don't get why, not clear feedback. To put it into perspective how my class probably felt, I showed for a lecture for the first time in like 3 weeks and maybe 10/45 people were actually present.

Lectures are very dense and all he does is read off his slides. He's allergic to his inbox. He's a very particular grader and his feedback is sparse. He's not very clear as to what you should focus on when exams come around. Get ready to memorize the IPA buddy.

Absolute beast of a professor. He takes complex topics and breaks it down so everyone can understand, and he teaches you exactly what you need know, so as long as you attend lecture, you won't need to consult many external resources. You will know the ins and outs of the IPA, speech acoustics, and speech perception after this class.

I enjoyed class with Myers. Homework every week and only two exams (final was second exam). He's a total dad (you'll see) and a quirky guy. Lectures were a little boring some days but he surprised us with his humor every now and then. Fair grader; if help is needed, willing to meet up outside of class. Come to class, do the work, you'll pass.

His lectures are pretty clear, full of references for you to read up on for interesting topics. He likes to teach at ungodly times, eight in the morning, so consider that. What you'll struggle with will probably be sound recognition for transcriptions. COVID-19 took our last test away, so I can't say anything about the rest of the class.

analysis.name: William Schwartz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I love love love Dr. Schwartz ! Took his UGS on circadian rhythms and honestly learned so much. He is such an amazing professor and also a very caring person. Attending lectures is crucial as his slideshows have nothing but pictures, but lectures are interesting and short.

Dr. Schwartz is a really chill prof, he learns everyone's names and makes an effort to get along with students. This class is an easy A but not a blowoff, you have to attend lectures and study in order to do well on the exams. Most of your grade goes to 3 exams so there's little room for error there, but there was no final. Definitely recommend!
This class is interesting, fun, and helpful. A great upper-div course.

Dr. Schwartz is wonderful! He learns all of his students names and tries to stay involved with their lives. Lecture heavy class that isn't recorded, so definitely attend. Very fun though. Also a good resource for a recommendation if you form a good relationship with him!!!

He is a great person but his lectures are kind of confusing/boring. We wrote 9 papers 70% <1 page, 30% longer. There were 2 quizzes and the final is a 5-minute oral presentation. He's nitpicky on grammar and the quizzes are also very detailed so make sure to actually pay attention/take notes. Interesting class got a 93 but you have to work for it.

analysis.name: Randolph Wilt
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 83 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Wilt genuinely cares about his students and is the only professor I'd recommend taking an 8 AM for! He offers plenty of extra credit to help students succeed. Exams come straight from the textbook, so studying is important, but lectures are engaging with lots of stories and real-life examples.

Dr. Wilt is extremely caring and approachable. He has tons of stories from his career and frequently references them throughout his lectures. Highly, highly recommend taking him for BA 324 or MAN 336 (I took him for BA 324). One of the most highly regarded professors at McCombs.
Professor Wilt was awesome! Every assignment criteria is very clear, and his lectures were great. He has a lot of cool experiences and tells fun stories to connect the course concepts.

Wilt is the best. He is very knowledgable. I took his class at 8 am and never struggled to stay awake. He is super engaging and his stories helped me learn the material. Exams can be weird and sometimes hard but you will be fine.

Professor Randolph is funny, caring, and easygoing. He has pretty strict policies to make sure people engage with the class, but is very nice and understanding. He himself does not grade very hard, but the TAs are very picky. Make sure to study extremely hard for the tests, because they can make or break your grade. Overall, I recommend him.

analysis.name: Rabun Taylor
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Would STRONGLY advise to run in the opposite direction if this man is your instructor. EXTREMELY tough grader. Doesn't specify he wants from you and then rips your grade to shreds. He's very quiet and only presents boring lectures. Lots of tests. No mercy shown. God forbid you don't know absolutely everything. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS

Originally I wasn't supposed to have Dr. Taylor as a professor for this course, and I regret not dropping it when I realized he had been switched to the class. He's friendly enough, but his lectures are hard not to sleep through, and his grading is ridiculous (and on few things). Especially if you are a STEM major I do not suggest him as a prof.

Professor Taylor was very caring but didn't provide much in terms of teaching. All your "learning" is through reading a dense textbook. Lectures were lengthy & unengaging. Tests were FRQ w easy "recall info" questions & essay questions; you can pick up points on the essay as long as you can back up your argument. Overall doable but painful at times

I wanted to learn Latin because I thought it would be fun (learned quickly that it would not be fun lol) This professor's lectures were always off topic and incoherent. I was left teaching myself (the TA helped ALOT!) If you take this class make sure you have enough built-in study time!! And read chapters before class! Latin can be really tough.

Dr. Taylor is a very caring professor, and you can tell he truly cares about what his students. The content itself was interesting, but the lectures were quite long and boring. Assignments are graded harshly with little room for error, and exams requiring pulling very specific elements off lecture slides. Nice guy but wouldn't recommend class.

analysis.name: Alfred Tuley
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: this semester's setup felt less organized. Graded instapolls for attendance and weekly quizzes. Lectures felt inconsistent and missed some key fundamentals, so they weren't very helpful. I'd rely more on student hub resources and use lectures as practice. Overall, I wish the setup hadn't changed.

His class is super chill & he's really funny. I would mention that he does tend to skim through topics and talk about it kinda vaguely. Most of your learning needed to pass the class and test is based off of the resources in canvas, not his lectures. quiz every week, tests are a little hard but with use of resources its easy. tons of extra credit.

Best professor at UT so far. He makes chemistry accessible to all. Highly recommend his office hours to get advice for quizzes and exams. He offers so many resources from himself and the chem dept. He is funny, caring, and devoted to his students. Studying lectures, quizzes, learning modules, and practice problems/exams are all necessary.

The class is not that difficult, and it can be interesting if you pay attention and put effort into the class. There are many resources provided to help learn and review for exams, which are very easy if you do them. Dr. Tuley explains concepts well in lecture and is very friendly. This class is very easy to do well in if you put in the effort.

He's an overall good professor and does care about his students knowing the material, but the class does get difficult in acids and bases. This is a unit that is in general already hard, but he's not the best at breaking down so self study a LOTTT before this exam. Prepare well for weekly quizzes. He offers lots of extra credit and 2 retakes.

analysis.name: Talitha Leflouria
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor LeFlouria was wonderful, and the class is fairly easy and informative. Prof LeFlouria does take a bit to get back with you on grading which can make it difficult to understand what she wants from you, but is overall helpful and knowledgeable.

Professor LeFlouria is amazing! I've taken both of her HIS365g courses and she has been wonderful both times! She approaches the topic she teaches in such a way where she's able to help explain both the gravity of the situation and make sure that she isn't overwhelming us at the same time. She really cares for her students!

The class is discussion-based so be prepared to participate and make sure to do the weekly readings. Other than that, just one presentation and one (relatively short) research term paper/end-of-semester project. You'll learn a lot about parts of US history that aren't taught elsewhere and gain hands-on research skills. Excellent professor!

Professor LeFlouria is great, she's really fun and sweet and clearly knows so much about the topic. This class is not hard at all, I have gotten a 100 on every assignment so far, but I do feel like I'm learning a lot. She teaches about things I would never have learned about in other history classes. Would definitely recommend.

She is a kind and inspiring professor, I talked to her a couple of times after class and she was always ready to answer my questions. You don't have to participate if you don't want to but it sure helps. Overall this was my favorite class this semester and I believe I learned a lot from it. Would 100% Recommend

analysis.name: Ann Thijs
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 138 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lecture and homework seemed so easy but the passing rate for each test was always super low! Tests were not an accurate representation of what was taught in lecture which makes it completely hard to perform well. I learn a great deal but did not get a complementary grade for all of the work I put in.

The wording on her tests is extremely difficult to understand. Everyone had to ask what the questions meant during the tests. I wish I wouldn't have taken her class. Also in class participation is 75% accuracy, so getting a one hundred is gonna be some work.

Dr. Thijs is a nice person but shes not a good lecturer. She fumbles her words, says um a lot, her sentences are incomplete because she pauses between words, and she goes through the powerpoints too fast. She was disappointed with our exam average and blamed it on us for not trying harder instead of asking what she was doing wrong.

Dont listen to bad reviews. This is a flipped classroom so a lot of the content is self-taught but I was used to that from my BIO311C class I took with another instructor. Literally just put in the hard work and pay attention and study and this class is a breeze. TAs were super helpful. Dr. Thijs is very nice and attentive to her students.

Very organized and fair if you put in effort. Flipped class where class is spent on Instapolls (free points) where she goes over every answer. Lots of small assignments and exams are similar to practice questions. Dr. Thijs is a great professor who cares about her students. Highly recommend both the class and her as a professor.

analysis.name: Sean Upshaw
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: extremely kind and easygoing. Class is pretty informational and interesting despite the fact I'm not a med student. Class is super easy, about 2 essays + 1 one-minute vlog a month. Attendance is optional but i would highly recommend to go his class, its already a small class and he puts a lot of effort into teaching. Overall amazing prof

Super kind, positive, and laid back guy! If you're not great with computer stuff the assignments can be a little hard, but he's such a chill grader that you just have to focus on getting them turned in on time. He's also very understanding if you email him about certain circumstances. Very glad I took this class with Upshaw, highly recommend.

guys trust, take this class. Professor Upshaw is super kind and this class is genuinely the most enjoyable class I've ever taken. The work is very simple and just follow the tutorials in the textbook and that's it. The books have videos embedded so actual reading is minimal. Pretty self paced but you do have to manage your time.
Very kind. He grades easy and has interesting material. Would take his class again.

For ADV 378: Shawn facilitated so many great discussions and had awesome guest lectures and I learned so much about Black advertising. Most lectures were straight from book material which was sometimes hard to focus on, but I feel like the greatest part of this course was the in-class conversations. He was so kind and truly cared about the course.

analysis.name: Delgerjargal Uvsh
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Gives brief and clear lectures, gives criteria for assignments (which there are not many of). My main problem is that she assigns a LOT of readings before class, and you have to know their contents because she'll give you a bluebook summary quiz over them for attendance sometimes. She makes attendance a big deal. Great class overall, though.

I took Dr. Uvsh's UGS about corruption. From the start, the rubric for the class was clear and grading was very chill. There are readings weekly but you lowkey don't *have* to do them to do well 😅. Overall, Dr. Uvsh is very nice and lectures are informative and relevant. She also responds to emails quickly. The TA, Vahan, was also great.

She was a super sweet professor who was always available for questions. She gave you a lot of creative freedom which I appreciated and allowed you to research what you were interested in. There was only one mid-term and it was super fair. Additionally the TA was super sweet and helpful. Overall she was a great professor.

Assigned a lot of readings, can do perfectly fine without doing them. Took feedback mid-semester and immediately applied it, reduced readings. Midterm exam was easy, have access to all slides and notes. Great class for the UGS credit and easy A.
There were a lot of readings but not super necessary to do. The only exam is open note, open PowerPoint. Most things can be completed pretty quickly, and she is flexible with deadlines.

analysis.name: Thomas Underwood
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super awesome guy, very easy to understand, presents material in a great way. Exams are solid, no curve balls. Homeworks are a bit time-consuming most of the time, but other than that - no complaints.

Underwood is a great lecturer and helps one understand the big picture well... however all I learned IS the big picture. Not much time is spent on the specifics, which hurt when doing graded HWs. TAs are helpful but can sometimes be lost as well. Tests are hard but are graded generously. All in all, with lots of  effort, a good grade is possible
Amazing lecturer - low-speed may be challenging and a lot of work, and he not only makes the subject approachable, but also very interesting.
Great professor. I enjoyed his class a lot and he taught complicated material extremely well.

Perfect lectures. Fair assignments that were difficult enough to learn material but were far from overwhelming. Highly flexible. Available outside of class to an extent that went above the norm and beyond expectations. Proud UT engineering has this quality of professors.

analysis.name: Ulrich Mueller
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Mueller is such a nice professor! Exams are based on lecture and are relatively straight forward. Attendance isn't mandatory but all the exam content is from the lectures so it helps to go. He offers lecture outlines and practice exams. He really wants to help your grade, so I def recommend him! Discussions are chill as long as you talk once.

love dr. mueller. he outlined everything on the exams early and was receptive to feedback. he truly cares about students as it showed he wanted us to succeed. his exams are not hard as long as you study. evolution is def a very interesting topics as is my fav class at ut so far. his exams gave cushion and room to do bad on the quizzes later.

Dr. Mueller is a great professor and truly wants to help you learn. We had two exams in the first half of the class. Study the lecture handouts because all the answers you need are there. Attendance is mandatory for discussion, but show up because it will help your grade. I recommend taking Mueller & Mats for INB 370!

His lectures were very straightforward. He provided a real-life example of almost every concept he taught. He provides a lecture outline that is where 90% of the test questions come from. Discussion is mandatory, but it helps with the reading questions on the test. There are only two grades for this half of the semester, and they are two exams.

Amazing professor! Attendance is not required for lecture, but is required for discussion. Exams are very very easy with multiple choice questions and True/False. He gives out lecture outlines and as long as you study those (know them by heart), you should get an A in his portion of evolution.

analysis.name: Luis Urrieta
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is strange. Required to go off campus for field studies as well as you have autonomy to create your own field study, which can turn out to be  annoying as it is highly time consuming at times. You have to go to every class, sick or not in order to do well in this class as well as he isn't very available outside of class. Glad its over!!

Qualitative Inquiry into Education for Social Change; Professor Urrietta was a fantastic lecturer and discussion facilitator. You have to attend class and participate, but I found the course content very interesting and easy to engage with. He gives you autonomy in defining your field observation project which can turn out to be a lot of fun!

Took this as a 5 week summer class and it was A LOT. So much reading! 7 papers due. 10 volunteer hours & 2 outdoor walks in 100+ degrees. Miserable. Lecture heavy with mandatory participation. Learned a lot but felt as if there was an agenda being pushed. Glad it's over.

analysis.name: Arban Uka
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Inspirational the right word to describe him. He makes students wanna do something more with their life. Amazing lecturers definitely yes. He always brings up interesting facts + engages students to give their opinion, even if the topic is not that hot (like differential equations). Would take again though I've graduated.

very smart and hardworking. very fair evaluation. always ready to help students. a bit messy and always busy (cause he finds time for everyone). kind and polite to extreme. sometimes hard to follow his genius track of thoughts :( . Still among best profs ive ever had
He details the math step by step, always.

analysis.name: Jason Urban
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Jason gives great feedback and is a fair grader. You can tell that he takes his work seriously and is truly passionate about what he does. I cannot recommend his class enough!

He is great! He gives really specific and helpful feedback to everyones work, and built a polite atmosphere in the online classroom. The class critique process is always so fun and helpful, and I have produce a lot of works Im proud with for my portfolio. Although the workload I can be a bit overwhelming sometimes, but all projects are fun.

I cannot stress enough how much I loved taking a litho class with Jason, he explained everything clearly and gave thorough demos. He does expect you to have good attendance and to actually work during class but it's worth it in order to understand everything that's taught. Definitely take a print class with him if you can!

He is one of the best professor I ever had! He is Inspirational, reasonable, friendly, caring, approachable, and very helpful. He always give clear guidelines when introducing projects. During discussions, he give you comments that can make you go further and want to go further.
nice funny smart cool guy. would recommend. Advice: don't be slovenly.

analysis.name: Victoria Davis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Davis has been the best professor I have had at UT. Shecares about her students and gives them as much help as possible. She grades harshly, but the rubrics are clear, and she allows drafts to receive feedback before the final, graded submission. She gives out simple extra credit assignments. The class is interactive/focused on collaboration.

Dr. Davis is so sweet and bubbly, and she really cares about each student. There are lots of assignments but they're all relatively easy and she's a reasonable grader. This is a pretty boring busywork class but she does a good job of still making it enjoyable and interactive. I would absolutely take her as a professor again.

Very good teacher. Grades harshly, but realistically. Offers extra credit and opportunities to make up for missed work. Will definitely help you improve your communication (both written and verbal), without tanking your grade unnecessarily. Is hard to get an A, though.

analysis.name: Vincent Viviani
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had in this school. Funny, friendly, energetic, kind, and helpful. Very straightforward rubric after standardization. All learning objectives are given and explained before exams, even if you didn't learn anything well, the supporting materials are great to help you out. Also gave bonus at the end of semester.

Very funny guy, and the accent isn't bad. Exams are extremely easy; there is no final. The one quiz per unit is also very easy. Easily the best gen chem 1 professor right now, since most other professors have quizzes every class. I showed up only for tests, since the material on Canvas is enough to learn. However, Prof. Viviani is a great lecturer.

Great professor! I must admit I fell asleep during most lectures (but still ended with an A!) Either way he is really funny and does cool experiments - plus generous with extra credit (+3% to your overall ending grade!). Gen chem 1 is light and taking it with Vivani is chill

Lectures are great and there are tons of review resources for the tests, including practice tests that are almost the exact same as the actual test. He's also super funny and does a bunch of experiments in the class. Definitely recommend him for gen chem 1!!!!

I took his class for both chem 1 and 2 and he was amazing even as the material was hard at times. He's extremely kind and funny. He only has 2 quizzes per unit and gives extra credit towards the end. He really cares for his students so during lectures, please listen to him, it makes me so sad to see ppl talking over him sometimes. My goat fr

analysis.name: Gustavo De Veciana
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Hes nice and the canvas was organized and had good resources, but my lord is it just impossible to learn from the slides. Probability is an math heavy class, and the lecture slides were just impossible to learn from. I have no doubt it would've been a much better lecture environment if he wrote notes on the board. I attended 90% of lectures.

Not a bad person, but found it hard to follow in lectures. Exams were alright and curved very fairly. There is a lot of homework, but it helped to study for exams and such. There is an alarming amount of people that receive a C at the end of the semester but overall not a bad class.

Dr. DeVeciana was an incredible professor! He makes a clear effort to know everyone and involve them to participate in class. His lectures are amazing, and you can build your number sense and intuition throughout the course. Tests are heavy but they follow past exams closely, and you only need a 90 to get an A in his class so that's pretty sweet!

I absolutely love De Veciana. He had the best lectures of any professor I have ever had. He is concise and does a lot of examples in class. His tests were extremely fair (not easy, but if you put in the work you'll get an A). The only cons are that he wasn't too helpful in office hours and he made the final stupid hard because grades were too good.

EE 351K with De Veciana is honestly a lot easier than with other professors, from what I heard from friends who had taken the class for the second time. EE 351K builds upon itself, so you'll NEED to build up a strong foundation in the early weeks. That said, it's a straightforward class once you understand the homeworks and the slides.

analysis.name: Vijay Garg
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are somewhat rigid, but it's because he has been doing this for so many years. He doesn't assign many things, but when he does it will usually be really hard (but he gives you a couple weeks to do it). His exams aren't too difficult if you understand what's going on. Read the book, because it's what he lectures from (and he wrote it).
Superficial lectures that make no sense, have to learn everything yourself in order to do the assignments.

The course provides important materials in software engineering, but taking this class is basically no different than studying by yourself with a textbook. If you registered for this course already, oh your next semester is not looking good.

So quiet it's difficult to understand him. 
No answers to practice problems in the textbook he wrote. 
No testing files for coding labs.

Physics is just a difficult subject. Regardless, he tries to make the lectures interesting with the use of cool demos. In general, he's a very nice guy and an awesome professor.
