Reading the book and doing the HW's are a must, his lectures really clear up misconceptions. Pretty funny guy too. Open to questions about grades too. Great prof.
Professor Zhen Yao is an amazing teacher. I love his teaching style - It is entertaining, and at the same time very informative.

Let me start off by saying I suck at Physics but the way the class was set up was nice because homework (quest) is only due once a week other physics classes have homework due twice a week. This caused me not to stay too behind. Attendace is kinda mandatory to take clicker quizes and at the end of the semester Yao curved, I passed bless you yao

analysis.name: Zoe Mantarakis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Beginning yoga is honestly not for pure beginners. She does NOT really explain or demonstrate the poses and the proper way to do them, which can be really confusing and even dangerous if you have actual zero prior yoga experience. Also kind of patronizing and self-serving sometimes with how she talked about herself and her accomplishments/training.
Professor Zoe is an incredibly kind and knowledgeable professor and is always willing to make accommodations. Grading is very easy as long as you do the yoga lectures. Overall very fun and engaging!

I did the web-based class so I did 2 45-minute lessons a week and recorded myself. Some weeks have a "meditation challenge" or other challenge. Midterm and final are not hard, and you can create something not just a written submission. She has flexibility with due dates. There are some extra credit options at the end or come in person for a makeup.

You could opt to go in-person or stay online to do the coursework. If you ever turned in something late or never submitted your assignment, just go to the in-person classes to get your credit back. She's kind of strict about the nature of yoga, so make sure to memorize all of the written portion of the limbs of yoga, niyamas, and yamas of a yogi.

Took intermediate yoga with her as someone that has prior experience of learning and teaching yoga. She doesn't do a very good job of explaining complicated poses and how to do them CAREFULLY. We had a class of 50 students kicking into headstands against a wall, which can be so so dangerous. She rarely provides modifications for harder poses too.

analysis.name: Bill Young
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 204 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: he is genuinely the worst professor ive taken. he only have you learn off of videos and blames the student for scoring low. DO NOT TAKE

This class was disorganized and unaccommodating for the pandemic and winter storm. The examples the professor provides are far more basic than the ones used in homeworks, practice problems, quizzes, and exams. The examples are copied from the textbook. The TAs and professor also exhibit a snarky attitude when you are confused about a concept.

Awful and frustrating class. I'm constantly drowning in assignments. HW after HW... His teaching style is awful - lecture slides are pretty much useless and exams test on a lot more than what is covered in his lecture videos. He stopped allowing cheat sheets on exams which is now making this class unbearable. And his attitude is condescending.

Dr. Young puts in effort, but the course structure is flawed. Weekly in-person classes feel like a waste, they are just practice problems better done alone. Worksheets and mock exams are labeled optional but are essential. Exams test formatting quirks and niche Python facts, not real coding skill. Unrealistic expectations for practical coding.
Take this class and be depressed for the semester.

analysis.name: Zachary Miner
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 96 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is the BEST calc professor you will ever have! M408C is not an easy class, so be prepared to put in work, but Dr. Miner explains things clearly, uses lots of examples, and cares a lot about his students' success. The class is organized well, so you can build on knowledge and actually understand the material, rather than just formulas.

I think people who haven't taken Calc BC would find this class pretty difficult. Lectures focused on the proofs for the different tests/techniques, which didn't help much in solving problems. Homework is also pretty long and time-consuming. However, the quizzes/tests are very easy if you do the homework. He is very helpful during office hours too.

Miner is a great and caring professor. This course satisfies the IBL requirement, so set your expectations accordingly. I found Dr. Miner to be a great help in learning to write better proofs and tackling non-obvious problems. Exams felt scary in the moment, but applying problem solving techniques learned in class are enough to solve them well.

I had all As throughout college before this class, it's SO hard. He grades exams super rough, and they're always really hard. Class is just students presenting their homework from the night before, so not helpful at all. Miner is super nice and will help you in office hours. He's a great guy, but take someone else who actually teaches.

Homework took me a while. Did not enjoy the IBL format as much as I thought I would. Great guy and accessible. Course majorly lacks feedback for a proof writing course. If you're going to pay to take this course just take it with someone who teaches it. Number theory is not a class you want to teach yourself.

analysis.name: Min Zhong
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 146 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Do NOT take her class and if you HAVE to, be prepared to put in 20+ hours of work per week. I studied for 50 hours over the course of two weeks for her exam and had no idea what the material was when I took the exam. She has 3-5 assignments per week and they all take 2-5 hours each. Please start studying for Bio 2 over Christmas break.

She is a caring professor and really sweet. She publishes a large amount of homework every week. Her tests are multiple choice and FRQs. For homework, you have to use the textbook specially for RGAs. At one point, every time I tried to study, I wanted to rip my hair out due to the questions being unpredictable sometimes.

have never in my life been more fearful of failing a class. There is tons of homework weekly and lots of weekly studying. The exams questions are so specific that its nearly impossible to study for. It's hard to get a lot out of her lectures because they are very hard to follow along and sometimes her accent makes it hard to understand. Don't take

Y'all I genuinely don't even know where to start. There are so so many paper handouts given in class that hardly relate to the content being taught that day if at all. The next unit in the class is typically began before we even take the exam for the prior unit. In class quizzes are basically mini exams, homework is HEAVY and graded insanely harsh.

She is like a toxic ex, she is SO nice and even gave us candy the Monday after Halloween but she seriously cannot teach and got mad at us for being honest in her feedback survey. What she teaches and assigns does not properly prepare you for the heavily weighted exams and she rarely gives practice exams. Depends too heavily on self-study. STAY AWAY

analysis.name: Pilar Zazueta
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor gives a study guide which includes questions that may be on the quizzes, yet grades you on a criteria that isn't given to you during or before the quiz. Quiz comments afterwards reference the specific things you were missing (that were not asked of), which you of course, lose points for. Boring lectures, participation is graded.
Genuinely grades everything too tough, not sure if anything would satisfy her. Also weirdly passive aggressive? Exams are annoying to prepare for, doable but her grading is over specific.

she is very nice and cares about students, weekly readings are easy and straightforward. We did do a couple presentations but they werent hard. Do have to do a 8-10 page essay end of the year. Overall easy class.

This class was easy and most assignments could be completely quickly as well. Lectures however might be the most boring I've ever had before. She sorta mumbles everything so even when you attempt to pay attention, it all goes through your head anyways. All depends on how nice your TA is, but every grade I recieved was generous or reasonable

lectures were god awful and boring. Make sure you do all assignments which takes up literally 20 min of ur time each week, theyre also easy af. attendance mandatory but only 40% show up.Easy class just know final is in person essay :/ and professor is just bad at lecturing. she does not know how to word things in a way that people can understand

analysis.name: Acacia Chan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Chan is amazing, could not recommend more. Very welcoming discussion space, very fair grading, and easy, enjoyable projects. She gives you the chance to revise and resubmit your projects once graded, and if you miss class, you can make it up by sending in a paragraph after watching the Zoom. Super reachable online for any questions, too.
Most fun I've ever had in a class

Ms. Chan is the sweetest and most kind professor I've had at UT. Attendance is mandatory, but her lectures are engaging and interesting. Her only downfall is her grading, she didn't grade 80% of our work until the day before grades were due which was very frustrating. Very sweet, and lax on extensions though, loved being in her class.

analysis.name: Rebecca A. Zarate (RAZ)
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Extremely easy, one open-note benchmark quiz per class determines the majority of your grade. The course is interesting and engaging, but sleep is more interesting and engaging, so that's what I did during the lectures.

I cannot recommend RAZ enough. One of the best professors I have had at UT. She was excellent at explaining coding concepts and her office hours are extremely helpful. So much material offered for the class and she is very understanding with questions.

Best teacher I think I had at UT Austin. Made me seriously consider statistics as a career path. Don't worry if you don't know anything before the class, Zarate is easy to talk to & she gives great advice. If you put some effort/interest in the course, you will get a good grade!

Super in depth lecturer. Classes technically didn't have attendance taken but all the work we did was in class based, practically no outside work necessary. As long as she sees that you are trying you will get a good grade if you put the work in. Highly recomend

She was my course coordinator, and is very energetic in lectures as well as very accessible outside of class. A lot of times, her email reminders were the reason I was submitting assignments on time. I'm sure any course she teaches would be a great time.

analysis.name: Renee Acosta
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I'm being so serious, as a STEM major, I think this is the best class/professor I've had and will remain that way for my foreseeable academic career. Real-world applicability of knowledge, genuinely easy to learn and helpful knowledge that can improve many life circumstances, and best of all, the field trips and overall genuine class culture!

If you need a UGS class, TAKE THIS ONE, IT'S THE EASIEST AND BEST ONE. Most of the grade is just attendance. We had field trips and talked about medicine, which ended up being really helpful information when flu season came around. My friend was jealous I was in this class compared to her UGS, cause it's just that easy.

The easiest class I took all semester. I got a lot of good information though, and it was nice to check in on our well-being throughout the semester. The class was VERY relaxed, and there aren't exams, so paying attention is fun but optional. Attendance is mandatory though, but it's not hard to get motivation to go because it's a fun class.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Prof Acosta is super nice, she cares about her students, she's lenient on due dates and she's a good teacher. There are easy weekly readings/discussion posts from a book she provides, 2 papers, and some easy projects. We also went on field trips around campus and she ends class early. The material is interesting too. A PERFECT UGS.

Dean Acosta is one of the best professors that I have ever had. She is extremely caring and genuinely cares if you are struggling or not and will do her best to help you. The semester is super fun and filled with museum trips, pilates and cycling classes, and very interesting lectures. She is an extremely accomplished and real person and is great!!

analysis.name: Daniel Ackerberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best econometrics prof at UT. His lectures are clear and easy to follow. If you go to class, he goes out of his way to help you with quizzes and exams. Exams are also only 30% of your course grade, and he writes easier exams than the other professors. He also gives great practice exams and hints. Take him!

One of the few good Econ profs at UT. He does really well to go over examples and explain the material during his lectures to where anyone can understand it. Genuinely wants you to do well. Tests are similar to practice exams he posts but a little harder. Maybe it was because I took this with 420s, but this was a cakewalk compared to that class
Professor Ackerberg has a great style of teaching, and makes econometrics easy and enjoyable. If you attend class, he will give you hints for quizzes and exams.

Great Professor, very good at breaking down economic principles that were previously hard for me. Only 2 exams, but if you study the lecture notes and quizzes, you're good to go. Go to his office hours before exams to help with key concepts. Papers are straightforward with clear grading, just follow the rubric, and you'll get an A. Best Econ class!

He does a great job of slowing and simplifying the material. He recaps the previous class and reiterates important parts. Upbeat and wants you to succeed! One homework assignment for a completion grade a week, and quizzes on Thursday (can take from home but tells answers in class often). Class gets curved at the end. Take him!

analysis.name: Abhay Samant
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Made this class trivially easy, might be the easiest class I've taken since elementary school, and yet I still did learn a little bit from the class. Probably not worth it if you really want to come out of the course with new development skills, but some interesting topics were lightly touched on. Nice professor all around, was very considerate.

Took this class online over summer. Course seemed very disorganized as assignments were randomly assigned and for exams we had no clue what would be on them. The content of the course is not hard but it was taught in a very un-structured way. With that being said, he made the final take home and was very lenient with grade cutoffs.

Course is a little disorganized but not hard to get around. Concepts were taught pretty clearly. Even though his lectures can be dry, he is genuinely a great guy to talk to outside of class and clearly cares about his work and students. Workload is very very manageable.

My class was Abhay's first semester teaching here at UT (or anywhere for that matter), and he did a great job. His style of teaching can move fast for people who are new to programming, but if you ask he will steer you to some areas for practice that really helps. He teaches through doing, not just lectures, so you will code most days of class.
He should be more prepared for his lecture material and homework guidelines. Lots of technical difficulties in class and unnecessary breakdowns.

analysis.name: Peter Abrami
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: his 2D class is mostly photography, drawing and maybe painting if you choose that for the last project. I sort of hoped for more exploration but it was still a fun class and Peter is a good teacher

My class was large, so that may have played a role, but individual feedback was limited mostly to a few sentences during critique. The amount of outside classwork was enormous, little time was given for each project considering the level of development he expected. I didn't find that the course improved my art or process noticeably, but it was fun.

I took core drawing with Peter, and I really enjoyed his teaching and feedback during critique. If youre taking drawing, the class is very basic in format and work. The prompts can be fun, and he normally lets you work pretty freely with composition and material. Attendance matters! If youre late or absent, expect to see a change in your grade!

While I had to take this as a required studio class, it was really great to go over the basics again. Peter pushes students to do their best, no matter what their skill set is. Really great guy and helps you get a firmer grasp of the basics while pushing you with skills you've already developed.

analysis.name: Charity-Joy Acchiardo

review_highlights.comment: I thought the class was fine. The Kahoots are a little annoying at the beginning, but you get used to them as the semester progresses. Exams aren't too difficult... just read the textbook and go over the inquisitives (homework assignments). Lectures are solid as well.

Her class was not that difficult, but she is pretty unprofessional and often says weirdly inappropriate things in class. I'm glad it was online, because dealing with her in person would not be pleasant. It wasn't even really pleasant online tbh. The class is ok, but I would recommend finding another section or professor to enroll in.
Some assignments took me a long time but the tests were an accurate reflection of them. Just study and you'll pass with ease.
She is completely inaccessible. I tried many times to get ahold of her through email and she never responded.  Really disappointing class experience.

Fun&Silly class. I had 2 professors: Mateer and Acciardo. The textbook doesn't worth purchasing because contains a bunch of specific examples. Class participation: kahoots & puzzlers. Homework: InQuizitives. 2 open book\note Exams(50 points each).Office Hours: case solutions with minimum explanations. If u rn't familiar with ECO, it will be tough.

analysis.name: Abena Osseo-Asare
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Osseo-Asare is one the best profs I've ever had. She truly engages with students, is curious to hear what we think, gives valuable feedback, and let's the lectures and discussions drift and take on a natural rhythm. She's also insanely smart! We only really have one big assignment for the semester, so it's low pressure. Highly recommend!

Overall great teacher! She is very passionate about medical related history, focusing mainly on maternal health and natural/herbal remedies. If I could, I would take this class and any other class she teaches again. Do not be deterred by the amount of reading and papers, it is definitely manageable.  You will not regret taking her!

She was super chill. One of the best professors I've had I think. Grades were based on a paragraph of feedback for readings (about 8-10), a sewing project (completion), and a final paper. Real easy course. Sometimes lectures go off track and a bunch of random things were added in there (like films she found) so the class was really laid back.

She is one of the best professors ever. She's extremely educated as a medical historian and encourages students to ask tough questions. She cracks jokes in class, but also makes sure students know when to get serious. Her lectures are always really well structured and interesting. Go to class and pay attention and you'll do well.

Dr. Osseo-Asare is an incredibly kind and passionate professor. She is very in tune with what student's go through and is always willing to listen and help. As long as you show up and participate, you will do well in this class. I have taken two of her courses and they have been some of my favorites at UT

analysis.name: Abhijit Mishra
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took his Applied ML with Python class and it's basically a intro to ML class. He has clear grading policies and assignments listed in his syllabus. A little lecture heavy but overall a caring professor if you participate and ask questions. Highly recommend his classes!! High quality and good material.

When I took the intro class with him, it was a lot of information to digest at first if you're new to this field but it gives you a really good overview of data science. He really does care about his students and one of my favorite professors (took all his classes).

I've take Dr. Mishra's Introduction to Human-Centered Data Science, which was very beginner friendly and well-structured. Additionally, I've conducted academic research related to Machine Learning, both for credit and independently to gain hands-on experience with him. Dr. Mishra genuinely cares about his students' learning and development.

I've taken Dr. Mishra's introductory course, which was incredibly beginner-friendly and well-structured. I've also conducted academic research related to Machine Learning, both for credit and independently to gain experience with him. It is very noticeable that Dr. Mishra genuinely cares about his students' learning and development.

Dr. Mishra's courses are the best you could take for the Data Science track in Informatics. Lectures are structured well, and he makes sure all of his students understand the material before moving on. His labs are always well structured - connecting class material to real-world applications & assignments are related to what we learned! Highly rec!

analysis.name: Sarah Abraham
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There is a lot of work for this class, but compared to other elective courses, this is by far the easiest. Just showing up to class is almost enough to get an A. Hope you get a good group for the projects so you're not stuck picking up other people's tasks. Final project was fun. Bad communicator, though, as I never got a single email answered.

Lectures covered content that wasn't entirely useful/beneficial for students.  Mandatory attendance through Instapoll. Overall just not a very engaging class.  Coding assignments were pretty fun and the group project is the highlight of the course, but beyond that, I did not really learn much or apply many concepts from class into the project.

Abraham requires attendance with daily quizzes at the start of class. Lecture felt useless, most of my understanding of the material came from self-study and other resources. Projects are brutal but graded leniently. There is an absurd amount of homework (does she think this is a core class lol). Absolutely do not take unless you love graphics.

Dr. Abraham was an okay professor. Her lectures were boring and unhelpful even though attendance was mandatory, making the hands-on activities and assignments difficult. There is a "hands-on" or homework activity due before every single class. She also takes a long time to respond to emails. Her class was "easy," but I didn't learn much from it.

Starts off pretty easy, but the lectures become less helpful as material gets more in depth. The daily "hands on" assignments become more difficult as less is covered, and you'll end up learning from online resources instead of lecture. Processing can be fun, but me and others were lost halfway through the semester. Dr. Abraham is great though!

analysis.name: Abimbola Adelakun
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: VAPAs are required in our core to encourage us to respect and appreciate the arts. This class did the exact opposite. I have never been so turned off to theater in my life. The lectures are boring, Adelakun is difficult to understand, my TA was a really tough grader, the work load outside of class is extensive. Do not take this course.

Her thick accent makes lectures very hard to understand. She teaches as if her students are in kindergarten (she kicked a student out of class for being on his phone). Everything about this class was so unnecessary and TAs' grading was very subjective.  All major assignments were due at the end of the semester leaving no time recover GPA. THE WORST

Professor Adelakun's lectures were very engaging and interactive. 
You'll  get to learn what you are interested in in addition to the basics. It's more than a language class because we learn so much about Yoruba culture as well. If you don't have a background in Yoruba, you may have to work a little harder but it's worth it!

Professor is understanding but grades a bit tough... Unorganized canvas page as well. Overall, she seems nice and understanding, but she focuses too much on the detail of assignments and is a tough grader in my opinion.

Definitely recommend this class. extra credit opportunities and opportunity to watch plays . Interesting readings too. Don't be misled by the bad reviews. just like every other class, you've got to put in some work. with extra credit opportunities, getting an A is quite easy. listen well and you will able to understand her accent.

analysis.name: Abi Maddox
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is one of the easiest MIS electives you can take. Professor Maddox was super nice, and you can tell she really cares about the topic of health IT. While the class is easy and not a lot of work, I did learn some new things from the lectures. No exams, just online quizzes, homework assignments, and group projects. Take this class!

Professor Maddox is one of the most caring professors I have had. She teaches a very interesting course and is passionate about her students learning. I would highly recommend taking her class. I learned a lot about health IT.

Health IT was one of the easiest classes at UT. The answers for the weekly quizzes were all found in the PowerPoints. The project at the end of the semester was very easy. The labs were just following and copying basic instructions.

Professor Maddox is very knowledgeable about everything in the Health IT field, and she conveys that expertise in a way that is easy to understand. She makes the class fun, and she provides a number of labs which give hands-on experience with prominent technologies in the field. It was a fun course, and I would definitely recommend it!

analysis.name: Jason Abrevaya
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class has gotten SIGNIFICANTLY HARDER since he last taught it in 2021. The exam averages in '23 were around 62% for the whole class. The practice exams from 2021 did not help at all since they were a piece of cake while the exams this year felt like a slaughterhouse. He's a nice guy but when the whole class does poorly, maybe he's the problem.

The exams are different than his lectures and he uses multiple choice questions a lot in his exams. I am normally an A student but I didn't do well in his class but he curved everything. 

The second midterm was unbelievable difficult and different than anything we've seen. It's not even part of the practice problems he handed before the exam

Just like another reviewer said, his rating is way overrated and overhyped. He really struggles to explain things in a simple way and we spend 1/3 of the class doing stuff that won't be in the exams. He makes a lot of mistakes on his exams (there were 6 mistakes on the final). The only good thing about him is that he replies fast to emails.

He is a good teacher, although the subject can get a little complicated at times because of all the variables, but the sample problems really prepare you for the exam. He wrote the textbook himself so he knows his stuff and tries to keep it engaging. Easy A, graded by mean score and standard deviations of the class so stay above average and ur good
Very straightforward class. Massive curve as long as you stay above the class averages on tests (which are like a 60%). Pretty easy A imo as there is alot of room for error.

analysis.name: Abhra Sarkar
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I was not very engaged with the lectures themselves; I found them to be sort of boring. The homework was graded very harshly. There are weekly labs that you do with a group, which are pretty easy, but there is coding involved. The final project was also very straightforward, and I liked that you didn't have to present it.

I loved Dr Sarkar. His lectures are dry, yes, but he always makes sure everyone understands and always welcomes questions. This was my first stats class so I was lost at first, but his class allowed me to catch on pretty quickly. Quizzes are open note and very manageable with very straightforward questions that if you prepare for, you do fine.

Dr. Sarkar is funny and tries to make this class palatable, but lectures are still very, VERY dry. Quizzes are open-note (1 drop, too), and labs are pretty easy. I would take him again solely because (unlike other profs) he doesn't make you present the final poster in person (3 hours of work and printing reduced to a 2-min presentation recording).

Lectures were really dry and difficult to understand. I stopped going to class and just read the slides and doing in class work on my own and I did just fine. Don't underestimate the quizzes they are difficult with few questions, most being weighted at least 10%. Lab sections are easy coding with helpful TAs. HW graded harshly, show all work

This class is very straightforward. "Labs" are basically discussion sections where you practice running code w a group. HWs are graded harshly, show all work. Other part of grade is a stats project and 3 "quizzes" which are open note exams weighted like 25%. I really like professor sarkar, he tries his very best for you to understand the concepts

analysis.name: Aaron Zimmerman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Physics at UT in general will be difficult, keep that in mind. With that being said, Professor Zimmerman is who you want to take if you're trying to actually learn physics while maintaining a high GPA. Very engaging and useful lectures. Extremely beneficial extra credit for just showing up to class. Office hours are also unmatched. My favorite prof

Best prof I've ever had. Lectures were amazing as he taught physics 2 in the most digestible way possible. If you can do HWs, you will be fine on the exam. +5 points on final grade was offered just for doing InstaPolls for completion. Don't worry about taking the class in community college; take physics 2 with Zimmerman and you will thank me

Lectures are always engaging and material is taught with clarity. Be sure to attend every lecture for up to 5% extra credit on the final, also helps you not get behind. Discussion sections are unnecessary & late but required to attend. Make sure to make an equation sheet for the exam- its very clutch. Very fair professor, 10/10.

He is amazing! He made attendance for extra 5 percent of the total grades which makes the total grade to 105. Keep attending the class and stay in touch with him, and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions, and you will get a satisfying grade in this his class! This class is worth being taken with him!!!

Professor Zimmerman was great at lecturing and was able to effectively teach all the material. However, I didn't like that the 3rd test took identical questions from the homework which isn't an accurate representation of performance (just memorizing).The discussion sections were mid, but the timing was horrible.

analysis.name: Scott Aaronson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Knowledgable but cant teach. Explains things too fast, doesnt realize students take longer to understand. Assumes complex things to be common sense. I attended every lecture but most of my learning came from elsewhere. Grading criteria was "1/3rd of class gets an A", left me in shock at my grade at the end. Impossible tests and hw, TAs confused too
For QIS, I thought the content was very interesting, and lectures were good and worth attending. Exams sometimes had unclear questions, but other than that, not terribly difficult.

I overall liked the structure of the course—the online textbook had clear explanations and the psets were difficult but not impossible, and I felt like I learned a lot. However, the exams were extremely difficult and worth a large percentage of the grade. You have to be good at algos and solving new problems in a test environment to do well.

Aaronson is knowledgeable about QIS, but is meh at teaching. His office smelled like a dead animal, until I realized it was his breath... He gets annoyed when students cant follow along with his occasional fast paced rants where he hardly touches base. His exams were unfair and took off too many points for small mistakes. Not worth taking ECE 379K.
Don't be fooled by the difficulty of the homework because the exams are infinitely harder and more unfair.

analysis.name: Aaron Rochlen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He asked for my number when I asked for the major project rubric. Very vague on what he expects and often changes it before the due dates. Experiences differ depending on your TA, but if you enjoy the subject, it's not too bad.

There are easier UGS courses, but the live concerts are nice. There's a $40 textbook of random online articles you will rarely use. Many of the assignment instructions have typos and are unorganized, but they expect your paper to be perfect. It seems like the TAs grade randomly and nitpick at random things that the rubric never specified.

He's a hit or miss depending on your personality - I didn't really like him, but you interact more with your TA than him if you don't participate in lectures. He will call you out to read a slide or answer a question if he notices you're not paying attention though. I felt his lectures were kind of slow paced so I wasn't that engaged.

Take the class if you need the credit but honestly professor is a lot to deal with. TAs will make the class much better. Was definetly not a fan of him and so weren't a lot of other people. He might like you he might not and his opinion stays the entire semester.

He knows what he's talking about and the class is never boring - but he's definitely a hit or miss personality for sure. If the subject matter genuinely interests you, I'd say go for it, because you generally spend more time with your TA in this class than with him.

analysis.name: Aaron Sandel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: [UGS: History of Friend VS Foe] I had Dr. Sandel for my UGS and I loved the class! It was so chill, we just had in class discussions on what love or friendship is, etc. Dr. Sandel seems really passionate about his studying of chimpanzees and it was rlly interesting to hear about his work in Africa. If you want a light + fun UGS, take this class!

Least scientific science course I have ever taken--Dr. Sandel is a joke. I genuinely didn't learn a thing all semester, I just listened to classmates debate about nothing in particular. Easy enough class I suppose, I didn't do anything besides free writes and making sticky note maps. There was no structure and even less learning. Waste of time.
The only reason I didn't hate Ant301. He went slow and made it easy to understand the topic!

(This review is for his UGS 302 class, there was just no way to select that on RMP)

Dr. Sandel is super kind and caring! His class was very easy, and basically, a guaranteed A if you attended the classes (attendance matters a lot). The actual subject, how chimpanzees make friends and enemies, was pretty interesting, although a little confusing.

OO OOH EE AH AH!!! These are the sounds of the Ngogo chimps that we studied in Professor Sandel's UGS 302 class. In this class, I made so many lasting social bonds. This class is my fav class I've taken so far in college, and Dr. Sandel was super nice & caring. This class changed my life. Would definitely take again. Attendance is mandatory.

analysis.name: Aaron Tugendhaft
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Tugendhaft was frequently available to students and was engaging in every single class. Each day was an insightful discussion with peers that garnered a deeper understanding of the material. I absolutely recommend taking any class by Professor Tugendhaft, you will not be disappointed.

Aaron structures his class for the sole purpose of you actually learning something. His class is not designed to put you under immense stress or anxiety about grades, its really all absorbing the subject matter. Even if you are struggling for whatever reason, related to the class or not, he will help you out. His lectures are very enjoyable.

Aaron is the best professor I've ever had at UT. He is an extremely talented, engaging lecturer and the first I've ever had who I feel legitimately cares about his students' academic progress. I'm taking another class with him next semester!

i'm sick of the aaron hate he is so awesome! he's so funny and incredibly smart and adapted what is usually very convoluted and complex material into a really interesting and easy format. i thought i was going to HATE this class--i could not have been more wrong! i loved the readings and the material and prof tugendhaft made it so much fun!

Essays are graded by the TA (who gave great feedback for improvement after I scheduled a meeting), but Dr. Tugendhaft requires a meeting prior to the submission of your essay. Ultimately, you get in what you put out—he expects you to read and come to class prepared, and he can often tell if students haven't been engaging with the assigned readings.

analysis.name: Aaron Moses
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Moses is a very passionate lecturer and cares a lot about his subject. There aren't a lot of assignments, however the exams are lengthy and challenging (the exams ARE open note). We had a 7 hour period to take the midterm and it took me 6 hours. The midterm has 9 essay questions, and the exams require a pretty good grasp of the content.

Professor Moses is an incredibly sweet person who knows a lot and cares about this subject. If you take detailed notes you should be fine but  be warned the tests take around 5-6 hours. They are open note but the questions can be quite hard, also have 9 essay questions. if you don't like art history then this class is def not the vapa for you.

Professor Moses is an incredible lecturer and is clearly passionate about the material. He made me genuinely interested in art history. However, the exams are brutal and both took me at least 4 hours (2 exams, 15% each of your grade). They're open note but 9 essay questions can be taxing. There are 5-6 other writing assignments besides the exam.

He's super passionate and it was interesting, but man, those exams were brutal. You have a long period to complete them (like all day) but they take like 4-5 hours and they're not easy. At some point, writing essays (something I'm very good at!) became physically difficult because I'd been at it for so long. Some other assignments, but not many.

Professor Moses' ARH 303 was very interesting and an easy VAPA. We had two tests that were open note and a few short writing assignments. The tests were easy if you paid attention to the lectures and took notes on the starred topics on the powerpoint slides. There is a textbook, but the lectures are so in-depth you don't have to read it or buy it.

analysis.name: Aaron Baker
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Exams are 30% each for a total of 90%. Difficult but fair tests similar to practice probs and HW. His lectures tended to be a panic-y period where I frantically wrote what he wrote to keep up. Tests weren't too bad as it only included a few topics from lecture -- most of what you learn won't be tested over, but you cant know that before-hand.

Transport is a difficult subject, but Dr Baker really takes the time to explain concepts that people have questions about, and he seems to have a lot of empathy for his students. The exams are fair, and the homework and in-class questions are adequate to prepare you for them. Definitely attend lectures; there is new content covered every day.
His exams are very hard and the averages for those are usually between 65 to 70%, but he gives a really good curve.

analysis.name: Dena Afrasiabi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is A LOT of work, especially if you don't start with any Persian. Very homework-heavy, flipped-classroom, so you work through the textbook on your own, class is for practice and tests. However, this professor really cares about student outcomes and tries her best to help. You could also see the class improving throughout the semester.

Great class and will really teach you Farsi if you commit to it. Simply doing the homework and making sure to get it right will basically get you literate. It is a time commitment, 2hrs three times a week and it takes about 2hrs to do homework every night too, upside is all the other assignments also take 2hrs so nothing is killer. She is also nice

The class is a mess. First time teaching and she's just as lost as us. Two papers and a presentation account for 80% of your final grade. She doesn't know how to use a computer or any kind of technology. The class organization is absent. Due dates are listed on the syllabus and make sure to remember them cuz no one will remind you. DON'T TAKE THIS!

analysis.name: Omoniyi Afolabi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Afolabi is an interesting professor. I learned a lot from his UGS302 Brazilian Studies class, and the small class format made it more engaging and fun. He can be hard to understand with his accent and his comments on papers dont always make sense, but he is very knowledgable about Brazil. One of the best classes I've taken at UT.

You do not need to read anything!!! he spends all of lecture going through the summary of that happened over the "assigned reading" and gets really off track, but ALL of the assignemnts are super easy and the prompts are so broad that you can just research and write instead of reading the dense material. HE GRADES ON GRAMMAR OVER CONTENT!!!

Dr. Afolabi is a very enthusiastic professor! His class is interesting and straightforward but can be pretty disorganized at times. Many papers are assigned, but the class does carry a writing flag. He grades mainly based on grammar instead of the essays' actual content. Once you understand his writing style, getting A's on the papers is very easy

Enthusiastic, fun, and interesting, but a lot of the content covered in class is unnecessary to do well. Once you understand how he grades papers will be easy A's, he is not tech savvy but genuinely cares about his students and loves teaching

Much of this class is saved by the interesting topic and the professor who presents the information. His regular enthusiasm and willingness to describe a culture which, at least to me, was novel proved to be highly valuable. However, his critiques of writing are at best technical and the stylistic and argumentative feedback was distinctly limited.

analysis.name: Afroze Shaikh
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took the EDP Career Planning course over the summer and enjoyed it! We learned so much—I especially loved our textbook since it was actually fun to read. There were reading/content quizzes, assignments graded on effort because they were focused on your personal career planning, and an interview of someone in your field of interest for the final.

Dr. Shaikh made her expectations for the class very clear and graded content fairly. She truly cares about each one of her students and is always open to talk about any concerns. This class did not require a ton of effort, but you should still put an honest effort into the assignments.

Dr. Shaikh is a caring and compassionate professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable and assigns relevant and thoughtful assignments. With fair effort, this class is very doable and enjoyable. She is wonderful!

analysis.name: Afsar Mohammad
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Presently, I'm in Prof. Afsar's "Modern India and Literature" class. I'm so lucky to get into the class which has a long wait list. And,Prof. Afsar never disappointed until now. He is passionate, fun and clarity of thought. Wonderful insights into the materials.

He is a great professor with lots of passion for his subject! I enjoyed every minute of his class. If you keep up with the work and go to class then you should have no problem getting the grade you want. How much you get out of the class depends on how much you put in!Make sure you meet him outside of class because he is a great person to get to kn

This is the third class I've taken with Afsar. He's a great professor. The subject material is always very interesting, and he doesn't shy away from controversial or 'awkward' topics. He always brings humor to the discussion as well. He is very interested in students' progress and is always willing to meet to discuss papers,etc.

Taking Prof. Afsar's new class "Pilgrimage in South Asia." Heard a lot about Prof. Afsar before, but this is my first class with him. Really enjoyable! Extremely fascinating/ real research experiences! Accessible Professor, loves to spend more time with the students. Values the student voice and he has a great smile!

Really cares for the progress of the student. Makes every class a memorable experience with lot of stories. I've been taking his courses continuosly. Specifically his course on South Asian Novel is my favorite.

analysis.name: Chris Aarons
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Aarons is hands down the best professor I've ever had in college. I have never learned more in any other class than I have in this class. His lectures are fun & really interesting. He sends out surveys to his students and really takes feedback & caters to what you need throughout the semester. If you have the chance to take him, DO IT!

Prof Aarons is by far one of the best professors I have had at UT. Taking Digital MKT with him impacted me in many ways - landing an internship, growing in knowledge, and being challenged to do my best work. He is an inspiring lecturer, hilarious, and gives priority to help his students even on weekends. His class will change your life! TAKE!

- THOUSANDS of dollars worth of AMAZING guest lecturers? Check. - Learning real-world skills that you can apply immediately? Check. - This class alone is worth an entire semester's tuition alone? CHECK. AND. MATE. You are doing yourself a disservice if you aren't going to take this class. Put your heart into this class and you will thrive.

Chris was the best professor I had at McCombs BY FAR. He is so caring & wise & willing to do anything to help his students & better their learning experience. I'll carry what I learned in his class with me for the rest of my professional life. He will also casually and humbly drop things like how he met Travis Scott or Amazon is one of his clients.

Aarons is hilarious, & the best professor ever!! It may seem like his instructions are vague, but it is all to help you think for yourself & unlock your full potential. He is always available to chat in office hours or even over the phone if u are confused, & his main priority is to make sure his students succeed! Lectures are also super engaging!

analysis.name: Ahmed Shamim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Because he was leaving this semester, it felt as if his class was sloppily composed due to his lack of passion for UT. He's great at what he does, but he put the bare minimum into this class's structure. However, he is great at explaining Bangla for non-native speakers and was such a kind and hilarious professor. Smart man, just very disorganized!
Dr. Shamim is a great teacher. He is fun, caring, and laid back. The workload is also very reasonable and slow-paced as he wants everyone to learn on the same page. Take him!

Professor Shamim is adaptable in his teaching methods. If a student is struggling with a particular part of the Bangla language, he will make sure that the student will eventually understand it. This ranges from the alphabet, general grammar, vocabulary, to even dialects. Not only that, he is available outside class if you ask him. Adore this guy!

analysis.name: Ahmed Helal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Take his class. Gives a heavy curve and material isn't complicated
He is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are clear and beneficial to the class. He engages his students with understandable materials. Would recommend everyone to take his class!

analysis.name: Shaherzad Ahmadi
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I did not think she was great at all. Her lectures were very sporadic and they did not follow a clear progression. She had way too many assignments and expectations for a lower division history course (over 20 pages worth of papers for the semester). She was available outside of class but she had clear favorites.

Liked her approach but lectures can be quite hard to follow. Tends to assume everyone is on the same page based on a few vocal students. However it was still pretty easy to make an A in the class, and I felt I didn't need to show up to make the grade. Essay assignments are the majority of the grade and can be done largely independently.
Pretty easy grader, I feel like if you put in the effort you'll make an A. "Shaz" knows her stuff.

Her lectures were highly informative and she encourages independent reading when writing papers. Shaherzad is extremely knowledgable and will guide you in the right direction. If you like the course title and topic, she's the person to take it with!

Like another reviewer said, Shaz's lectures lack any sense of cohesion. She jumps around in topics, time periods and regions frequently. Judging by the lack of attendance everyday, I would say most people agree with me when I say that this class was a waste of time. Shaz is very smart, but a bad teacher.

analysis.name: Ahmed Siddiqi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This course is an introductory survey of the political philosophy of several philosophers throughout the western world. Those who are uninterested in reading antiquated texts pertaining to political philosophy should not take this course. This course contains substantial reading. This course was incredibly thought-provoking.
Professor Siddiqi is very thorough. His class is difficult for a lower division government class, but I found it enjoyable. If you don't like philosophy, you may want to steer clear.

Great guy, great professor. Class is clear-cut & minimalist: do the daily readings, come ready to discuss/debate, and complete the two assigned papers. Final grade comprised of few assignments, w/ each paper weighted HEAVILY. Can be a tough grader w/ sorta unrealistic standards, but final is easy. Very intellectual, pensive guy - great to talk to.

He is really good at leading discussion based courses and helps keep class discussions from getting too tangential.  I didn't do a lot of the readings near the end because I was swamped and got recked by the final.  I liked him though, wish I could take again and try harder.   Really cool to talk with during office hours.

He's a great professor, and the class was a lot of fun. I'm a huge history nerd, and I really learned a lot and gained new insight into politics and philosophy. The reading and the class discussions were great too.

analysis.name: Enrique Aguayo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: an amazing professor, i would highly recommend to take this class. he is a very patience person and a very fair grader. show up to class and you'll do well. because of the material of the class and how it is taught dont take this class as a freshman which is the mistake i made. would retake this class still.

Professor Aguayo is extremely understanding. He is also a student, so he understands the stress of finals season. Attendance in his class is for extra credit. His assignments are clear, and I literally ended with a 100 by turning all the assignments in. Definitely take this class if you need the credit!

This class was easy, but I  learned a lot. There's some freedom in how you complete the assignments. He doesn't post any information for each lecture until like an hour before class, so there's not much time to review things before class. Great class for people unsure of their career path or who want to learn how to prepare to enter the workforce.

analysis.name: Kamran Aghaie
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Terrible professor. The class had no structure and the lectures were whatever he came up with that day. The only way to do well in the class is to write to what his preconceived opinions are about the given subject. You wont learn anything from him only on your own.

Professor Aghaie was the opposite of helpful and supporting. His lectures consisted of him going off on tangents about whatever he felt like discussing that given day so most of the learning was up to you as the student. It often felt like he was making the class structure up as he went along and he never responds to emails. I q dropped.

I think getting an A is pretty manageable if you do the readings and go to all the lectures. However, I didn't really feel that his lectures were very organized, and having to take notes on literally everything he says because it'll end up on the test becomes annoying when, on the test, you're having to remember his jumbled trail of thought.

Lectures were really random and didn't relate to the assigned readings often, had to mostly self learn/ study with the textbook. Primarily about history of the middle east, not gov, which was still interesting, but the random lectures and quite difficult timed essay mt/ finals were still difficult.

The class was just weekly readings and build up to a final research paper. Readings were long and often went undiscussed in class because Dr. Aghaie would go off on long tangents (he is clearly VERY intelligent on this subject, and makes that known). He was approachable, but was often unhelpful with feedback. Course was unorganized. TA was useless.

analysis.name: Ashish Agarwal
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There's no way to get around it; this class is hard. Homework will consume a lot of your time (8+ hours per assignment). But the workload does get lighter through the semester. Dr. Agarwal is nice and cares about his students; lectures could be more engaging though. Read the cases to participate in class, and study well in advance for the tests.

A challenging yet rewarding class based on Harvard Business School cases. Agarwal teaches MIS concepts through real-world examples and cold-calls often. Homework is independent and helps build Excel skills, especially for beginners. Exams are tough and oddly worded, but you learn a lot and  Agarwal is an excellent professor overall.

professor agarwal is a great professor. The concepts covered in the class and inherently difficult and directly apply to real world scenarios. Go to class and actually listen to lectures/discussion. Professor agarwal is also very approachable and willing to help you with any questions you may have.
Passionate about what he's teaching, but needs to be more structured. Also, the tests were worded weirdly and did not test how well you understood the topics discussed in class.

MIS301H will consume all of your time and if you don't study three times as much as you think you need to, you won't do well. While he is nice and generally decent at presenting the info., understanding the material falls solely on you. Do not take this class if you don't want to read thirty pages a night or spend less than 30 hours on assignments.

analysis.name: Seema Agarwala
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Agarwala is knowledgable and explains concepts well. However, she can be intimidating and impatient with students if they come unprepared to class or don't answer questions a particular way. Sometimes, the lectures seemed disorganized. Overall, not a hard class. Make sure you're prepared because she will ask questions about the previous lecture

Her lectures are dense and can be hard to follow, especially if you lack background knowledge. Attendance is mandatory, so if you'll miss more than three classes, this course may not be for you. Exams are application-focused with more points allocated to the FRQ. Overall, I wouldn't take this course again.

Dr. Agarwala is so knowledgeable and her lectures are very concise without fluffing up any information. The discussion sections led by her TAs were also incredibly helpful and everyone involved in the team ensures that you're ready for the exams. The exams and analyses of research papers ensures success in and out of her class. Take her!

Neuro development is an amazing class that absolutely improved how I read and write academic papers. This class is completely worth it if you are ready to put a substantial amount of effort in. She does cold call and her quizzes are hard, but you only need a 90+ to get an A and something like an 86+ to get an A-.

Dr. Argawala is incredibly impatient with her students and creates a hostile learning environment. She gets frustrated when students ask questions and is overall condescending. She does not promote a safe place whatsoever and will mock and embarrass you for saying the wrong thing in class.

analysis.name: Ahmed Gheith
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 99 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Gheith actually cares about teaching, and is very good at it. There are projects every week, ranging from fairly easy (3 hrs) to very hard (25hrs). I've taken 3 classes with Gheith so far, and if he taught any more, I'd take them too.

Gheith is an amazing teacher who knows the material cold (lectures with no notes) and is very nice in office hours. That said, the class is extremely tough, and of the 14 projects, I and most people I know put in 40+ hours of effort on 4 of them. Find a solid group to work with and plan carefully before writing any code, and you will do well

He's an excellent professor, but OS is genuinely one of the hardest classes you can take. It will be really difficult for you. Yes, even you. I'd take it again, but only because of the friends I made in it. I literally lost 15lbs because I was working so much on it. Really. It's 50-60 hrs/week. If you do take it, don't take anything else hard.
Helpful professor and knows the material inside & out. However, his CS 429 Summer class was insanely challenging. The assignments and quizzes were brutal. I think half the class ended up dropping.

One of those classes where you come out with a profound jump in mastery even if you only got a C-. The lectures are an absolute delight, he has immense understanding of the material. Likely the hardest programming projects you will do during your time at UT, but also thoroughly instructive and insightful. May have to no-life this class to do well.

analysis.name: Kristen Adams
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Adams for BME 344 was pretty good; she got the job done and was funny. She also brings her dogs often to class. Weekly homework took a while but it was reasonable. Final exam is optional. You can miss 6 class instapolls which is generous. Weekly quiz over the previous hw, and occasional pop quizzes just to add as bonus (fine if you miss).

I went back here to say that I am so glad Im taking other BME professors rn that are genuinely qualified to teach at this level and material. After going through several of her classes, I almost lost faith in pursuing BME. She dropped my grade by a letter grade for not taking an instapoll during an exam I literally took and directly handed to her.

She cares way more about Instapolls (which she takes even during exam days), than showing your mastery of the material. Wish she just had a sign-in sheet. Lecturing style is monotone with slow pacing; shows no enthusiasm in the material. You'll learn way more from watching CPPMechEngTutorials, who saved me during the heat transfer unit.

Instructor is condescending in Office Hours. TA never shows up to Office hours. LA was very helpful tho so go to them for help. Heat transfer is pretty difficult and instructor struggles with teaching it because of staffing issues so be prepared. 1 exam is dropped so try to do well for them and don't take final exam unless you have to.

Even when I was physically in class and completed Instapoll, I was marked “absent” because I had not taken the optional bonus quiz. No clear communication, policies that were not detailed in the syllabus were suddenly enforced later. One additional absence results in a 10% drop from your overall grade. Grade dropped from A to B.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Adams
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is a simple but engaging VAPA that Dr. Adams structured to be easy. The class is beyond manageable and has little to no workload as long as you pay attention to the lectures, do the readings, and study a bit for the weekly quizzes. There were no exams in the class, and instead of a final, there is a fun final project. Highly Recommended!

I'd die for Lizzy. If you didnt like her you probably thought you could get away with doing nothing, which is just plain lazy and you only have yourself to blame. Loved her lectures, she's so funny. Have to buy tophat for attendance. No tests, just weekly quizzes with 2 drops and a final project. Loved this class so much, it was really interesting.

Dr. Adams is a great lecturer, but it's the lengthy daily readings that made me dread going to this class, as well as the weekly quizzes.  You truly will learn a lot, but unless you like learning out of an online textbook and then going and being talked at about it, I don't recommend.  If you're looking for an easy a though, take her Rome class.

As a STEM major, I really enjoyed this class. No tests, engaging lectures, and weekly quizzes every Friday. The annotations/readings due before every class can be difficult to stay consistent with, but you only need to write a few sentences. Write your notes during lecture and review by re-listening to recorded lectures on 2x speed.

I fell ill and had to drop.  The nature of the course is fast paced but I love the way she has the course structured and once I understood the flow it got so much easier.  It takes time to learn another language but the way she teaches does make it really fun. I plan to take her class again.

analysis.name: Adam Bush
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bush's class was pretty enjoyable and easy enough to get an A in. Projects are a large part of your grade, which have really confusing directions but at least are graded easily. Essentially no homework (completion, really short even if you do it) and only 2 exams if you do well on both. You gotta go to class though for your hw/participation.

Dr. Bush integrated his research in a way that made the class so much more interesting than your typical circuits class. Seeing as it was a BME class, he integrated physiological circuits and imaging from his lab so that we had cool projects like analyzing our own vasculature. He also had super neat demos and plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Lectures were posted online & 50% of the grade was essentially participation (20% attendance, 30% projects which were graded very leniently). I feel he has gotten a bad rep. I came into this class honestly expecting the worst but he has improved immensely as compared to previous semesters. Optional final & exams were very similar (easier) than HW.

Prof Bush was good at explaining the concepts during lecture, and his tests were very fair. Optional final if you do good enough on the midterms, and the homeworks are all optional too. Light amount of coursework and overall easy class. Only complaint is that there weren't enough instructions given on the projects, and there was little time given.

Dr. Bush was new to teaching. He had never taken a circuits class before having to teach it, and many students did poorly on the first test; however, he gave his students several chances to raise their grades. Students who failed the first exam ended the class with A's. Also, there were plenty of optional extra credit opportunities.

analysis.name: Adam Cobb
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He expected class participation yet was rude to students who didn't answer exactly correctly. He was also weird about using computers and will give you a very hard time if you are even slightly late to class. There are only 4 assignments and they're graded very strictly. The material is interesting but do not take his class if you can help it.

The topics discussed in this class were interesting, and I even enjoyed some of the assignments. However, Dr. Cobb is the most disrespectful and condescending professor I've had at UT. A good part of the grade is participation, but he makes it almost impossible to participate as he belittles you and your opinions.

Very harsh grader. Extremely short tempered, often rude, and does not give students space to learn. Grades on the assumption that every student knows the same amount of knowledge as him. Often talks over students as well. This is very unfortunate as the course material was extremely interesting.

analysis.name: Adrian Rodriguez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took it last fall, and thermo is a pretty harsh class, but Prof Rodriguez teaches the concepts very well, and his TAs were pretty approachable. The grading wasn't too punishing, and I was able to reach a B despite thinking I was barely gonna pass. Oh, also, he likes to bring snacks to every lecture, so that was pretty cool of him to do.

Dr. Rodriguez is great, and you can tell he wants his students to do well. Thermo is naturally a difficult class, but he definitely made it easier through his effort and availability. Weekly quizzes are based on one hw problem from the additional set, and make sure to use the ASME test bank to study for tests, as problems are often recycled.

It's Thermo; it will be difficult. However, Rodriguez is caring and communicative enough to lighten the mental load. We used an online textbook (ZyBooks) with participation (watch a few animations) and challenge (homework problems) activities built in. Study for weekly quizzes, cram for tests, and rest assured Rodriguez is there to help out.

It was Rodriguez's first time teaching this course, and I really appreciated his willingness to work with students to make the class a smoother ride. Thermo is a difficult class, but he provided many opportunities for extra credit and always asked for feedback. His lectures were engaging, and I enjoyed his class.
Dr. Rodriguez had the most organized Canvas page I have ever seen, and he makes expectations very clear. Super kind and approachable- would highly recommend for 318M

analysis.name: Adriana Rizk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Adriana's enthusiasm for teaching truly stands out. She sets high expectations in a way that is encouraging rather than forceful, creating an environment where students feel motivated to grow. She allows young students to discover music for themselves, helping them develop discipline and autonomy at such a young age. Thank you for this experience!

Adriana is a wonderful teacher. It's impressive to see someone so young balance dual majors while demonstrating such maturity and intuition when working with children. She brings both professionalism and warmth to her teaching, creating a positive and engaging environment for her students. For the kids classroom felt like a room full of friends.

I had the opportunity to take private lessons with Adriana, and she is an incredibly patient, organized, and thoughtful teacher. She approaches each lesson with creativity and is able to adapt her teaching to meet students where they are, which makes the learning process both comfortable and motivating.

analysis.name: Ari Adut
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Adut is kind, approachable, and a very skilled lecturer. Attendance isn't mandatory BUT coming to class helps a ton, especially if you do not do the readings. Three tests count for 100% of your grade but they are straightforward.This class is a breeze as long as you pay attention, take notes, and go to the review sessions.

This class was probably the easiest class I have taken in university, although it can be boring at times. Dr. Adut is a very kind person, so the class felt very relaxed. I would definitely take again.

Prof Adut is very knowledgable/passionate about what he teaches. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you show up and take good notes then you will do quite well on his tests. The course was made up of 3 written exams, no final.

Honestly, I don't advocate skipping class but if you were to only show up to the review and memorized it, you'd pass with a B. No joke. Don't bother buying the book, NEVER miss review day, but don't buy the book.

Dr. Adut was a great professor and lecturer, wanting his students to constantly participate. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you skip class you will miss all of the information on the exams. Don't bother buying the books, I never needed to read them because Dr. Adut was so good at explaining the information. Take this class!

analysis.name: Adam Clulow
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Clulow is an excellent lecturer and professor. This course is graded by quite a few components which can pile up fast if you're not prepared. You have 3 free absences throughout the semester, and Dr. Clulow is readily available to work with students on extensions, extra credit, etc. Highly recommend for an overview of Japanese martial history.

Professor Clulow is an amazing professor who obviously cares a lot about the material he teaches. His lectures are engaging, funny, and in-depth. Most readings he makes accessible through Canvas. The course is thought-provoking and interesting, and Prof Clulow makes every effort to make sure his students understand the material.

Loved this class! An exciting approach to a history class with many clear connections drawn between the events of the distant past and present. I swear I think about something I learned in this class at least once a week. Just remember to stay on top of your independent research project because the due dates will sneak up on you.

Clulow is a great teacher and you can tell he loves what he teaches, he's super kind and almost always gives an extension if you reach out to him. Assignments were not too hard as long as you show effort you should get 80s and above. You only really need the lectures for the mid-term, everything else is accessible via online information. Cool Class

Dr. Clulow was one of my favorite professors ever. He is super knowledgable, passionate and engaging. His lectures are fun and easy to get engaged with via watching clips, listening to songs, and tying in pop-culture. He responds to emails super quickly and if you can't make office hours he will work with you. A lot of readings, but not difficult.

analysis.name: Adam Klivans
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Klivans is brilliant and he knows his stuff, but he's not the best at explaining concepts. He records lectures and assigns them as hw before every class. In class, you do absurdly challenging practice problems. Tests and homeworks are VERY difficult. The greatest thing about this class though: he's a very lenient grader and it's curved.

I do not recommend this class. The grading is really tough and it is sorta difficult to ask questions and get a good response. Most of the material on homeworks and exams were never touched on in class. For a class that was supposed to not be so bad, it was my hardest class
