Klivans is definitely one of the more difficult 313 professors although he curves the grades at the end. He will be sarcastic if you ask a question, although he does try to make sure you understand. It is a flipped class so lectures are online, problems worked in class. Also gives pop quizzes in class.
Disappointing how ineffective his lectures are for an online class. He is clearly very knowledgeable and smart, but poorly communicates ideas in an easy to understand manner.

I should have just said this to Klivans during class, but if you're going to have a linear algebra/probability heavy lecture, you should give the students a heads-up. Also, instead of saying ""You're not gonna learn this anywhere else better," it would be more helpful to point us to other resources (b/c he's very bad at explaining stuff).

analysis.name: Ainash Childebayeva
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This was definitely one of the harder anthropology classes, especially bc I had no genetics background. She lectures very quickly, & I got points off for unimportant stuff, but she's knowledgeable. You can tell she cares more about her research than teaching. Admirable professor but not an easy class - check prior syllabi before registering.

had her for INB-337. All she does is read off the slides, no emotion, no care, nothing interesting in teaching style. She's showed up late to her own class so many times. As of right now she's been late more than on time. Class is boring and she's intentionally vague on assignments.

I had her for a different class than the one I had listed here. But the points still remains that she is not really capable of teaching and has a huge ego and I guess the department is making her teach some other classes for the fall.

Lots of reading (~2 scientific papers by the start of each class). Lectures were often too fast to make time for class discussion and student lectures which were unproductive in my opinion. Very disorganized, most assignments had no rubric or clear guidelines and instructions would be changed at the last minute. Was hard to discern what she wanted.

The courseload was very heavy, office hours were often cancelled. Had to read 2 scientific research papers and a textbook chapter by every class, had a 5,000-word research paper due at end of the semester and 2 exams worth 30% of the grade. Found it hard to keep up with slides in lecture due to the speed of her lectures and lack of explaining.

analysis.name: Yukie Aida
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Unorganized schedule that we were behind on Homework. Overall, she posted assignments late as well as exams her format did not help in studying. READ the textbook and take good notes on her class. Late on grading as well, and quizzes every day so try not to miss her class as much as possible cause those points will save you. Choose Wisely

I can see why she has so many good reviews because at heart, she is such a nice and caring person. However, I found her lecture pacing incredibly slow, especially in the first half of the semester. At times it felt like "Okay let's move on, but we'd spend too much time on the SAME thing. She also tends to keep class over the allotted time.

Amazing professor. Extremely kind and genuinely wants to help you learn Japanese. The course load is what you expect for any language learning class; lots of homework, quizzes, and exams. Still, this was one of the funnest classes I've ever taken and that was due to how great Aida-sensei is as a person and a lecturer.

Aida-sensei genuinely cares about her students, and their learning. Additionally, she presents material in a clear, easy to understand manner, and encourages active participation to learn the language. An added bonus: she is incredibly energetic and her class is fun to attend.

One of my favorite teachers. She is super sweet and makes class fun. Homework and quizzes every day, but it's manageable. She forgets to upload things sometimes, but nothing that can't be found on the JOSHU website. She's good at getting you to practice speaking and repetition in class, so you retain quite a lot. Really good for starting Japanese.

analysis.name: Aimee Hosemann
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class is super easy and interesting. No final, just a book report, so a lot of people stopped going to class after the midterm. I went to every lecture though because they were honestly fun. Discussions were kind of a waste of time but attendance is mandatory. No text book but a few cool, short books are assigned, as well as journal readings.

Professor Hosemann is a pro! She is a super smart, well cultured professor. Everything is fair game in lectures, this course is really entertaining because you get to explore so many things that are otherwise taboo. Really glad I took this class, it almost makes me want to be an anthropology major.

Extremely easy class. She is a very engaging professor. You really don't need to show up for lecture after the midterm. Discussion sections: go to them. If you go to lecture, no attendance, it'll be a very interesting discussion, but I didn't find them extremely helpful after the midterm. No final exam! Only a book report, so as long as you read...

She is DEF one of the best professors at UT! I loved her class, if I wasn't a Sr., I'd probably switch to Anthro. She really cares about what students think and assignments are "discussions" with her on paper, which she responds to via Canvas! Not to mention EVERY lecture is interesting. Even if you wouldn't normally think its an interesting topic.

It was a summer course, so it was a little more compacted, but still great. There were only 3 "journal entries" which are written in third person. She wants to hear what you think ALWAYS. In lecture and on paper. She was a seriously great lecturer and sincerely cares about her students. I could tell she LOVES her job. I am so glad I took the class.

analysis.name: Manasicha Akepiyapornchai
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Mana was an excellent teacher and is clearly knowledgeable and cares about the things she teaches. I took her class about the BG with her and learned a lot. Grading was easy as long as you actually take the time to read the instructions and meet the clear requirements.

(I took ANS379 Translating Asia. I'm not sure why there isn't an option.) Mana is truly a student-centered teacher, always willing to help, really cares about her students, and listens to their concerns. One thing to be aware of is that her course requires a significant amount of reading. Her grading is very nice, rarely loses points.

Pretty easy class, however for a non-hindu may be confusing. professor is very friendly and always willing to help. Her understanding of Hinduism and its philosophies/beliefs is a little off. So if you are a hindu you may be confused or even heavily disagree with her approach to some gods. Overall she is very kind and I enjoyed this course

I took Prof. Mana for South Asian gods and goddesses....her class is an easy A. I never even did the readings when I was taking this class (I was born and raised Hindu) but for someone who wasn't it may be more difficult...she assigns bunch of readings in class. She often also rambles on during class as well but overall this class was an easy A.

Honestly such a sweet and informative professor. There's a lot of reading, but you could get away by just skimming through them. She's also very accommodating as long as you communicate with her! I had no real knowledge about Hinduism, but it's very doable.

analysis.name: Aida Torabi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Let me just preface this by saying that as a professor, Dr. Torabi is pretty nice. However the biggest problem with her class is that the exams are designed for you to fail because they are completely different from all the HW problems we get and are significantly harder. Honestly just take someone else if you can.
Very hard!!!  I literally got a like a 58 on first test

She's lowk rude sometimes and I swear she goes over the easiest examples in class and then the exams/homeworks are way, way harder. She confronted the class after the MEDIAN on MT2 was a 57 and told us to study harder… lol just admit you're not a good prof it's fine. It's fine tho, she gave us 0.5% extra credit at the end of the semester, how kind

Idek if she could get a A on her own tests. Other professors make midterms more conceptual but she spams math questions. puts questions on the test that she hasn't taught the class how to work. We're supposed to learn to solve the questions thru the HW –> the crazy hard test questions aren't covered there. dont take her if you value your gpa/time.

Good reviews on here will just say she's nice –> she is but she's a terrible lecturer. Shows simple applications of concepts in lecture but on exams and HWs tests on very complex applications of concepts. 1% EC but that's if you show up to all lectures and do 12 extra HW assignments (all with over 15 questions). No curves on exams w/ an avg of 60!

analysis.name: Akash Kanojia
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is a fantastic class to get an in-depth understanding of markets. This is completely an open discussion class, but Akash does a great job of explaining everything in a fun and detailed way. There are two exams which are difficult, but the class gets curved anyways. Highly recommend taking this class and getting to know Akash!

By far my favorite class I've taken. Half the grade is participation and the tests are heavily curved. If you show up and participate you are almost guaranteed an A. He's extremely smart and has great real world experiences, and he really cares about his students. No better class to learn about what is going on in markets AND how to talk about them

Great class to learn about markets and keep up to date. There are 2 exams that are pretty difficult but the class gets curved to a 3.6 anyways so it doesn't matter as long as you get within the average (~65). His class emphasizes participation so show up and try to contribute as much as possible its worth 30% of your grade. Overall, great professor

Great professor and lectures, sensible content to address markets from different perspective (and each week has a market lecture too). Exams aren't too hard, it's like 2/3 general understanding from lectures and readings and then 1/3 hard/nitpicky questions "to make a curve." If you listen in class, a day's studying probably enough.

Akash is an excellent professor who is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject matter. If you really want to learn about markets, you'll absolutely love this course. The tests are tough, but the class is heavily curved. He's one of my favorite professors I've had at McCombs. Just show up, participate, and you'll do well.

analysis.name: Deji Akinwande
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The exams are multiple choice but not much partial credit is awarded if you select the wrong answer for whatever reason. Lectures didn't feel that helpful either, so I would recommend reading the textbook and/or watching the relevant Razavi Electronics I and II lectures on YouTube and doing the assigned practice problems to succeed in this course.

I loved Deji's lectures, he made funny anecdotes about his life and somehow strung it back to transistors and circuits haha. The exams were very chill, but since they're mcq, its a bit unforgiving if you make small mistakes. He does pull questions  from the textbook though, so theoretically you can just do all the book problems. Labs are good too.

One of the best professors in the department!
If you get 100 on the final exam, you will automatically get an A in the class.
I have had such an awesome semester with him. Definitely recommend, I wish I could take another class taught by him!

Dr. Akiwande was an amazing professor! He cracks funny jokes and tells his life stories sometimes during lectures. I learned a lot about how transistors work in his class. Although it's a lab class, the tests still make up 60% of your grades. But they are all MCs and very doable! This was an excellent class, and he was an amazing guy to talk to!

analysis.name: Erin Akins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Erin gives amazing feedback & understands most students are not english majors. She makes class inclusive, fun & engaging, one I always woke up to go to. Her feedback is super helpful, drops quizzes, and grades super leniently, while also wanting you to stretch your understanding. 4 books to read, and 3 papers, only hw is reading. AMAZING PROF

I took Banned Books with Erin and she is probably one of the best professors i've had. By far my favorite class of the semester and I'm sure everyone else in my class would agree. She takes the books to new levels and is phenomenal at explaining she may act like she's all over the place but she knows what she's doing. Cant wait to read her books.

Class was Rhetoric of Apology and it was very interesting & doable! Akins is currently a grad student, and the only issue was the slow grading and limited feedback as the course progressed. There is no TA so that's why grading multiple essays took a long time. Rewrites for points back are available and its overall a great class for a writing flag!

analysis.name: Akemi Katayama
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Katayama may seem a little intimidating at times but she overall cares for her students very much and you can tell she really wants you to succeed. Pay attention in class and be ready to participate. Reading the textbook before class really gets you a head start on lessons in class. 601D is easy but 610D is a little more difficult

I loved Katayama-sensei when I took her for 601 and 610. She's a little strict at times but it shapes you into a good Japanese speaker. Show her you care and that you like Japanese and she'll love you. Read the book before class, study your kanji, participate in class, and you'll do great, especially for 610D

Sensei is a great teacher but you do have to put effort into the class. As one of the previous comments said, she doesn't care for slackers. But she does care that you get an education and really immerse yourself in Japanese, so try in class and take the time to talk with her in office hours

Daily Quiz at the start of the class( at the start of your day too) won't spend time on Kanji, force everyone to shut their mic, go over things too fast but again and again, daily homework is also a pain

Nice but plain. I had her for and 8 am class and she was not the most exciting person to take up to. She does't care much for slackers but she's very helpful if you go to her office. It's a pretty easy class with a lot of quiz and homework grades. If you show up everyday, you also get +2 points on your overall grade.

analysis.name: Karen Akre
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are mandatory due to partial iClicker grade but are not very helpful. She just lectures off of slides It is better to just take notes from the book while going through the slides at home. Her tests are very unpredictable, no reviews, only a chat session the night before the test. Generally 25 MC, T/F, and about 5-8 free response.

A very disorganized class. would rather take another professor. Was very nonchalant regarding helping students study for exams. R Great at explaining but you could NEVER know what to expect on exams. Just hope your T.A. prepares you well..
Just read off her slides the entire time. I only went because of the clicker questions. If you do the readings, you can pass her class. Honestly, I was really bored in class. Not engaging at all.

analysis.name: Alexander Marras
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Despite the monotone voice, his lectures explain concepts very well and learning from him was not difficult.  Weekly quizzes based on the homework, and the homework is from the textbook. Exams are a mix of free response solving conceptual short answer/multiple choice, and are pretty fair. Very helpful office hours if you have questions.

Great professor. Lectures are good, help with high-level understanding and intuition. Quizzes are from homework, fairly easy. The only downside is that tests are meant to challenge you, so some of the questions, you have to work out intuitionally, memorizing text book questions won't always help. Otherwise, great guy, fun class.

the only bad thing about this professor is that he sounds like he hates his life when he lectures, but if you stuggle with insomnia this class will definitely cure you! weekly homework is a bit challenging, but super super helpful for exams. quizzes are regurgitated hw questions. he also curves amazingly and genuinely wants students to succeed.

Weekly homework that is graded for completion. Weekly quizzes that are identical to a homework problem. Good and interesting lectures. Tests consist of open-ended computational questions as well as conceptual questions at the end. Nice professor and offers opportunities for extra credit :)

Very nice and understanding professor. I learned a lot from his class, and I enjoyed his personality. He gave tons of extra credit and allowed us to replace our worst exam. No required reading quizzes, and I honestly didn't need them for most of the class. Would take him again!

analysis.name: Alfonso Cuevas
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Do not take his course. You learn nothing. There is no curve for all his courses. Lecture is a mess. There is quiz after every lecture. The quiz is not relevant to what he said. He is happy to see students make mistakes in exam and then he would say "I made a trick on that question and many of you were wrong." The worst professor I have ever seen.

Taking a class with Cuevas is like hiking up a mountain with a man on your back who smashes your knees with a hammer every 1000 steps and then blames you for having your knees in front of his hammer. He accused a large portion of the class of cheating because they used a technique for convolution that Cuevas couldn't do. He grades very hard.

Dr. Cuevas is very respectable as an engineer. However, his teaching is not the best.   He relies heavily on the textbook, fails to clearly explain examples, and has exams that are much more difficult than they need to be. Often, it is better to just read the textbook rather than attend lecture. Too bad there's pop quizzes.

was rude when i asked for help on a problem and dismissed me. proceeded to help a student on same problem right after. TAs grade harsh on lab reports, had to chase them down for feedback. does not post lectures & thinks that benefits students in their learning.seems like i got the short end of the stick with him but he made 411 wayy too complicated

Cuevas isn't a horrible guy, so I almost feel bad writing a bad review, but the truth is he is a bad teacher. He is super knowledgeable but horrible at conveying it. While I think people exaggerate on how hard exams are (they arent bad + he's nice with partial), he doesnt teach well enough to prepare you for them, and he can be very condescending

analysis.name: Eman  Alasadi
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I would say the only downside of this class is the grade distribution, but I really love her resources like her practice sets. I re-took CH301 after taking Laude last semester. She is SO incredible and straightforward and the way that she teaches makes perfect sense to me. We learn exactly what we need to do well on the exam, no fluff!

If you have to take any sort of Chemistry at UT, TAKE HER. This is probably the most caring and thoughtful professor I have ever had. Her lectures are actual fun and she goes out of her way to make sure students understand. Uploads all here lectures online and offers so many resources for studying. Occasional extra credit during class

Truly an outstanding professor. She goes above and beyond to support her students and provides an exceptional amount of resources to help you succeed. She is deeply invested in making sure students actually understand the material and is always willing to spend extra time explaining concepts. PChem could use slightly more rigor, but she's great

Professor Eman was the best chemistry professor ever!! She is super sweet and wants everyone to succeed. She offered 2 makeup exams at the end of the semester that will replace your lowest two exams. She is hilarious and lectures were always engaging. You do have to study and put in some time/work, but all the material is accessible and organized.

The best professor I've ever had. She gives out: extra credit, participation quizzes, practice questions, multiple practice exams for each unit, cheat sheets, FAQ's, annotated lectures, her YT channel and transcripts, a STUDY SCHEDULE, and keys to go with everything I just mentioned. Hilarious, laid back but caring. Exam grading is clear. TAKE HER.

analysis.name: Alissa Mrazek
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Mrazek was an amazing professor who clearly cares about her students and the topic. The class was easy but really engaging and helpful. However, you should only take it if you genuinely care about learning. There are two journal entries a week and attendance is really important to get a good grade.

Professor Mrazek is super nice and gives ample opportunities to build a relationship with students outside of class. Grade is based on attendance, daily quizzes, projects, and 2 exams. Daily quizzes are based off of the previous class lecture and homework which is a good refresher.Class starts with meditating and has a movement break in the middle.

Dr. Mrazek was the best professor I have ever had. She was so engaging, kind, and the content of the class changed my life. She does have a bit of a strict assignment deadline policy, but you have multiple drops and she gives you plenty of time for the bigger assignments. If I could take her class again I would do it in a heartbeat.

Dr. Mrazek has been one of my favorite professors at UT. This class has taught me multiple strategies to better my own mental health that I will continue to utilize for years to come. I felt such a sense of belonging in the class, and Dr. Mrazek makes sure there are opportunities for each student to connect with her personally.

Dr.Mrazek is one of the best professors at UT! The course is genuinely life changing and the professor is approachable and helpful!! LOVED this class!! Highly recommend. Workload is not bad and doable!!

analysis.name: Alexander Etz
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is easy, just make sure you attend the weekly labs and do the labs, case studies and prepare for the quizzes. Mona is an amazing TA, I'm not really good at coding and she helped a lot to understand the concepts and formulas. If you are able to take the class with her, take it.
The lectures honestly make the material kinda interesting and fun. Basically PSY 317 but I had a much easier time.

This class is all based on the TA you get. The only time you'll use the lectures are for the quizzes throughout the semester. Lab was easy as long as you followed along with the TA and I felt it was an overall easy A if you get a good TA.

How well you do in this class depends on your TA. The instructions for the final project components are not very clear, so I would go to office hours to ask for feedback before each part is due. If you make every correction your TA gives on the components, you will get a 100 on the final project. The labs are easy, just follow along with the TA.

Etz is a nice guy. I only gave him 4/5 because sometimes when I asked questions his answers were not very clear. But for the class, as long as you pay attention to the lectures you should be fine. The textbook is written by the old professor, Curly, who also does the lectures and I usually just did Command F during the weekly quizzes for help.

analysis.name: Dananjaya Appulage
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took Dr. Dan at ACC for Chem 2 Lab. He's very kind, wants you to succeed. Thick accent and speaks fast, so his lab lectures are a little hard to understand, but he is a generous grader. He will try his best to help direct you to the correct answer and even lets you redo work. Be cautious taking him for lecture, might be hard to understand content.

They removed my rating before, but I stand by what I said. This was the worst science professor I have ever had in 3 separate countries. He was rude, homophobic, spoke constantly and handed out papers during active exams, and treated his students as less than. 
This man shouldn't teach.

I went to every class. I aced every online quiz due to 2 attempts, and I aced every homework assignment. I stayed for 1:1s. I went to tutoring. I did group work nothing worked. I found the professor to be really hard to understand with his thick accent, but equally hard to understand his concepts when he broke it down and that becomes your problem.

I wish professor Dan used the board more. He is super chill and understanding but just goes through the course contents on the presentation. At the end of the semester, the presentation wasn't working and when he taught on the board, it was so much more informative. Great professor overall. Easy to get As if you invest enough time.

He cares about his students, offers flexible schedules, and inspires us to do our best. He shares his experiences, gives helpful advice and encourages questions if we don't understand. He's available during office hours and is passionate about learning. I'm glad I took chemistry with him. Amazing professor!

analysis.name: Brendan Apfeld
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Awesome Professor. Chill, young dude. Does not grade hard. If you actually do the assignments then you can expect an easy A in this class. There are 2 multi choice tests and a paper at the end of the semester. The paper is only 4 pages tho! I got a 90 and an 80 on the tests with only a few hours of studying for each. And a 95 on the paper.

Apfeld's class is fairly easy, though the tests are more difficult than you might expect. He makes occasional jokes and his videos that he plays during lectures are generally very entertaining, though the lectures themselves are sometimes boring. Attendance is not mandatory though your alternative is the most boring set of books put to print.

Took a risk taking a first-time teacher and it paid off. Very fair exams, fun assignments and great teacher. Glad I took him. Only con is the textbook sucks, but he said he hates it and won't use it again. The exams are fairly lectured based, but he puts the powerpoints online so its not life or death if you miss some classes!

I LOVED Apfeld! He really wants his students to do well. It's 25% midterm & 25% final (both curved), 25% a paper (he'll give you 100 if you check all the boxes he's looking for), and 25% a series of community engagement things (5 for 5% each). I was nervous about it but I was really glad he made us do them. He's a great guy and a good teacher!

I took a chance on Professor Apfeld. This was his first time teaching a college class so he had no reviews or anything. That said, this is a very talented young dude and a great teacher. Readings are long, but study (memorize) the lecture slides HARD for every quiz and test and you can get fairly easy 100's. It's April and I have a 99.3 average.

analysis.name: Jamie Aprile
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Completely unrealistic expectations! This is an Intro course and half or more of the students are non-majors and she expects everyone to memorize the what, where, when and significance of EVERY SINGLE artifact, building, and sculpture we have EVER SEEN in class or in the book. Absolutely ridiculous! This is like an UD Art History class! Do not take

She does read off a paper but that's because she is telling you the stories of mythology. If you think she is rambling then you aren't paying attention. It's not too much, but you have to write down EVERYTHING! Then reguritate it on the test and you will get an A. Sometimes I would have to read the book for discussion post but it was easy enough.

Very poor teacher. Reads off a sheet for the entire 50 min and mumbles her sentences. Worst of all, when I had her she designed her tests so that no one could finish (not even on purpose). She's new and I think she got flustered and didn't know how to conduct the class during those 4 days we missed because of the weather. AVOID

She is ridiculously passionate. Honestly, it really is a TON of information in only THREE tests, so there's a ton of studying needed for each test. That being said, people grumble about it being super hard, BUT it really isn't If you take decent lecture notes a ton of those too!) and read the SUMMARIES online, NOT the book. Study SMART. Easy A.

She was a really good professor. After a few classes though, the class (which comprised of 9 students) figured that we have to ask questions because she literally can talk non-stop for an hour straight. She used power points for her slide so there is at least some visual aids in the class. There will be a lot of reading though.

analysis.name: Amber Taylor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I can't say enough great things. Very caring and gives wonderful feedback. By far the most supportive and invested professor I have had. Her students are lucky to have her. Expect a well-structured class that you will really learn from.

Took for Rhetoric of City Streets. You get to choose a topic related to Austin that interests you to research for the whole semester. Most smaller assignments are completion pass/fail, with two large essays, and one final multimedia project. Definitely recommend!

I loved taking Rhetoric of City Streets with Professor Taylor so much that now every time a new course schedule comes out, I check for her name specifically to see if she's teaching a new class that I could take. There is writing, obviously, but she gives you plenty of class time to work on the projects and offers great, constructive feedback.

a true hidden gem for a writing flag. tookrhetoric of city streets with her and do not regret it. super flexible and caring and the class is actually very interesting. papers do tend to be on the heavier side, but taylor is always willing to help and grades leniantly. you also have a lot of opportunities for extra credit!

analysis.name: Amanda Garrett
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Assignment instructions can be ambiguous. Adds a lot of unnecessary assignments to the course that do not help enhance our knowledge or performance in lab. It seems like their purpose is to waste our time. The professor is very nice, and when she lectures, it is helpful. However, she only lectures for 10-15 minutes once a week.

W Prof Seminars always introduced to us new things for research/ECs. Lab quizzes were tricky as they tested on some random specific details in the protocol. My TAs were THE BEST (shout out to Janice and Tu-Quyen), always super helpful. Labs were longish, a lot of EC, PyMol project was fun, practical was light, a lot of busy work (my only complaint)

Dr. Garrett makes it very easy to succeed in this class, if you're willing to put in the effort. Certain weeks can be very assignment heavy (never more than 3-4hrs outside lab), but you always know what to expect and there's never any surprises. Canvas is organized very well, and Dr. Garrett/TAs are very kind/receptive w/ questions and feedback! :)

This class is well-organized and an easy A, but the workload for a 2 hr credit is considerable. Weekly reflection essays & PyMOL activities often took hours, plus there are weekly lab quizzes to study for and pre-lab assignments due. Labs are helpful but incredibly long. She offers lots of extra credit and drops your lowest quiz though.

Dr. Garrett is genuinely the most kind and caring professor I've had at UT. The course can have a heavy-ish workload if you leave everything to the last minute but the TAs are so understanding. So accessible outside of class if you have any questions about the major, career plans, etc!!

analysis.name: Amanda Koltz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Koltz and Wolf, along with the teaching team were nice and knowledgeable. The class itself wasn't bad, it's mainly memorization-based and exams are heavily graded. However, the class was harder than what I had expected it to be. There are a few projects that the TAs grade strictly on, and exams are a mix of MC and FRQ. Content is interesting!

Dr. Koltz and Dr. Wolf were great lecturers! The content was mostly memorization and the exams were not too difficult. The exams did take a long time to be graded and there are outside projects that are easy but you do have to still do them. Very interesting class and content overall and both professors were kind and understanding.

The content of this class is not TOO difficult, but the course structure is set up a lot harder than it needs to be. Grades are almost completely based on exams, and each exam is graded atleast a month after it's taken. Grades aren't posted until LAST minute. They mentioned a curve, didn't apply it. So stressful not knowing how you're doing.

Dr. Koltz was a great lecturer, and she and Dr. Wolf made sure to cover everything needed for each exam! It's mostly memorization, but as long as you stay on top of the content it's manageable. The discussion projects are also a good grade boost, just make sure to actually try on them.

I personally did not enjoy this class, I felt that the lectures weren't that intriguing. The grades are hidden throughout the semester so you can't see how you stand in the class, and assignments can take 2-3 weeks to return to you. At least there's no final. If you really like ecology then this class might be for you, but it wasn't for me.

analysis.name: Amy Liu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great UGS to take! The topic of the course was interesting and engaging. Dr. Liu is very kind and a good lecturer. The weekly quizzes are exactly what is covered in lecture, so if you take notes they will be very easy. There are multiple in-class essays, but they are pretty straightforward to prepare for and write. Gave extra points at the end.

Easiest UGS ever, the only negative thing was at 8am. Attendance is not mandatory, but quizzes are based on lectures which are not accessible outside of class so...you miss out a lot if you don't attend. My TA Meiying Xu was the sweetest person ever and I got 100s on all essays that I personally thought were very mid when I wrote them.

Dr. Amy Liu was a very good lecturer that kept her students entertained and intrigued throughout classes. The weekly discussion sections were also a great time to go over lecture materials and the quizzes often got content directly from the lectures so if you paid attention you were fine. She was very generous with her grading and often gave 100s.

Dr. Liu is an amazing professor! I took this class for the credit, but the content she covers is honestly really interesting. Write down what she says WORD FOR WORD during the lectures, because the quizzes are fully based on what she says. My TA graded a bit hard on the first essay, but after that you'll figure out her expectations for the essays.

Great UGS! Lectures and class content were extremely interesting, and weekly quizzes were almost rote what was taught in class.  Dr. Liu is also wonderful. She brought us breakfast burritos and pineapple bread to sweeten the 8 AM once! You will need to write 4 essays in class, but follow the rubric and you will be fine. No quiz makeups, but drops.

analysis.name: Amy Thompson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Easy class with clear grading expectations. Make sure to put effort into the weekly discussion posts, show up to section meetings, and go to most lectures because attendance is taken randomly. I wasn't super interested in this class but Professor Thompson did a good job teaching and I would definitely recommend her if you need to take this class.

One of the best classes I've taken. Only thing you have to worry about is your participation grade in the discussion sections since they weigh heavy. Most of the class work is made up weekly DBs over the topic of the week. Exams (2 total) are easy if you follow the review provided.  Keep track of deadlines, attend class and you should be fine.

Sweetest prof and truly cares about what she teaches + she's pretty quick to respond outside of class. There are short participation assignments at the end of lecture once in a while and the exams are really easy if you prepare (class Avg. ~90). Around 10 EC opportunities, each worth 0.5 pts for a max of 2.5 pts on your overall grade.

The professor is a great lecturer, and the class is pretty easy. Not a lot of homework, just reading and discussions. The worst part is that she takes attendance on random dates, so you really want to go to every lecture, and the discussion sections feel a bit useless to me. Overall, though, really good professor and class, 8.5/10
Very sweet, engaging lectures, comprehensive, kind. Reasonable with grading and assignments. This was a very good intro GRG class.

analysis.name: Amy Howard
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's very caring! There are three exams (40%) that are fill-in-the-blank. The rest of the class is composed of daily discussion boards at the end of lectures, a few in-class assignments, and a few outside-of-class papers. They are great buffers to the hard exams. If you put in the work, you will succeed (don't rely on the study guide, though).

She has been one of the kindest professors I've had. While the material can be challenging, if you pay attention and study, you will be fine. You can tell that she cares a lot about each student and wants to see everyone succeed, so utilize office hours if you need! She is also funny and very relatable, which makes class enjoyable.

She is super sweet and kind, as well as funny and relatable!! Class consists of 3 exams, the final one being cumulative; it's a lot of information given to you in lectures, so study well because the exams are the majority of the grade. There will be extra credit, I suggest doing all of them.

analysis.name: Amy Meeks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Meeks is a very good intro teacher; the class is very lecture-heavy, and you have to pay attention to succeed on the tests. She offers a lot of extra credit, but there is a lot of McGraw-Hill.

Dr. Meek is the sweetest lady ever! She treats her students like they're her children in a way. Anyways...she is very EASY! Tests are basically just like her powerpoints so reading the book is not really necessary but it does help. It was an easy A for me. I would reccomend her!
Had plenty of time to take notes by hand. She's adorable, and grades fairly. Show up, take notes, and you'll be sure to get an A+. Ended up with a 100 in the class.  Loved her.

I love all things psychology and I couldn't handle this class, it was so boring. You just went to class and filled in powerpoint slides she would give you, you also have to use a laptop because she goes way to quickly to take by hand. Her lectures go along with the book so if you don't go to class you can use that. She gives a lot of extra credit.

She was a  nice lady. The book is not necessary as the exams are mainly based off her PowerPoints. They're very straight-forward, so as long as you pay attention and read your notes a couple of times, you should EASILY get an A. Only issue about her is that her lectures usually ended late. She gives extra credit for papers and perfect attendance.

analysis.name: Andrew Weems
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Weems is a super funny and engaging lecturer. I can tell that he cares about the learning of his students. He really values teamwork in class so make sure you find good groupmates at the beginning of the year. The only criticism I have is that this class is a LOT. It has all the same coursework as advanced cell biology except with exams added.

Dr. Weems is truly passionate about cell biology! He is super funny, and will answer any question you have. Exams are open note. Discussion sections are extra credit, BUT they are super helpful if the TA continues to be AJ. There is a lot of material and readings, but I have truly learned a lot! He is super strict on deadlines so keep up.

Really funny guy, lectures were always interesting and easy to understand. A lot of the content was reading dependent, but it isn't anything super difficult to grasp. Great professor, take him for MBS 320 if you don't mind reading and writing every week.
He's a pretty solid prof with funny lectures. The tests are tricky but they're open note. Attendance is part of your grade

analysis.name: Sarah Angulo
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I LOVED this class! I looked forward to it each week, and Professor Angulo is so caring! The assignments and exams were straightforward, and our papers were always about interesting topics. I highly recommend this class! I love my small group in the class, and Isabella was an amazing TA this semester! Also, I loved the extra credit opportunities.

Take her if you can! Dr. Angulo genuinely cares about you and your success. She tailors course content to make it more relevant for students— her lectures are SO interesting. I didn't know anyone in this class but they all feel like family now. Exams are super fair if you attend lectures and read the textbook. Isabella was also the sweetest TA.

Dr. A made this class so enjoyable! And even though I had already learned a lot of the concepts, the class never felt boring to me. Lectures are team-based: the professor goes over the slides, and we break into teams to discuss them. Dr. A is so kind and knowledgeable, and I would highly recommend taking this class!

Amazing prof. Her lectures are super engaging and she is obviously very knowledgable about what she is teaching. There is so much extra credit and the exams are very easy if you read the textbook and use the study guides she posts.

Professor Angulo is straightforward when it comes to what to expect on tests. She provides detailed study guides and many of the questions come straight from lecture. PowerPoint slides aren't published online so I would recommend attending class regularly. She's approachable and very kind to her students. Would highly suggest taking her class!

analysis.name: Amanda Hager
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 128 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Hager is the best professor I had during my freshman year. There is a extra credit opportunity that is worth 1 % added to your final course grade by using Piazza frequently. On the last day of class, she gave us 2 points on our final exam just by showing up. She is an amazing lecture and really nice. There is HW due every week. I love her!!!!!!

Overall, very nice person and amazingly clear grading criteria. The first two exams are pretty close to each other and require a bit of work to understand, but she gives lots of materials to prepare. Towards the end of the class, homeworks felt more like busy work than anything, but still very helpful to studying for final. Would take again.

Amanda is by far the best professor in the math department. She is so nice and cares so much for her students. Her exams are not hard at all if you attend class and do your homework. Exams are quest based with a few free response questions. I took her for M305G AND M408N and it was a great experience. She's amazing.

Dr. Hager is the most involved professor I had during my time at UT. She is absolutely rooting for students to get an A in her class and makes it very possible to do so. Attendance is required once every week or so for the in person assignments, but I'd say to go as often as you can because she'll give hw answers in lecture!

She is my unicorn. Her lectures were always well prepared and easy to follow. I always felt comfortable asking my questions in class, and she was also accessible outside of class. I genuinely believe she cared about me, and she graded a lot of work with individualized comments, which I appreciated.

analysis.name: Drew Hays
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great prof! She includes diff activities/experiements during lecture to keep you engaged and she's knowledgeable and passionate abt food science. I'm not sure if this was j me tho, but she wasn't that accessible outside of class b/c she never responded to my emails, even those about accommodations

Professor Hays is a great professor and I enjoyed taking NTR 307 with her this semester. She is strict with attendance and uses squarecap, so if you miss class a lot, I wouldn't take this course. There is 1 major group project that she grades strictly. Outside of the project, there are 2 take home quizzes per week. Overall, I loved this class!

I had a passion for nutrition going into the course but she still had me so engaged. She taught a lot about critical thinking and scrutinizing diet culture. She is also a food scientist so she brings in some really interesting discourse about that as well. I really recommend that you take this class with her.

Ms. Hays is very knowledgable and can seem intimidating, but she just wants her students to do well. Go to class everyday, participate, take notes on the lecture slides she posts to Canvas, make flashcards, and you'll get an A. The textbook is helpful, and will be needed for the lab anyways. She can be a little grumpy, but overall a good professor.

Professor Hays was amazing! Although she may seem intimidating at first, you'll quickly see that she is a very good professor. The workload is minimal - as long as you read and pay attention in class, you will do fine! Few, easy assignments. Hays gives quick, to-the-point lectures and often lets class out early. Really enjoyed the class.

analysis.name: Aquasia Shaw
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
(-) Seems like a cool person ig but that's all I can say
(+) Terrible at letting us know if class was in-person or zoom. Bad at giving instructions for in-class assignments & knocked off points for instructions she never gave. Never posted slides or study guides despite exams being lecture heavy. Same as last years reviews, just overall, bad.

Worst class I have taken. It is EXTREMELY unorganized, does not follow the syllabus, gives major assignments with hardly any guidance, horrible communication, and tough grading. She never posted lecture slides. Not to mention she threw a dry erase marker across the room at a student for whispering with no previous warning. Awful class.

I feel bad giving her a poor rating, but I feel like there were a lot of things wrong with her class and teaching style. She didn't really teach us anything. She was more of a facilitator for our group projects while grading us unreasonably hard and giving little to no instruction. I feel like with time, she'll get better, but 355 was a disaster.

such a hard grader and her feedback makes 0 sense. She will take off 10+ points off of a paper for the SMALLEST thing and papers are a large percentage of your grade. assignments had absolutely no criteria or guidance. VERY political and I was afraid to speak out for the opposite position because she would've taken it out against me and my grade.

She is really disorganized and you really don't know your grade in the class until the end of the semester. The class does not follow the syllabus. She threw us into assignments and projects with little to no guidance and she grades harshly. Not a mean lady like the other comment claims, just really disorganized.

analysis.name: Andrea Pittard
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this ancient Rome class for my VAPA, and it is way more work than I was expecting. There are weekly lecture videos (~2 hours), Perusall comments every week, 2 essays, and 4 challenging tests. I would take a different course for VAPA credit if you can. But Pittard is super engaging and the content (even though it's a lot) is interesting.

You know that meme about men only thinking about the Roman empire? This is a great class for that. Jokes aside, she was a great grader and lecturer and the class being online allowed for much flexibility. Grades were quizzes and essays.
Took this class because I thought it was going to be an easy A, and I just found out the professor now switched to making exams 65 questions, monitored, and worth 40% of your grade. Not worth it.

This class is very manageable—just stay on top of lectures and readings. You'll write two papers, but they're easy if you pay attention. Homework mostly involves simple annotations based on short readings. The content is straightforward, though lecture-heavy so ensure to watch them. Great and easy way to earn VAPA credit!
Interesting content, but very time consuming. Spent longer working on this class each week than Physics 2.

analysis.name: Arjun Sobnack
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sobnack doesn't know what he's doing at all, ever. If he's as good at rock climbing as he is at teaching, he's a subpar climber at best. It is possible to do well because of the generous curve, especially if you've taken Calc BC before. He is so creative, he can make even the easiest topic seem impossible.

Sobnack does have super hard tests/quiz, mainly b/c he uses odd symbols and sometimes Q's are more theoretical than hard calculations (lot of proofs, Q's don't use numbers but symbols instead) You might be shocked by the first quiz, but literally trust the curve and you'll likely be ok. This class WILL make you smarter & I appreciate in retrospect.

Nice guy, but unable to communicate his knowledge of math to students. He kinda fixed this and started a curve (60->90). No recorded lectures. Practice sets weren't provided until the night before a quiz/exam, and often came w/o solutions & were unreflective of the exam. Homework is unreflective of exam. Graded only by tests, quizzes, and homework.

VERY difficult class to stay motivated in; NOT recommended if you're new to Calc 2. Very DIY w/ resources beyond lecture. It's you, Quest, & the textbook. Exam Qs are hard to understand & impossible to solve in time. Exams: 3 FRQs with 2-4 parts each. If you miss one, the next may be impossible. Nice Prof. Avoid or commit to a life of uncertainty.

chill guy but makes me want to kms so bad. genuinely got diddled by every quiz/test in this class. the in class examples are like not too bad but then the quiz and tests have GENIUNELY been dug out of the deepest depths of his bootyhole. he meekly chuckles and tries to be helpful. silly guy but AT WHAT COST. he also rock climbs which is pretty tuff

analysis.name: Arturo Jimenez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He cares very deeply about film and teaches it well. He also is slightly eviI. He has high expectations and tweaks if there's low engagement  He treats this as a weed-out class, forgetting that he actually teaches an INTRO class.

Arturo was a good professor. He kept the class engaged and did his best to encourage student participation. Students sometimes won't answer, and it'll make the atmosphere awkward at times, but other than that, as long as you have a good TA, you should be good. Be sure you take this class seriously and make work you're proud of.

Arturo is an okay professor! His lectures are often surface-level but sometimes he goes more in depth on some interesting industry topics like film festivals etc. He often seemed uninterested in teaching the class and like he hated it LOL but this class definitely does teach you vital things to go into film production. Just wish he dived deeper :/

Professor Jimenez is my favorite professor I've had so far! His lectures were so informative and helpful to get an intro understanding of the industry. 
He is so passionate about film, which might be his only flaw. It seems like he expects everyone to be as passionate as he is, which is understandable since he's teaching hundreds of film students.

Prof. Jimenez is extremely passionate about the film industry, sometimes to a fault. Lectures are informative and fun, but he will get verbally upset if students do not engage with his lecture/answer questions often enough. The 3 film projects are tough to organize but are graded fairly, and the TA's give lots of incredible feedback on your work.

analysis.name: Eugenio Arima
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Landscape Ecology grade consists of attendance, labs, exams, and project. I would recommend having experience with GIS before taking ANY class with him as he isn't the most patient with teaching GIS. He records lab sessions. He has clear instructions for assignments, and gives students a good idea of what is on exams, and is lenient with grading.

Excellent classes, relevant material and modern platforms for geoprocessing. Learned a lot. Weekly assignments were moderately challenging but easy enough to complete and helped reinforce concepts and techniques learned in class. Hands on experience using Python and ArcGIS, great experience for career in GIS.

Very knowledgeable professor but expected students to have some sort of background in GIS. Labs were not too difficult and course content was interesting. Didn't rely too much on the textbooks and exams were not too difficult.

Dr. Arima's lectures were very interesting although a coupleof the concepts are difficult to understand at first. He is very understanding and cares about his students, and he has a very funny sense of humor. The labs weren't too difficult but make sure to put time into the outside assignments and start studying for exams a couple days beforehand.

ENV-203 (intro GIS) was a joke. The labs are able to be completed in the lab period and as long as you studied for the midterm you're fine. ENV-310 (advanced GIS) is a whole different world. Not only is it WAY harder (exteremely hard) but the labs are long and hard. Lectures are kinda confusing but google helps. At least it has real world uses.

analysis.name: Maria Arredondo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Arredondo is the most kind and caring professor I have had throughout my time at UT. You can tell she truly cares about her students and has compassion for them as human beings! Her classes are easy and you actually learn useful things! Her lectures are engaging, lots of videos and activities! So fun! Take her classes!

Dr. Arredondo is incredibly kind and her lectures and tests are extremely easy and somewhat common sense. Her powerpoints are super easy to understand and help a lot with the tests. The grading distribution is very fair and you will without a doubt get an A, highly recommend her class!!

I had her this semester and I was scared because she had little reviews. However, she was so so sweet and literally will help you with anything. Super approachable as well. I didn't pay attention in class also 6 free absences and I studied the day or two before the exams and I did well on the exams. Memorization based exams mostly. Just take her!

I loved this class, the lectures were very interesting and interactive. The content wasn't hard to follow, very straightforward. Studied on the day of the exams and made an A on all of them. Just do your work and pay attention and you'll be fine.

I love Dr. Arredondo! The class is easy - just common sense with some extra detail.   All of the assignments had clear-cut grading criteria; if you ever have trouble, she and her TA were very helpful. Exams were simple as well, Quizlet was great for studying. Readings were assigned but I rarely did them.

analysis.name: Arielle Woznica
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of my favorite classes I've ever taken! She's a great lecturer and the material is interesting itself. Course is a bit more self driven because the grade is mostly exam heavy and homework/instapoll is completion, but she provides a lot of help if you seek it and she is constantly available. Exams are fair, and she offers a bit of extra credit.

Really great professor, it's obvious she's very passionate about cell biology and as long as you keep up with the material throughout the semester you will do fine. Super knowledgable and very approachable outside class. There's a big emphasis on designing experiments that demonstrate cellular processes so the class isn't just brute memorization

Taught cell biology in a cool way. You need to go to class to do well, attendance isn't "mandatory" but it probably is in order to be prepared for exams. Very accessible outside of class and was always willing to explain things in class and not make you feel silly.

analysis.name: Arianna Avalle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Avalle had been my all time favorite professor. Throughout the semester, she not only wanted me to succeed, but she went out of her way to make sure that I understood the material. She was very reachable outside of class and during office hours. I cannot say enough nice things about her. Often, she brought homemade treats to class.

I noticed that one of the reviews stated that Professor Avalle “tries too hard to be liked”. This is actually a positive! Professor Avalle goes out of her way to get to know the needs and ambitions of each individual student. She always tries to form a bond with each of her students and it is evident that she deeply cares!

I would definitely take intro to Italian with Arianna again if given the chance, she is such a kind professor and understanding! You can tell she has a passion for what she does, I really enjoyed this class despite having zero previous Italian knowledge. I found that the class flowed nicely and modules were easy to follow! 10/10 recommend beginners

analysis.name: Ashley Green
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's passionate and very well-versed in conservation, but in turn means she's a harsh grader. Will take off points for grammar, formatting, punctuation, etc. Also a very slow grader; did not start receiving grades til the start of March (mid-sem). Expect to do a homework assignment due before every class. Exams are FRQ heavy.

this course felt like so much work. Always hard to find big project assignment instructions on canvas. disorganized. Very harsh grader. Curriculum is very interesting! Good lecturer, not much class interaction.

I genuinely struggled trying to get myself to show up to this class. I was excited to take ecology but it was nothing like I expected. She didn't give us anything to prepare for exams. This class was so much harder than it needed to be & very unorganized. It was disheartening because I've heard other 373 classes are so much easier. Not an easy A

She knows her stuff and loves her field, but she does not know how to teach. The entire class is her lecturing at students, making it difficult to stay engaged. Students often slept while she lectured lol. Three exams and no drops, so if you bomb the first exam (our class average was a 69!), there's no way of getting an A. Very discouraging.

Class was interesting honestly. It felt like she was learning content for the first time with us, and honestly lots of what was on the slides was very surface-level. Exams were odd, and she refuses to give practice problems otherwise she's "giving us the answers". Not the worst professor ever, but I expected better.

analysis.name: Astrid Runggaldier
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I have never felt so disrespected or afraid of a professor in my entire life. I genuinely dread going to class and facing her wrath and I am a good, dedicated student. I do NOT recommend taking a course with her. She's not blunt, she's demeaning. Does not shy away from humiliating students, so the discussions are usually silent out of pure fear.

I accidentally took an upper-division art history class as a freshman, so this class was a bit tough for me. Dr. Runggaldier is pretty vague in her directions and I received some pretty poor grades because of misinterpretations. She uses lecture slides but they don't have text on them, just photos, so it's not really helpful for exam reviewing.

She obviously is very knowledgeable in her field; her class is reading, and lecture heavy. The majority of your grade is dependent on a multi-part project throughout the semester, and if you are not accustomed to writing for art it can be a learning curve, if you are thinking about this class for your VAPA I would recommend something easier.

This professor is a very harsh grader. EOY project is worth so much, but she has never given anybody a 100 on a single section of the project that was submitted (I checked the Canvas median). The tests aren't that hard, but what kills is you are the essays that are apparently "never perfect". Please don't take if you scared of getting a A- or B+.

AMAZING PROF!! Best choice I could have made for first semester VAPA. She cares about student understanding of the material and constantly asks for feedback. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll have to attend every lecture and read the textbook to do well. Material is incredibly interesting and she makes lectures engaging. Would take again!

analysis.name: Ashley Matheny
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr Matheny is the sweetest professor and really cares about her students. She tells you pretty much exactly what is on the exams. Two midterms and a semester project, easy peasy. She moves due dates if she feels her students are too busy. Great lecturer as well, definitely recommend!

Dr. Matheny is an incredible professor! I thoroughly enjoyed taking her Intro to Hydro course. Although I got a B, I would absolutely take another class with her, as my B was due to my own personal issues. She was very helpful and understanding, and her lectures were entertaining even online. You can tell she is very passionate and knowledgeable.

Dr. Matheny is a great professor. She is easy to listen to, and makes her lectures interesting. The class isn't super hard, as long as you pay attention during lecture. Assignments were always graded quickly and fairly, and she is super accommodating if you need anything. Would definitely recommend taking any of her class, she is such a gem!

I loved this course and Dr. Matheny. She worked with students to make sure that everything was fair, assignments were graded within a week (usually within a few days), and she is just such a fun person. Definitely one of my absolute favorite professors. You can really tell that she cares about her students over grading

Amazing lecturer and always ready to help everyone understand anything, inside or outside of the classroom. Gives lots of examples for 'real life' career/scientist skills. Creates a community feeling around projects and research! Would definitely take her class again!

analysis.name: Ashley  Moran
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Moran is awesome, very knowledgeable in her field, and cares about her students. Participate in class discussions, as she keeps a very close eye on who talks and uses that to determine participation grades. Tests are short answer questions that aren't hard if you pay attention in class. The readings will help but you don't NEED them to pass.
She is a very caring professor, but the class it pretty content heavy and tests can be tough. You definitely have to do the readings and work hard.
Kindest professor ever! Easy, fair grader and very caring of her students. The content is very interesting and presented in a way that is easy to understand and remember. Would recommend!

One of the best Professors I have ever had. She genuinely cares about the content and her students and is an amazing lecturer. Weekly discussion posts over assigned readings are due every Sunday but are mostly completion grades and cover material discussed in the following lectures. I've never retained so much from a class I loved it!

Professor Moran is a great professor who is extremely knowledgeable about the course content. There are lots of dense readings every week to get through and a weekly reaction discussion post. Lectures can be a bit slow at times, but the course is super interesting and enjoyable. Professor Moran is very helpful and wants you to succeed!

analysis.name: Ashley Coleman Taylor
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Taylor was very organized and clear on her expectations. Was graded on 4 short papers (1 page or so), a video, and a reply video. As long as you read the assignment in detail and hit each point, you will succeed.

Dr. Coleman Taylor is an exemplary educator. She embodies a pedagogical ethos that is in alignment with the intersectional feminist theory she teaches. She treats students as people first, which can be rare to find at the university level. Her feedback is insightful and she challenges you to always dig deeper. You will leave class a different you.

THE BEST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD! It was an honor to be taught by Dr. Coleman Taylor. She teaches a thought-provoking, inclusive curriculum that expands upon typical cis, white, male narratives She is also incredibly knowledgeable, often invites amazing guest speakers, and truly cares about her students. I highly recommend her classes.
Very little details or feedback and she doesn't keep up with grades so you never know where you stand in the class. I was scared to speak up in class because she could be very condescending.

analysis.name: Ash D'Harcourt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was fun and engaging. The way Prof Ash structured and paced the course was intuitive and low-stakes, allowing you to focus on the content without stressing about your grade. Grading was very fair, and the TAs consistently provided helpful feedback.
rtf308 is so easy and the TAs are pretty lenient on grading!! be prepared to write essays but other than that its a great vapa

This class was low stress and taught in a way that made it a great intro to going to college. The lectures were all genuinely amusing, and the asynchronous format was really accommodating. The exams were open note and easy as long as you took good notes from the lectures, and the grading criteria for the writing assignments was incredibly clear.

I loved Ash's class! Ten out of ten - one of the sweetest profs I've had at UT. There were at least 10x during the semester that I laughed out loud at a joke they cracked during lecture. Super entertaining to listen to and the lectures were pre-recorded which was great for my full schedule. You can tell they really care about their students.

I love Ash!! Such an incredible professor who really cares about their students. They were always super responsive to emails and there were at least 10x during the semester that I laughed out loud at something funny they said in the lecture. TAKE ASH'S CLASS!! It's asynchronous online, so watch the pre-recorded lectures whenever in the week.

analysis.name: Lucy Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: No tests, we don't even take notes in class. Just come and listen and engage in the lecture, and you're all good. Homework and projects outside of class aren't too bad either. Definitely take her if you can.

They fell kind of behind so felt like everything was pushed back at last second but outside of that the professor is nice but this class was just a class I decided to take outside of my major so any grade I may have gotten because of that is on me.

The sweetest professor ever, take this class!!! Her class is so laid back and chill. Assignments are simple and easy, projects are also very straightforward. This class is a relief and I actually learned a lot.
0 extra credit. Will give an A- if 0.1 decimals off an A

As an engineering major, this was a nice class. laid back, discussion based. Just do your part in group projects and keep up with assignments. Dr. Atkinson (who prefers Lucy) is witty and engaging with her lectures. Breath of fresh air.

analysis.name: ATILA NOVOSELAC
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Only thing I disliked about the class was the enormous 1" = 1' model we had to make, which cost like $100 (divided by 5 people). Other than that, the class was chill and easy with cool speakers.

Professor Novoselac is an outstanding introduction to architectural engineering. He is extremely knowledgeable, friendly, understanding, and very approachable. The guest lecture panels throughout the course were especially useful. One time, when our projects were accidentally thrown away by a janitor, he even bought the entire class Ferrero Rocher!

Professor Novoselac is a very nice person, and he tried to help all of us navigate the beginnings of ARE. The guest lecturers were interesting. Sometimes the material was disorganized. The group project took a long time to complete, so think ahead for that. Very nice beginning to Architectural Engineering for me!

This is a great guy. Super chill and easiest class I've taken. Tests are all open book/open note, project 1 was a little tedious but everything else was super easy. Even though this class was really chill, I think I got a lot out of the guest speakers. Take advantage of the opportunity to learn in this class!!

Lectures included guest speakers who has slides we would take notes on. Notes would be turned in at the end of the year (I love that he made us take notes because I could not tell you one thing a presenter said from the top of my head but it was useful ArchE stuff). Group project was somewhat hard, but office hours helped and buy materials aheaddd.

analysis.name: Athanasio Papalexandrou
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The prof is great but the older reviews exaggerate how easy the class is- you need to work for an A. Lectures are recorded & there are mandatory labs w/ weekly response papers (completion grade). TAs grade the first exam harshly, and you need to rewatch the lectures and pay attention to catch the details they want you to mention on exams

Definitely not as easy as the previous reviews have claimed, but the class was doable. T/F and MCQs felt like random trivia questions at times, but the writing portions were easy as long as you keep up with lectures and discussion sessions. Grading varies by TA, mine graded harshly initially but became more lenient as the semester progressed.

You can tell he really cares about what he teaches, he's passionate and that makes lectures interesting. There is a lot of reading needed for the class and the lab but it's very manageable if you're good at writing. The workload is light! I very much recommend the class, you don't need to go to the lectures as long as you watch them online.

Took two semesters of his art history classes. Easy grading; wrote a terrible-quality paper and still got a B on it. Incredibly kind and genuinely wants to get to know his students. Very thick accent that is both endearing and a bit hard to understand. He is super passionate about the subject, which helps if you are not interested in art.

Such a cute prof. Kind of funny, referred to Augustus of Prima Porta as incredibly sexy. Was absent one day, and came to office hours once and he spent the entire time going over the presentation. Caring prof. Greek accent takes a while to get used to. ATTEND LECTURES!!! Grading is P/F for lab questions and from tests. No final either.

analysis.name: Wang Atlas
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall this was a really great class. Prof posts all of his slides with the concepts very clearly described. Wasn't the best lecturer imo but going to lecture isn't necessary to gain a lot from the class. Homeworks and final project took a lot of time, but overall were worth it.

Professor Wang is a true legend and perhaps the smartest person I've ever encountered. 

Unlike many professors who just read textbooks, he teaches effortlessly from his vast knowledge. He's engaging, incredibly kind, and adaptable, always happy to take questions and meet student needs. 

Such a pity UT cannot keep him teaching longer!
