Besides the fact that he is one of the best researchers in his field, Prof. Wang is also a great teacher! He has very well-organized lectures and is a grandmaster describing the intuition of the material.
Lectures are fun. The class is not all that difficult, but Prof. Wang does go in depth in lectures and is very willing to dive deep into specific things the class asks.

analysis.name: Nigel Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Do not take Atkinson. His lectures are so convoluted that you can easily get confused even if you already understand the material from the textbook. You have to decipher what his tests are asking and you probably won't pass unless you memorize the whole book or have his old exams. Thankfully I had a wonderful TA so that's the only reason I passed.

Neuroepigenetics- This is a hard class but if you do the homework and the study guides (which are basically the tests), an A is very achievable. He is very knowledgeable but a little hard to understand, will clarify when asked. We had 2 group poster projects that are worth as much as the test, and are easy to get an A for if you follow the rubric.

Hard class. If you can read for yourself and understand the material, you can get an A. The tests are difficult. He doesn't add anything to his lectures, so it is almost pointless to go; it'd be better to just spend that time reading the book. Half of the test question are from old homeworks/old tests and the other half are new.

CONS:
The epigenetics class was: VERY DISORGANIZED, had no clear rubric/expectations, and the grades were returned WEEKS later. It is PROJECT HEAVY ( 4 presentations and a Wikipedia article). 
PROS:
He grades presentations/ article relative to others/yourself/ and level of effort. The practice exams ARE the exams (still hard though). An A is doable

He is a nice guy, but his lectures are painfully boring. His tests are difficult, and he writes them aiming for a 70-72 average. He does not curve or use plus/ minus grading. The class was disorganized and the expectations were unclear. You pretty much learn from your book and TA. I consider myself a strong bio student, but struggled in this class.

analysis.name: Mihran Aroian
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 166 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment:
The workload is so much for a 3 credit class that it's borderline disrespectful to students. 
I had a 6 credit class with the same amount of homework, if not less. I will lose my scholarship if I drop it but if I could go back and not take it, I would 100% avoid it.

This class was the most annoyingly difficult course I've taken. Not because the material is difficult to understand, but because the exams are near impossible due to the sheer amount of detail and random topics included from a vast amount of readings, articles, case studies, and slow/long/boring debriefing/lecture videos. DON'T take this class!
I got 60 points taken often for not writing my name, are you serious?? dude needs to get laid. please do not take this class, like run rn. literally take any  other class.

Currently in his class and he is easily the worst professor I have ever had at UT. Has the highest materials fee of any professor ($150) and gives way too many assignments and homework for a 3 credit class. I have a 4 credit class with less homework than his. Dude is so paranoid about cheating he mentions it in every single paragraph and assignment

The most expensive, time-consuming, and confusing class I've taken here at UT. The exams are heavily opinion-based, and the course content is relatively easy. The issue lies in how the course is structured, how things are graded, and how the lectures and exams don't align in any sense.

analysis.name: Lucinda Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures are really helpful and easy to understand. She is engaging and gives you bonus questions that are super easy if you came to class!

Dr. Lucy is the BEST! She makes the lectures interesting and provides plenty of in-class extra credit. You do have to read the books for the tests, but luckily they're pretty interesting. She really enjoys discussions too, sometimes we would get so busy discussing in class that we would end up having to cut information off of the tests!

This class was okay. It definitely was not hard by any means but i will say there is a lot of work you need to do. Each module takes an hour to two hours to complete so it definitely sucked doing those but most of the stuff is things you will see on the exam. I read the textbook sometimes but mostly never and still got an A.

I loved this class and i loved her as a professor. She makes the class fun and easy to understand. Also the tests were easy as long as you read your notes and sometimes textbook. Attendance not mandatory but the bonus questions were based on class lectures. it was an easy A.

I'm not a business major, was thrown into this class (since another was cancelled 2 days before classes started) but could not be happier. She really kept this class interesting and fun, and gave plenty of opportunities to succeed. Read the book, take good notes, and you'll get an A+, and you'll actually enjoy yourself. Favorite professor so far!

analysis.name: Rowland Atiase
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Atiase is by far my least favorite professor I have ever taken. His sarcastic attempts at humor seem to demean students more often than encourage or amuse them. You come to class to copy down verbal notes which could be posted online instead. Homework is explained, in a confusing, hard to understand manner, leaving you to learn on your own.

This class consists of you doing a ton of reading and written homework/handouts before class (at least 2 hrs for each "lecture"), coming to class to copy notes verbatim that he won't post online, and then getting called on to answer the questions you did before class without a good explanation. You have to teach yourself--just avoid altogether

Don't do it! Claims that he doesn't give us busy work, but that is all he gives us. Teaches too fast, and has the audacity to call exams "parties". He is a very smart guy, as he's worked at some very high up companies in the world, but teaching just isn't his thing. Avoid him at all costs please, unless you are feeling like a risk-taker.

Prof Atiase may not be my favorite professor ever, but he definitely is not as bad as the other reviews here make him out to be. There is a lot of written homework due before each class, but it is completion and he just wants you to attempt it before actually seeing the solutions in class. Tests are very similar to the review problems which is nice

Homework structure supports memorization, not learning. Lectures are worthless fill-in-the-blank notes that he reads from. He either assigns busy work or problems that he has not prepared you to complete. Hard to understand due to accent. Only reason I did okay was bc his test was near identical to the review. Lots of wasted time in class. ACC 312H

analysis.name: Florence Atiase
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is pretty tough and not just because of the subject matter. It's how she grades. I really wish I took this class with a different professor! Avoid, if you can.
Sometimes hard to understand and hard to follow in lectures. Also, very uninteresting to listen to because of the way she teaches
Her class was very difficult but she did a great job of making difficult material more easy to understand.
A very good professor, helpful, good explanations.

analysis.name: Luis Aviles
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took his beginner level (6week long) Spanish course and was forced to pay 62$ for a program to do work that wasn't even graded. Yet he expected everyone to finish (literally) 12 assignments every day. His lectures were unfocused, and I spent most of my time in breakout rooms w peers. Despite him saying he cared it was abundantly clear he didn't.

The quizzes were a little tricky but he really offers a lot of content to study for both exams and quizzes, and makes class really fun to go to. He engages with each student and genuinely cares for each person's wellbeing. Most fun I've had taking a class in college for a long time, and I will miss this prof

I took SPN 314 with Prof Aviles in summer 2021, and I really enjoyed it. He is super enthusiastic and helpful, and he really cares about the students' learning. There was a lot of homework because it was a summer class, but it wasn't too challenging. Overall, it was a great course and I highly recommend taking it with Prof Aviles!

analysis.name: Avigail Noy
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've had. The content was phenomenal and she is such a kind professor. It is reading heavy and discussion based so make sure to read or at least skim. No tests however there are 4 written assignments and weekly journals, but so far they have not given me any issue and 2 of the papers are only 2 pages long.

Took Arabic Lit. Highly difficult class yet rewarding -- you learn a lot! Readings are super difficult. Noy's lectures are amazing and she is easy to reach outside of class and understanding. PLEASE CONTRIBUTE IN THIS CLASS. It's small and discussion based, don't take it if you're not ready to talk. DO THE READINGS, she likes to see effort!

I took her arabian nights class, and really loved it. the class is interesting, and Noy is very knowledgeable. she is a hard grader, however, and sometimes frustratingly so -- a few times i thought about throwing my computer out the window. LOTS of reading. too much. not burdensome, though. overall, id recommend for people interested.

analysis.name: Ronen Avraham
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Uses Socratic method to a fault, basically to have students teach for him. Grades are completely arbitrary and he provides no feedback. I received high A's on all homework papers (no feedback provided), and this was completely inconsistent with the final grade. He spent half a class arguing he should be allowed to buy votes. Not approachable.
Prof. Avraham is really sweet and loves torts.  He explains a lot of things at a level even a 5 year old could understand. Some other readings were hard to understand.  Overall, highly recommended.
Avraham is funny and makes class enjoyable.  I had him for Torts. He really covers everything he wants you to know during class, so don't miss class!

analysis.name: Aurora Wallace
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a new professor at UT but friendly. Lectures are straightforward. Homeworks are short. She offers plenty of support if you're confused. Participation work is required on Mondays, but she gives makeups for it. Exams closely follow the practice materials and HW, though they can get tricky—especially the final. Highly recommend!

Really great experience taking her for Probability 1. Explains everything very clearly and tests are pretty easy as long as you are familiar with the material. Gives a lot of really good prep material for the tests too.

She TRULY cares about whether or not her students understand the material. She checks in to make sure we understand what she is saying throughout the lecture and advocates for lots of practice tests. Genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had, you should definitely take her class!

Best math teacher I've ever had. I took her for calc one and for lectures you would read the textbook before class and then complete a really short online assignment. The weekly homework load was very manageable. subject was explained very well and always answered questions.

The course content itself is incredibly easy. If you get stuck, she is very helpful over email/office hours. I did very well on the HWs and midterms, but I just barely got an A bc of the final, which is weighted 30%. In-class activities once a week for a participation grade. Handwriting is a bit difficult to read at times.

analysis.name: Michael Aubrey
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I don't think Dr. Aubrey should be teaching Gen Chem 2. His quizzes are hard and you can't study for them because he puts a harder version of the example that you have never seen, he makes mistakes that have to be corrected by students. He doesn't explain things during lecture and expects us to know a lot (we are 2nd semester first-year students).

He does seem very sweet, and I can tell he's trying, but for the portion I was there for (electrochemistry) I genuinely never had any clue what was going on during class. I felt like he was just saying things, but I could never follow the lecture. I did manage to do well on the first exam somehow, but honestly try for another professor if possible.

Really sweet guy, but like other reviews said he kind of struggles with lecturing in a clear, easy-to-understand way if you don't already know the subject material. It's clear he knows a lot about what he's teaching, but you'll definitely need to study outside of class. Overall a pretty average class experience.

This class is recommended for the chemistry major/honors track and so most of us thought we had to take it, but you do not have to! Dr. Aubrey is one of those guys that are just way too smart to be teaching intro to gen chem. Because he is so smart he does not explain nor teach very well. He is not a good teacher, but he is nice, I don't recommend.

He really like students to engage in real applications that can be used to show to future recruiters. We made our own Google app. Labs are easy but tests were tricky. Overall, Aziz is awesome.

The lectures slightly boring but the labs are interesting.  I did minimal studying for the tests and make high B's.  Aziz is very helpful during office hours.  During class he often makes careless mistakes during examples, but usually is quick to catch them.  Overall good professor for this class. I would recommend taking him.
One of the worst professor's at UT. Teaches about software and tools that he himself does not know. Recommend not to take this course.

analysis.name: Hina Azam
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very difficult and time consuming class, but not impossible. Attendance and participation are required. Daily 6 question open ended book quiz's. Very strict grader but revisions on papers are allowed. So is 6% of extra credit. She's very passionate about this course and a sweet person but I did not enjoy taking this class.

The class is very hefty and for a UGS there is an unnecessary heavy workload. The professors and TA's are very nit-picky graders and most of the time their comments and feedback is not helpful. The books/content is interesting but the class if fast paced and your work is graded slowly. I would not recommend this class.

This class is unnecessarily overdesigned and beyond disorganized. There is an unnecessary amount of assignments that serve no purpose but to lower your grade. It would be okay if the feedback was helpful and the assignments were graded fairly, but critiques were ambiguous, and points were deducted for small mistakes, which became very discouraging.

I do not recommend Dr. Azam. She assigns 3 500 page books in your first semester of college. While you are learning to be a successful student she grades harsh and does not give leeway. I also find the content unrepresentative of an accurate intro to Islam and can give students the wrong point of view of what the religion is.
Just don't take. No reason for a UGS to be sinking your GPA as bad as this. No matter what you do it won't be right. Absurd grading. Poorly organized. Save yourself the sanity

analysis.name: Bartholomew Sparrow
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Sparrow can be pretty intimidating and blunt but in a good way. That said, as the semester went on, it became more and more clear that he genuinely cares for his students. The class games are really fun if you're into history, roleplay, strategy, and giving speeches. NO TECH! Would recommend.

As some of the other reviews will tell you, Dr. Sparrow can be pretty intimidating and blunt. That said, as the semester went on, it became more and more clear that he genuinely cares for his students. The class games are really fun if you're into history, roleplay, strategy, and giving speeches. Otherwise... it may be rough. Also NO TECH!

Had Sparrow for Rethinking the Founding UGS where we role played historical events in some weird game? We were graded on whether we won the game or not, and had to give speeches and act in character. One of my characters was Native American and I was not allowed notes for my speeches bc I was supposed to be illiterate. Lowkey fun but frustrating.

Overall, the class is fairly easy if you keep up with the readings and pay attention. However, the grading criteria for almost all of the assignments/projects are really vague with little to no clarification given. He can also catch an attitude and it makes class feel awkward sometimes. Not the worst class I've ever taken, but not the best either.

He was very critical of so many things, his expectations & rubrics were never clear. This course is all over the place. It was fun somedays just he was like not...also VERY ANTI-TECH, never used canvas...How I got an A....IDK

analysis.name: Barbara Chisholm
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: an easy class but sitting a room for 1.5 hours with this professor will drain you. if you arent a theatre kid or its a required course dont take this class. shes super obnoxious when you have questions and she doesnt really give clear instructions for material. she also talks about her personal life way too much and trauma dumps about her career.
really fun professor and helped me ease into college as a freshman. classes develop a sense of community within peers and the professor. overall really fun and great class

Took this class as an elective so I can fill my schedule & I'm SO glad I did. Barbara is very sweet and funny and has been one of my favorite professors at UT by far. Attendance is mandatory (you can only miss 2 classes unexcused) but don't worry bc you won't want to skip. TD 303 definitely helps break out of your shell & interact with classmates.

I took this class to fulfill one of my elective requirements as a senior. The assignments are easy as long as you get memorized, and there is definitely a sense of community within the class, as everyone is new to acting. Attendance is a huge part of the grade, but Barbara is easy to reach outside of class if you really need to skip for any reason!

One of the most fun classes I have ever taken in my academic career. There are 3 assignments where there are lines to memorize throughout the course, the first 2 are collaborative and the last one is a monologue. Nothing difficult to memorize at all. The class is small and meets so frequently that there is def a sense of community at the end. 10/10

analysis.name: Ben Bays
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bays is probably one of the most caring professors here at UT. Comics & Cartoons was such a fun and relaxing VAPA, and he often brought snacks for us and comic books to look at. His point system is super easy, so many people finished most of the class pretty early on. I loved coming to his lectures even if I was completed with my points!

I took RTF 347C: Business of Video Games, and I gotta say, this was the most fun RTF class I've ever taken at UT. He does post a lot of different class assignments, but you don't necessarily need to do all of them since the grading scale for this class is points-based. A score of 95 points is all that you need to earn an A in this class.
This specific class is basically create digital media and you get maximum credit. It's really cool to be able to create things as an elective without any strict rules, would definitely recommend!

Took him for comics and cartoons as my VAPA and it was beyond easy. All assignments are fun little drawings and are not graded on quality. Ben is a SUPER caring guy and loves what he does and who he teaches. I will miss this class every day.

Awesome Professor! Plenty of extra credit, super easy class for upper division credit. Take his class, you won't regret it. He is very kind and supportive. He patiently reviews almost all of the assignments.

analysis.name: Sanjay Banerjee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Excellent professor. Clearly explains complex topics. Great office hours though not overly accessible. HW is nothing too extreme and prepares ok for exams. Exams are hard but curved to the moon (including final exam and final grade). Previous review stating class is based off reading textbook and coming in with questions is incorrect.

Prof gives pretty fair exams, but they're graded very hard. Lectures are pretty bad, but textbook and hw are good to teach all the necessary contents for the 2 exams. Probably your best bet for solid state given the grade distribution for the other profs are not good
Good course and very doable if you attend class.

He makes solid state a doable class. He explains concepts clearly and answers questions well. Attending class is important because he does tell you what concepts will and will not be tested on. Tests are somewhat similar to home works. Conceptually this is a difficult class. However, Banerjee is a liberal grader. 45 is B, 65 A.

Overall a great and caring prof. His lectures are pretty dense and goes quickly through the material, but if you go to OH he is willing to help clear up any misunderstandings you have. THE TEXTBOOK IS KEY, read and go through EOC problems and you'll do well on the exams as they are similar in style. Tough test grader but lenient on grading (75~A).

analysis.name: ETHEL BAYER SANTOS
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are hard to understand- but the exercises that she provides for the exams are extremely helpful- and I don't see how anyone wouldn't get an A in this class. Use your resources and you'll be fine. She likes open discussion, so will try to get you to talk during classes. She is sweet, and cares a lot about the subject.

Unfortunately I didn't have a great time in this class, mostly due to the lectures. The powerpoints were somehow both overly complex and vague at the same time, and I ended up using the textbook to understand many of the topics we had to cover. Exams were fine though, but I wouldn't be surprised if she changes things up in the future.

Unfortunately, my experience with Dr. Santos disappointing. The course lacked clear guidance and structure, making it difficult for students to understand expectations or succeed. Opportunities for meaningful feedback and support were minimal, and most times, the instructor's tone felt discouraging rather than constructive. Avoid if possible.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Mayne
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Truly cares to make class engaging. Kind and excited about French! Fantastic lecturer and fun exercises to really make you practice. The work is not too bad. Her outfits are always fun and attitude happy. Sometimes she can not pay attention to the time during class, so we get out late or rush a quiz. However its a great class and I recommend her.

An excellent, caring, and loving professor. She just wants the best for her students & truly loves the French language and culture. Most meetings consisted of us talking to our peers in French and then working as a class to learn something new. Lots of extra credit if you go to OH, exams are pretty easy. Pretty lenient grading, just do your work.
The format of this class really ensures that you have lots of participation time -- my french speaking skills improved so much. Liz is funny and made this class a blast!
I think the last person who left the review put a 1 for quality on accident. Great professor who cares about her students, fun class tbh.

analysis.name: Sheryl Beach
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Beach was an incredible professor. I thought the lectures followed the textbook too much, so there was no reason to take notes on the lectures and the textbook, just follow one. I found the lectures to be informative, sometimes I got bored, that's not on the professor, though. What is taught in lecture will be on the exam so focus!

Professor Beach is a fine professor and seems very passionate about research in her field. This class is easily approachable if you have taken some other stats classes but is probably not worth it if not. Lectures are pretty boring but she is forgiving, lenient, and overall a nice person. Labs are pretty easy but exams were a little too dense also.

She is a nice professor, but there are LOTS of readings give to you every week. You have to read these textbooks and readings for the short answer/essay questions on the exams. Unless you already have a good knowledge in this field, I would not recommend you taking her class as this class takes too much of your time.

Slow, boring, intro level course. The final was too long and like only one person in the room finished it in the time allotted. She's really kind and seems very approachable, but honestly if you can help it, don't take this class at all. 
She's allegedly very passionate about water quality, but I didn't see any passion in this course.

Not only are the lectures unbearably boring, but they often skim information in a way that doesn't even match up with what's on the exam. Certain exam questions are purposely made to be confusing, like using interchangeable words for a process as options with a definition that doesn't even match the terms used in book. Doesn't care about you at all

analysis.name: Elizabeth Cullingford
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's so cool! She's retiring, so this review probably won't be used by anyone, but I still want to let everyone know what a great professor she is. Very interesting lectures, and knows her stuff about Shakespeare. She's very straightforward and can be a bit surprising, but it's endearing.

Prof. Cullingford is by far my favorite professor! She truly cares about her students and is passionate about the subject material. There is a fair amount of reading, but that's almost the only homework and you do not have to be thorough to participate in class. Her essays are short with revisions and there are lots of completion grades.

Our class time was discussion-based and we were graded solely on writing. Professor Cullingford gives a lot of feedback, and tends to be pretty blunt, but she improved my writing immensely. Take time to get to know her, and go to office hours- she is so interesting and will openly offer advice. She is the kind of professor who wants you to succeed!

Dr. Cullingford has a vast array of knowledge that is admirable & interesting to listen to.  Sometimes, her behavior acted like that of a Shakespeare purist (unable to receive criticism against Shakespeare that addressed his sexism, racism, etc).  Very difficult grader whose numerous vague comments for feedback could almost be perceived as rude.

There is a reason for Prof Cullingford's 5/5. She is so caring and funny to her students. She was very understanding during covid and made sure to make us feel comfortable. Very detailed feedback on essays. She gave us a chance to revise both essays and recorded the average of our revision and the original. Hard to get a high A on essays.

analysis.name: Beatriz Schleppe
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, she has been great to have this semester. She is so understanding, caring, and engages with her students. She does give a lot of homework, but that's normal for a language course since it's worth a lot of credits. She is strict on grammar, but I really love that because it helps improve a lot. There is no required textbook. Recommend 100%

Ok to be fair I took this class when writing flags were mandatory so idk how the material will change, but I loved Mme Schleppe, she's witty and caring, and really wants you to just learn the language. This class really helped me deepen my understanding of the french language and encourage me to continue learning french.

I love Madame Schleppe! She is a great professor and so funny. The class is pretty fast-paced. However, that is expected from an advanced language class. She sets up all the assignments with detailed instructions, is very thorough with grading, and gives excellent feedback. There are a few oral and written exams and a final project.

Mme Schleppe was an amazing French professor and really knew how to connect learning advanced French concepts with talking about current issues going on in society. Nonetheless, the class is extremely grammar-intensive and if you should definitely brush up on grammar topics if you need before taking the class with any professor.

Mme Schleppe is an amazing French professor! She is really easy to talk to and definitely always there for you if you need anything. She does give a good amount of homework which is expected to get better at the language and will call on you in class so be prepared to speak. As long as you prepare and do your work you will love the class

analysis.name: Bernadeta Kaminska
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Great prof, as Polish was already a language I spoke, (with many errors) she made sure to correct me and taught me a lot I previously did not know.
You have to pay attention, she is very nice and sweet.

Pani Kaminska was truly one of the best professors I have had in my life. She was incredibly fun and I loved how we also learned about Poland's culture. The small class size allowed us to get individual help and do lots of group work. Definitely take her class!

analysis.name: Janine Barchas
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ridiculous standards for what she wants from her essays (not difficult, she just has her own ideas for what SHE thinks your writing should look like, and will crucify you if you don't give her what she wants to see). I found her obsession with Jane Austen and constant patting herself on the back obnoxious enough that I wouldn't take her again.

If you're a Jane Austen fanatic, and are ready to join a cult dedicated to her excellency, I still wouldn't recommend this class. Grades are based upon essays to do with "research" where the expectations are very unclear + 2 exams. Professor and TA's can be arrogant and VERY particular to their own point of view, and VERY condescending otherwise.

Dr. Barchas is somewhat unapproachable and has very strict views when it comes to grading. Students never get access to the rubric and expectations for all assignments are not made clear whatsoever. Lectures are somewhat useful as they serve as material for the quizzes, research papers, and midterm. Attendance is mandatory for discussion sections.

Barchas has a psycho-sexual relationship with Jane Austen. She obsesses over her to the point of sucking out all the fun of her novels. When first signing up, I read the warnings of this class, and ignored them. I thought I would be the exception - I love to read, write, and I'm well versed in Austen. Listen to me now: you are NEVER the exception.

This is the worst professor I have ever met in my life. She knows nothing about teaching. She just grades your paper whatever she wants and she ruins many students' GPA. If you want to take her class, please prepare for a C or D for this class.l

analysis.name: Amit Bhasin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I never took the course. He seems like a chill guy, though. I spoke to him a couple of times in person, and he is very knowledgeable about the subject matter he is teaching. I didn't fully follow everything because the class was not related to my major :( I would highly recommend taking any class that he teaches!

He's a great guy I really enjoyed going to class and learning about asphalt lol :). He always listens to the class in terms of making open notes or group quizzes. You can work on homework's in groups and the final exam was open notes. The final was pretty similar to the in person quizzes we took in class. Overall great guy and interesting class.
I took him for design of Bituminous Materials. Very knowledgeable about the subject and gave great lectures where you really do learn a lot. Quizzes are very fair.

A fantastic professor, who genuinely cares about the well-being of his students. In his lectures he gives you important background knowledge and information about the assignments. In every class he promotes curiosity and critical thinking. Although the course load is very heavy with multiple research papers, this course will allow you to grow.

Perhaps my favorite professor at UT, knowledgable, approachable, caring and well-prepared. The project can be a lot of work but is also fun, you learn so much. I would definitely take another class with him.

analysis.name: Venkataraman Bhaskar
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is a hard class in general, but I would say he is the best professor to take it with. The homework are 10% midterm is 40% and final is 50% of the grade but his curve is the only reason I passed. As long as you show up and take good notes you should have an easier time on the exams. Try to find people to do homework with to help you understand.

High stakes exams (Midterm 40% and Final 50%). No recorded lectures, but lecture notes are posted. Homeworks (10 total, 2 drop) are good practice for the exams. Midterm and Final are curved for fairness for those unable to attend midterm (Final 90%). I would recommend staying on top of the course material as falling behind can easily overwhelm you.

Bhaskar is a smart man which is why it's so easy to get confused when he explains. Watch videos for clarity and DO additional practice problems. There is one midterm worth 40% (avg ~60) and one final worth 50% (avg ~68). I got below average for both exams and got a B so he curves good. DO NOT WAIT LAST MINUTE FOR STUDYING. Keep practicing activley.

The class is very interesting and the problems are fun.... when you are given effective material to work with. Homeworks do not prepare us for exam questions and often take multiple hours to do. I got myself sick once because of how much time it took to do one homework. The material is very interesting, just study as much as you can!

analysis.name: William Best
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Best professor ever! He knows how to keep students engaged, even though most of us are only taking it for the credit. In his lectures, he makes complicated concepts easy to understand. If you take his class, please participate and ask questions. He is genuinely so kind, funny, and nerdy in a good way.

Take Dr. Best!! This class was easy. Homework was a big part of your grade, but they are easy if you read the textbook. Tests were taken at home and open note. Lectures were also interesting and Dr. Best tries to make them as interactive as possible.

Prof. Best is an amazing lecturer, and he knows why most students are taking his class, so he makes it as fun and engaging as he can. I would recommend this as a science credit for sure, one of the best classes I've taken here at UT.

Dr. Best is great. Knows students are there for credit, you are still able to get something out of his class if you go every week. There are instapolls in class not for credit and questions for EC every single class so attendance helps your grade.

He knows most people taking this class are not majoring in anything related to astronomy. Still genuinely one of the sweetest, most passionate professors I've ever met. My only regret with this class is not paying attention more during the lecture and choosing to do other class work instead. Every lecture was extremely interesting and engaging.

analysis.name: Chandra Bhat
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bhat is a pretty good professor. His exams are fair, but he underestimates the time it takes to do them which led to a failing class average on the 1st exam. The class only has 2 exams, mid-term is 30%, final is 40% of your grade, homework is 25%, & participation is 5%. He covers how to do the HW well in class and is an understanding prof

He is a great prof! Super nice, cares about students, explains concepts well. However, there is breakdown in grading with the student grader being SUPER harsh and Dr. Bhat did not accept any feedback on that. Material can get confusing, homeworks are easy but the exams are incredibly hard

He really cares about his students. There's are one midterm (30%) and final (40%). He pretty much gave us all the answers to the homework (25%) in class so it is important to attended them all (they are not recorded). He made the exams open notes which helped tremendously. If you understand how to do the homework and you go to class you'll be fine.

Good instructor, worst professor in my life. After class, I asked a calculation question cz I was confused on the concept. He raged because I didn't get the concept. He kept saying "I don't know how you can't get this" over and over. He didn't try to listen to me. I was asking different one first time learning transportation system in my life.

The material itself was super interesting, but Bhat wasn't the best lecturer. His handwriting was sloppy and he went on many different roundabouts that didn't pertain to the content. Any time I contacted him for help on hwk or clarifying grading he would spew off some philosophical nonsense and wouldn't answer my questions

analysis.name: Eric Bickel
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor seems intent on using his class as some sort of "filter". While his first priority should be ensuring students understand the material, he is more interested in using his position for his own interests. Exams seem to be deliberately convoluted. You'd think some people would have better things to do in life but maybe he doesn't.

Exams consist of topics not practiced on the homework and rarely mentioned in class. Doesn't prioritize making sure students actually understand the material and are able to practice it. Alongside this, there is a heavy workload with tests, case studies and homework, along with weekly quizzes.

he is honestly not a bad professor but sometimes lectures are boring. the exams are very fair and are similar to the practice ones that he uploads but they definitely felt very rushed. the case studies and hw take forever to complete though. overall not as bad as what these reviews are making him seem like.

Studied the material he gave us + textbook for weeks in preparation for the final. Did not matter he decided to test us over software formulas and stuff that was not on the textbook or any class work. There was no way to study for that final. A lot of people failed even with his “holiday bonus”. Condescending when you ask questions. Bad teacher.

Avoid this guy if you can. His exams are hard, w/ concepts that are barely touched on in class. Grading feels almost vindictive. The class doesn't feel like an educational experience—it feels like a punishment for not deciphering his convoluted teaching style. Case studies are lengthly, discussions mandatory, 8am, no exam drops, steer clear of him.

analysis.name: Fabrizio Bisetti
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is probably the hardest classes that I have taken at UT. The subject itself is very difficult, but Professor Bisetti is extremely knowledgeable on the topic. He is extremely helpful at office hours and I feel that I truly have a good grasp on this difficult subject because of the classes rigor.

CFD is an extremely hard subject but Prof. Bisetti is obviously an expert and is amazing at teaching it. This class was very hard at the start as sometimes the homework focus on material he hasn't taught yet, but lecture slides are posted before hand. Group project heavy but plenty of guidance is given. Overall, hard class but amazing teacher.
Get ready to work in this class. The topic he teaches is difficult, but he makes the content even more complicated. Very strict and has no compassion for his students.

Dr. Bisetti is a fantastic professor. His understanding of and enthusiasm for the topic are unmatched, and he is extremely helpful if you seek guidance outside of class. The course is very difficult, but this is the nature of the subject. I think Bisetti does a good job of making it manageable without losing rigor.
Good luck in this class. It will take up all of your waking and sleeping hours

analysis.name: Luke Bishop
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This Spanish class was time-consuming, but very doable. Doing the homework/online work really helps to understand the grammar and vocabulary. Class was enjoyable because we were able to practice talking and applying what we learn from the workbook. Also, Professor Bishop is very patient and helpful when learning new concepts. Really recommend him!

Awesome prof, super fun and great music taste. 610D is the heaviest homework load in the Spanish sequence, but Prof Luke makes it worth it with great, engaging lectures. He's clearly passionate about Spanish and I definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Awesome professor and taught the content really well. Just a super nice guy as well. He gives great feedback and is very approachable. There's homework every day, but if you do it there's no way you won't do well. I really enjoyed being in the class.

This class, as with the Spanish classes at UT, comes with a lot of outside work due to it being a 6 hour credit! He gives great feedback on homework and as long as you put in the effort you will do well in the course! I recommend making quizlets for vocab and using the chapter reviews in the textbook to study for the exams! Participation is vital!

Although the textbook did awful job at explaining the grammar, Luke was great at helping you understand. If you didn't get it he would rephrase his explanations until one stuck. Very helpful office hours.

analysis.name: Daniel Bisett
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Nice guy w an unfortunate grading policy. His class material is engaging, but competitive nature of the final project makes caring about material>grade difficult. Wants you to read his mind and doesn't go by rubrics well. Said he would curve us down. Also asked for good CES survey scores. If the final wasn't a competition he wouldn't have to ask.

Prof Bisett is definitely passionate about marketing and cares for students. But he has inconsistent grading, curves down, and often doesnt follow his own rubric. Tests are easy but the curve down really messes with your grade. He uses AI for slides and tests which make the class feel less personal and is frustrating imo. Wouldnt take again unforch

While this class is interesting and Professor Bisett clearly knows a lot about marketing, the grading scale of this class is one of the worst at UT. He curves the class down and 30% of your grade is dependent on a group project, where he shows clear favoritism and the grading scale is unclear. He also frequently used AI for slides.

OK professor. Easy quizzes and exam. Complete all possible extra credit because he will try to give you the lowest final grade possible. I ended this class with a 91 and received a B freaking plus as a letter grade.. because of his unfair grading policy. The final presentation policy is a nightmare.

While the lectures can be interesting at times, the grading sucks. He wants his students to compete in order to get a good grade in the class. The final project is worth 30% of the grade, and if you are not a finalist, you can only get an 80%!! He also cleary has favorite students!!

analysis.name: Douglas Biow
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Biow is a great person but his class and these ratings were so deceiving. Most people often found themselves feeling worthless after getting grades back from their papers since they grade them so harshly. The mean for the papers is usually in the 70's range and for a UGS class, it should not be that hard. The films are also so boring.

The content is easy and enjoyable, no exams, but the class is formatted HORRIBLY, and the professor is very confused by his own syllabus. Doesn't know how to use Canvas, not clear about due dates at all. TA mentioned he was about to retire, but I saw he's teaching English classes this summer and fall. Don't take him, just unnecessary stress.

The professor's lectures were very engaging, covering a wide range of topics, and the class exposed me to many films that I wouldn't have otherwise watched, many of which were exceptional and now among my all-time favorites. There are no exams but there are essays, but you can choose the topic of each essay and which film it's about.
He is wonderful! He loves what he teaches and is very knowledgeable about all kinds of film.

Preparing for them is very time consuming (I did about 8 hours per test), but it pays off and I did really well. It is not any easy class but it is doable if you apply yourself when it comes to the test. LOTS of readings but aim for big picture understanding not little stuff

This is a very easy course to take during the summer. To be honest, the lectures were taken from Dr. Crosnoe so he is really the one who should be getting this great review. The paper assignments were easy and the discussion boards were not time consuming, I always had time to do all the assignments. The TA I had was not harsh either, great class!

Professor McCaslin is a very nice professor, but this class is so much work. That's expected for a course like this, but the assignments felt endless. It took forever to get feedback for assignments that were necessary for the final grade. I had the same grade for 90% of the semester with no real idea of how I was doing until the final week.

Reading and an assignment due every week. Assignment builds up to term research paper at the end of the year. Easy, but lectures at you/so incredibly boring/ not relatable to your research bc you aren't actually conducting research, just writing about a potential research topic. Takes participation but you can miss 3 and it wont effect your grade.

Essays are not bad but are graded so late it's impossible to know what your final grade will be. 2 reflection essays, 3 reading responses, and a midterm and final. Expects you to read 20+ pages of readings before every class. Exams are short response and fill in the blank, never multiple choice. Manageable to get a B, don't expect to get an A.

analysis.name: Christopher Bryan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Bryan is a very good professor and keeps students engaged. However, be prepared to never know what grade you'll have in this class as things never get graded. Additionally, he can sometimes get caught up in his own research rather than actually listening to students and letting us discuss with our peers. Super easy and interesting class!!

Prof. Bryan is one of the best professor in UT by far. He is very charismatic, he cares about his students and his class lectures are very interesting. This is the way we should be learning, he has a lot of experience in the field and a lot of good anecdotes to tell during class. Hopefully, I take another class with him because is a great person.

The professor is clearly passionate about the subject and does a great job of explaining concepts/lessons of his research. Deadlines and assignments were always clearly communicated, and the feedback provided was constructive. I highly recommend this class because it teaches invaluable skills and the class is very interactive.

Do not pass up Dr. Bryan!! He is an amazing lecturer and cares deeply about applying class concepts to the real world. His TA Johno was also amazing and I would 100% recommend any course taught by Dr. Bryan. This class helped open my eyes to how other people think and was provided with new perspectives. One of my fav classes at UT hands down,

Prof. Bryan was one of the best professors I had at UT. His class was engaging, and the material felt relevant beyond the classroom. He knew every student by name and encouraged open discussion. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Dean Bredeson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Only 10 unit quizzes, 5 optional EC lectures, and the final. There is no +- for this class, attending EC lectures is an extra point onto your FINAL GRADE. After quizzes, I had a 97. After 4/5 lectures, I had a 101. BUT, the final is worth 50% of your grade! I bombed it. Dont be afraid to email Bredeson, he sent me 2 EC assignments for a B.

FAVORITE PROFESSOR I'VE HAD SO FAR AT UT. Very funny, knows a lot about this topic, very interesting. He talks fast but always repeats himself and I'm always able to write all my notes. Probably the first class I've never skipped because it's actually really interesting. LOVELOVELOVE him and will really miss his class.

One big test thats lowkey stressful, other than that he does nothing. Not necessarily a bad thing because his $120 textbook was easy to read, but if that's not your learning style DO NOT TAKE IT. Because he doesn't give anything aside from short vague vids. But honestly wasn't as hard as i thought it would be, just stressful toward the end.

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR! Unresponsive to emails, quizzes can only be taken once and have very ambiguous questions that can be subjective or not based on one word. I have full regret for taking this class online. Readings aren't too bad they just take a while to decipher. Overall bad experience would NOT take him ever again.

He was not a good professor. Hosts review sessions but does not have notes/powerpoints so it's really hard to follow along. You cannot hear what he is saying and its very to miss what he is talking about. Not accessible outside of class and doesn't leave any feedback. He makes you buy his textbook and its the most reading i've ever done.

analysis.name: Erika Bsumek
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I had a really great time with this class during this semester. She has openly said that she is not trying to trick you or hurt your GPA, and she just wants you to have a great experience. There's a few group projects, but if everyone does their part, it won't be an issue. Our final is going to be take home at the end of the semester as well.

Dr. Bsmuek is a good professor. She really cares about every student's success. She knows her stuff. She also expects you to put in the work, too. There are weekly discussion posts that take a few hours to read for and complete. If this class is at a weird time again, that's because you're meeting with students in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

Easiest class I've ever taken at UT. Professor Bsumek gave me an A just for showing up to class. Homework is minimal, 4 projects in the class, rare reading and three presentations. My favourite part of the class was talking for 3 hours each class about the environment and how we can help bettering it. I wish she was professor for all my classes.

Attendance was via QR code and there were no exams. A few discussion boards and writing assignments that were pretty easy but the main part is the group project so it just depends on if you get lucky with your group or not. I didn't think grading was too harsh but was TA dependent. Overall really easy class if you need a history credit

Interesting class, but reading HEAVY. Minimum 2 works/pdfs before each class and had multiple papers due throughout the sem. Few papers were very repetitive (multiple 'drafts' of the same paper, I barely had to change anything substantial- just a hassle)
Don't procrastinate the final project, HEAVILY INVOLVED.
Bsumek is nice and understanding.

analysis.name: Michael Butterworth
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: TAs collectively decided a C is the average. the class used to be really easy but now it is insanely unrealistic for a UGS. there are way better UGS courses. dont take this if you just need a credit. my TA was awful just made us come and asked if we had questions because she has no plan and we all sat in silence for an hour.

I really enjoyed his lectures! You can tell he truly cares about the content and is incredibly knowledgeable about it. He has a great enthusiasm toward baseball which makes it that much more interesting to learn about. Would love to take another course from him in the future.

LOVED this UGS. Do not understand the low ratings he gets on here. First off, he is a super nice, funny, well-rounded guy. He is so passionate about baseball which made me want to show up to lectures (which were not required). ONLY complaint was the TAs.

I almost never leave reviews, but this class deserves a warning. class material not hard but grading is harsh. Discussion average in the 65-73, papers land in the same range, no curve or extra credit. I maintain straight As in tougher STEM courses, but I only pull a C here. The evaluation standards feel excessive for an otherwise reasonable class.

This professor is one of those professors that will give you more work just because he knows people will not care about his class. He is a harsh grader, and in my opinion does not follow the grading criteria and just grades depending on his opinions of the paper, and I feel like the TAs do not even know half of the stuff we are talking about.

analysis.name: Nicole Butterbaugh
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Your grade depends heavily on your group, be prepared to pick up the slack for other just to pass. Reporting it does nothing. Study guides are disorganized and include unnecessary material, while giving no clear direction on what to study. Assignments have extremely poor instructions. Overall, one of the most unhelpful and frustrating instructors

The most impressive part of this class is how simple material was turned into an unnecessarily harsh and mind-numbing course. Feedback didn't improve grades, studying didn't help exams, and missing class meant penalties with no leniency. 

The course could have been more manageable and engaging. Frustrating and poorly handled, I hope she eases up.

Do not take her if you have any other option. To say the least, the assignments were odd, with poor instructions, and poor explanations when you asked for clarification.  The only thing you could do for a test was pray, most of the topics on the tests we never covered. And the group project, all I can say is good luck.

Do NOT take this class. I thought it wasnt going to be that bad but it is. The lectures are so boring and there is SO much work. The tests are hard and she is not the nicest. Seriously take any other class. Especially if you know you already have a busy semester!

The material was easy to learn, and although the assignments did not have the clearest instructions, they were also pretty straightforward. When asking questions for help, she wasn't the most helpful or nicest, but she did her job I guess.

analysis.name: David Buss
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's not too open to criticisms of his research work, but I have to give it to him, he's a great professor. Assigned textbooks are very helpful. Attendance not mandatory, but you should just go and experience his lectures. Very interesting course, but don't get caught up in the narrow social framework of Evo Psych. Always stay skeptical.

He is one of the best professors here at UT hands down. You'll definitely need to read the textbook to pass the exams but the readings are manageable. He loves to interact with his students and he is a very funny guy. One of my favorite courses I have taken.

Dr. Buss is back to teaching evolutionary psych! I'd highly recommend the class. The only grades are 4 exams, which are fair and the info is largely covered in the lectures. (But reading will help a lot). Very interesting topic and lectures -- no attendance taken but you'll want to go. Dr. Buss and the TA are truly experts in this topic.

The lectures had a lot of interesting and valuable material! This course was only graded on 4 exams, but they were all very easy to pass as long as you did the readings. The lecture slides also give an overview of material you needed to focus on knowing for each exam.
This class was a complete joke.

analysis.name: Christopher Burke
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 89 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Burke is amazing! If you can take him, DO. His lectures are engaging and make OM an easy to understand concepts. If you attend class weekly, you won't need to study outside of class. The homework is easy and take less than 30 mins weekly. You absolutely should attend class (no tech allowed) to succeed on the exams, but it's very doable.

I enjoyed Professor Burke's class. He's an engaging lecturer who explains material clearly, is approachable during office hours, and is always willing to help. He's also very understanding and accommodating. The weekly homework is manageable, and while the exams can be challenging, staying on top of the material and studying makes them very doable

I truly don't get what people in here are saying because Burke is by far the best OM professor. He's super understanding but stern. He's always there for you and he's a pretty good lecturer. 100% recommend. If you don't like OM in general, every prof will be challenging. Just work a bit hard ig

This professor does not care about his students one bit. If I were given the option to take another course taught by him or drop out of UT, I would start packing my bags and go. I have never met a professor who grades so harshly on exams and then looks at his students as if it is our fault. This guy will laugh at you for failing and not help.

Burke is a pretty humorous guy who always begins his class talking about the weekly UT sports scene. Classes are slides based on readings, and assignments are simple excel worksheets and interactive textbook questions. He makes a review slide for the midterms and if you study those you will do well. Class is usually released 30 minutes early.

analysis.name: Andrew Butters
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I looked forward to professor Butters's classes every week! I learned so much about journalism from the stories he told of his experiences as a journalist. We wrote 3 stories throughout the semester and he offered much guidance and good feedback. Attendance is definitely important!

Professor Butters was so kind and passionate about journalism. I looked forward to the lab every week. Professor Butters was very accessible and always willing to help and share experiences from his past that were humorous and inspiring. I wish I was a journalism major so I could take more classes with Butters, his lectures were very engaging.

analysis.name: Joshua Burby
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: he a cool dude, its obvious he really love physics and teaching it in general which i think is awesome but he's trying to teach us at a much higher level than the class should be, n it just confuses everyone. he just be goin through 2 page long proofs every class and god damn i'm lost as hell. exams r 13% and hws are like 50% so its chill doe.

Dr. Burby's class is the most difficult course I've taken. Every day in class he has a problem and solves it the most complicated way. Doesn't give you formulas you just have to know. He makes his own homework questions and they are ungodly difficult. The TA's are stuck sometimes, and extra credit was just 2 more exams. GG WP 0/10 NO RE

He is not a very good professor. His lectures go beyond classical mechanics and he ends up lecturing about derivations and proofs. You end up having to teach yourself most of the material in order to do the HWs. The test and HWs are very hard. The test and HWs always have some hard questions that he wrote himself. The TAs carry this class.

Nice guy, but overcomplicates too much for an intro course. 1st test was like hw, but everything got worse. Homework problems had concepts not covered in class and 2nd test tried to apply hw "concepts", except we never fully learned them. Asked for feedback but didnt follow it. TAs are a godsend, but even they + other grads cant solve some problems

Second midterm stats:
Mean: 39.7
Median: 42.86
HIGH Score: 78.57

Do not take him it's not worth it.

analysis.name: William Bulko
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr.Bulko is an awesome lecturer and his class is fairly easy (10 HW assignments - small iOS apps; 1 semester project App). His lectures mostly consist of him doing Swift/xCode demos and the assignments are pretty enjoyable. My TA was great and most people get A's on the HW, but the instructions are picky. Start the project early!

He was great, he was really funny and he made you want to come to lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but it earns you slip days for homework. He makes the subject really accessible and a really good lecturer.

REFUSED to share lecture recordings when I missed a week due to medical emergencies. He asked me: "So if you had gotten ill in 2019, before anyone was even considering recording classes, what would you have done?" He should ask himself how he could better provide us the resources we need in order to succeed given these difficult times.

I found Bulko's CS311 class easy and manageable in terms of concept and workload, and a good counterpart to Mike Scott's difficult CS 314 class. His lectures are understanding and entertaining (enhanced by his amusing/dry jokes (depending on the person)). HW can be unnecessarily difficult, but tests are a lot easier. Just watch out for your TA.

IThis class is really boring but Bulko knows that and tries to keep the lectures semi-interesting, but still if you're not careful you'll fall asleep. The TA's were not very helpful but if you form a study group for the homework you should get good grades. Make a good cheatsheet for the test and you'll be solid, they're not as hard as the hw.

analysis.name: Henry Byron
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Henry explains concepts clearly and demonstrates genuine concern for student success. However, lectures tend to lack engagement, with lengthy, difficult-to-follow slides and a presentation style thats really boring. Exams are challenging, but the grading policy reduces the weight of the lowest test score.

Professor Henry is fantastic. Topics in lectures are clearly conveyed to students using approachable language and class assignments. He takes an individual interest into each students success both in and out of the classroom as well. His classes are tough mainly because of the McCombs standardization of accounting classes however.

He is a caring and knowledgeable professor. I really enjoyed his lectures because he encouraged participation and explained concepts in depth. He engaged us quite well with the content, allowing a fundamental and intuitive understanding of the course. He was also generous with grading and attendance. 10/10!

analysis.name: Delia Byrnes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a great lecturer! Interesting topics, books and movies. Since the class is small, it was mainly discussion about the book/movie. She gives great feedback on essays and is really willing to help you out. Weekly reading or movie watching. Part of your grade is participating in discussion and divided up between three essays and pop quizzes

Awesome instructor! the class itself is very small and intimate. The variety of reading and film materials makes the class interesting and I had fun. You get 3 unexcused absences for this class - make sure you don't skip more than that and you should be fine. Overall, the class requires minimal work and participation.
shes a great professor. she really cares about her students and has a fun class. the book and movie choices are so interesting and she lets you revise your essays for another grade!

analysis.name: John Bybee
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: There are far better professors at UT teaching this course. The only thing you get from Bybee is a regurgitated version of the researchers on campus who are critically engaging with these topics. The class is incredibly easy though and, honestly, pretty painless if you don't mind dealing with a grad student who likes to hear himself talk.

Easy class. terrible design. Vague direction from professor, unnecessarily long and pointless assignments.  Grad student on an ego trip.  Does not inspire college level interaction from class. Treats students as tho they are  still in kindergarten.  If u have the option and don't want to shoot urself mid-semester,choose another prof.

I had professor bybee in the spring semester and really enjoyed his class. He took the time to meet with students before the semester began and was passionate about the subject matter. Only drawback was that it was a lot of writing that can pile up if you are not careful. Would recommend!

analysis.name: Alexis Carre
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: These other reviews are crazy, this prof will have u praying a frat bro drunk driving home at 9AM hits you JUST so you don't have to listen to his French, smoke latent, disengaged demeanor. this is not an easy A class, prepare to grovel, prepare to read 1 book per week. Doesn't sound like a lot but it catches up to you. oh and he cold calls :)

LOTS of reading u have to buy all of them, 7 books ranging from 70 to 10. Don't read, you'll be lost. He has difficulty explaining the reading in simple terms for the class to understand and tends to go very slowly through the material. We were constantly behind. cold calls but most of the time the class just stared back at him in silence.

Defrinitely do the readings and attend class and you're in for an easy A. The classes and readings are foundational for succeeding in the papers, but he does a good job explaining what he wants to see and what he expects in the papers. Great lectures, I learned a lot and he really made me think over problems with a new perspective.

Tough but fair. Once you realize what he wants from your essays, it gets a lot easier. Attendance is required, and participate in class for full credit. Ask questions in class. Definitely read the books, you'll learn something new and you can't write a good essay without them. This class was super difficult, but also a great learning experience.

Lecture heavy (you'll fail after enough absences), be prepared to take notes, and do try to read the books for a chance at extra credit during discussion. Sometimes gave us emails on extra notes and thoughts on lectures. Once had a turn-in issue and he was very gracious and allowed me to turn it in even after the close date. 3 papers 1 final.

analysis.name: Rhonda Evans Case
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely one of the funniest professors I have ever had. While the content can be boring at some points, she is very engaging and fun to listen to. As long as you show up to lectures, loosely pay attention, and review before the exam, you will get a good grade in this class. The exams are intuitive if you listen in class.

Easily one of the BEST professors I've met. If you have the chance to take one of her courses, I'd highly recommend it. The course content was new, interesting, & particularly relevant. She's very down to earth, open to feedback, and offers great advice. Super knowledgeable with engaging lectures. If you commit to this class, you'll be rewarded.

Dr. Evans is a great person and good for life advice (she sets aside time for this in class, but I mean one-on-one). The class itself was more unorganized than I hoped, that might just be that semester. Many assignments were restructured or canceled with course material seemingly too much with too little depth. Great remote/online accessibility!

If you need an upper level gov I would highly suggest this one. The content of the course was about the politics of critical minerals which not a lot of people really know much about but she made it interesting. Dr. Evans was such an amazing and understanding professor. I went through a tough year and she helped me through it & gave the best advice

Professor was great at lecturing but course content was dense. There was so much material and it was tough to navigate and contextualize it. She provides everything needed in lectures, I barely read. My issue was more it was heavy in content and didn't leave room to understand things in depth. She is a caring person and takes feedback into account.

analysis.name: Carley Law
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If there's another professor for the class you need, take the other one. Her grading depends heavily on your relationship with her, plus you won't know your grade until the end of the semester when it is too late to do any changes or do better in the next projects. Very passive-aggressive with her emails if you even get one from her back.

She is a very tough grader and is very disrespectful. She does not care about the wellbeing of her students. She is very unclear about her projects and assignments and gets mad when students don't understand. She will embarrass you in front of the whole class and is very unencouraging.

Honestly kind and caring professor when it comes to critique and individual feedback. Though, does not hold herself to the same standards she puts onto her students. Pushed back deadlines, last minute project changes, passive-aggressive when it comes to discussing grades, and does not grade anything until the last minute. Sweet but unprofessional.

You only receive grades back at the very end of the semester. Even when she likes something in class, you may receive a poor grade on it and there's no way to know. She's extremely nit picky in her grading. When her TA told me they liked something, she would disagree but I would not know this until grades came out. The grading feels subjective.

Carley, by far, is one of the most passionate professors I've ever had. You can tell she loves what she teaches, and she teaches it well. I was never stressed by her class and the assignments she gives out. Very understanding of your time! As for the other and much lower ratings for her, I think she has improved her teaching methods and syllabus.

analysis.name: Ruth Buskirk
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 267 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, you could get an A if you just answered her learning objectives and slept through lectures, which I did. Buskirk's tests can be very hard with questions that seem to provide two or more correct answers. She may be a tough grader but she is very helpful in office hours and cares about your success if you participate. she is best UTbio prof

She's a good lecturer but you need to have previous bio knowledge. I came in with no bio knowledge whatsoever and I didn't do great in the class. I studied hard and it was still hard to understand. Three exams and a final, she averages your lowest exam with your final or something like that.

Dr. Buskirk was my fav prof! Had her for 311C and 311D. As long as you show up to lecture and pay attention, you'll do fine. Textbook is "required", but most people never used it and all material you need to know will be covered during class. She makes it very clear what she expects you to know for quizzes and reuses homework/polling questions.

Dr. Buskirk is an amazing professor! You will learn a ton of stuff in her class. The class is very organized and the workload is perfect. Just make sure you stay on track or you will fall behind for tests. Her tests are pretty tricky. You will have to master every topic from every angle in order to do well on her tests. Take her for Bio if you can!

Buskirk is simply amazing.  Her lectures only have what is going to be on the test and you don't have to read the textbook, but it is helpful.
