She gives out paper that tell you what you have to know for the test.  If you know everything there you will get a near perfect.  She offers Q&A sessions before every test that are extremely helpful.

analysis.name: Samuel Cantor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super easy class, take this if you can for credit. He is a funny dude. Grades are in class participation and debates.
Amazing professor loved his lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory but credit is taken in class.
Interesting lectures and he's a really cool dude. Very chill class

analysis.name: Cesar Salgado
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The single worst professor I have had in my two years at U.T  His lectures are not lectures---he just stands up and rambles on any topic, not neccesarily one dealing with the course subject. Expect any questions  you have to be ignored and class to always run up to thirty minutes late. Avoid at any cost.

This was the second class I took with Dr. Salgado, and it was MUCH more challenging than the first, but he's still his funny, engaging self. You're reading long primary documents written in 17th century spanish as homework, which was very frustrating, but ultimately it was a history class and massively improved my reading comprehension.

Probably the best lecturer I've had so far. He is so knowledgeable and passionate about the course, and it shows. He's pretty funny, very understanding of deadlines, and is just a caring person in general. Some of the readings can be very lengthy, but the syllabus lets you know what you'll be reading ahead of time, so you can plan for it.

I took Visualizing Cuba with him and he was great. You can tell he really cares about the topic and is very knowledgeable. He tended to go off on tangents sometimes, but they were always related to the lecture and interesting regardless. Spoke to him a couple of times outside of class as well and he was very warm and pleasant to be around always.

Amazing professor, eye-opening lectures, feedback, and readings. Love his side comments. Understanding on deadlines. 
Heavy readings, and he could improve assignment expectations. 
There's also room for more discussions with students in class. He'd often let you speak for about 3 seconds, and that's all your time to form up a thought, in Spanish.

analysis.name: Celina Nevarez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took this class as a summer course, so the amount of daily homework required was a bit overwhelming at times, but that's to be expected for an online class over the summer. Overall, this professor was SO sweet and replied quickly if you sent her an email. Her energy and enthusiasm made taking this class over the summer bearable.

Celina is very energetic and relies a lot on your participation in class. I believe the more your participation, the better your homework gets graded. But she is quite picky on grading so the smallest mistakes take you to a 90. She is understanding however if you talk to her outside of class. She's a little slow with anything online though.

Took her for SPN 314. Dreaded showing up to this class everyday. The class wasn't super hard, but it was a lot of work. She seemed annoyed anytime you would ask her a question. Didn't have clear grading criteria. Would always give me lower marks for participation based on my vibe. She told me this during her office hours, btw. Kinda cray.

She just isn't a good teacher. She barely knows how to explain the material and gets defensive when people try to communicate with her about it. She was very disorganized most of the time and would make us confused about the due dates for assignments. She is generally a nice person, but if you want to save your GPA, don't take her.

Do not recommend. Made going to class unbearable and would call out students in front of everyone over something trivial and students weren't doing anything wrong. Concepts are bearable. Expect daily homework and pop quizzes. Would also write to-do list for next class instead of posting on canvas so if you missed class, you're out of luck

analysis.name: Chang Liu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: IDC what anyone says about him, he's probably my favorite SLHS professor. He makes me want to do audiology. The course can be difficult, but he is so caring and not a tough grader at all, literally, if you just try, you will get at LEAST a B-. The first unit is more physics, the second is more anatomy. Such a caring guy, great class.

Be warned, this was the hardest class I've ever taken in my life. If you are doing hearing science, just know that it is just physics, arithmetic, acoustics, circular waves, and calculating sine wave formulas. This should be labeled as a MATH class, not a hearing science class. The teacher has a heavy accent.

Test are worth 50% of the grade and there are only two. Great professor and very kind just his lectures are sometimes scattered and hard to understand. you will do well if you attend each class and he offeres many extra credit opportunties.

Dr. Liu is an awesome professor! He explains everything very well -- despite his accent which you will eventually understand. Super caring and helpful towards his students, so don't be afraid to ask him questions! Just go to class, take notes, and lastly I highly recommended RECORDING because it can get fast sometimes! :)

Course is kind of hard, first half is physics based and second is conceptual. Bi-weekly quizzes that are short, but you have to study a lot to fully understand concepts that MAY be on the quiz. Sometimes unorganized and jumps back and forth in slides, but posts the slides before class. Labs are group projects which can be frustrating at times.

analysis.name: Chih Shih
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Middle of the road professor. You don't need the textbook & lecture attendence is just in-class physics polls, which aren't bad. Tests are very similar to the review & it's easy to do well if you just do a little work. Not as bad as people say but he is rather old and struggles with tech/demos. Very nice guy and values students learning over grades

Professor Shih gives lectures that rarely extend beyond deriving equations and assignments that go much beyond deriving equations. He is difficult to hear in the back of the room and writes very small on the blackboard. The assignments will take hours of trial-and-error if you don't rely entirely on AI. Tests were very difficult.

Dr.Shih's physics II course is very challenging. I would recommend taking it only if you have sufficient resources outside for learning & have good experience with physics prior, bc he assumes physics I has prepared you well enough already & that you can learn/grasp complex material quickly. He said often the grading rules on the syllabus are final

I do not recommend taking physics with Dr. Shih. The exams were of similar difficulty to the homeworks, but the lectures don't properly prepare you to do the Quest problems. Lecture was always derivation and never actual problem solving. He would only go over his Quest Exam Reviews, but couldn't work technology well so it wasn't very helpful.

Explains everything very thoroughly but theres so much content you can forget how you got somewhere. ASK QUESTIONS, or stop him if he's going too fast. He cares, but without feedback he just assumes you understand. Hw took 2-4 hrs/week. Tests use similar questions to the practice test, or the easiest questions on the hw. Curves, but not by much.

analysis.name: Chad Alvarez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was honestly enjoyable. Basically all you have to do is complete the assigned reading and go to class and engage in discussion. All in all, this was a great class.

Dr. Alvarez is by far the best professor that I had at UT. As a MALS major, I had him for two different classes, one of which was my capstone. He is someone who encourages meaningful and present engagement with peers and the material, but is always helpful in aiding discussion. He is so knowledgeable and truly loves his students. TAKE HIS CLASS!

He is an excellent lecturer, but the readings are terrible. Luckily, if you go to class it's enough. I never read, just skimmed and reviewed the day before the test. It's an Easy A if you read but if you don't it's still an easy B.

New class structure where you only have two one-hour essay tests. Each one is 50% of your grade and are graded subjectively, grade can easily change depending on if a TA or prof graded your exam. Prompts were very broad and you had to use readings as evidence. There is a lot of material to read, I skipped lecture and only read and improved my grade

Overall an easy class, and you can read the readings during class and and chime in once you get the idea to get participation credit. 30% of the grade is a map quiz (super easy), 40% is attendance/participation/and a project that takes like 2 hrs, and 30% final. Only need to study 5 or so hrs for final. All in all a great class and I learned a ton.

analysis.name: Lilly Chin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super chill professor who gives good lectures. Her way of attendance is a form at the end of class where she asks how you're doing in the class and what should she review at the start of next class. She answers people's questions with good answers and even if the question is somewhat simple. W proff

THE GOAT TAKE HER FOR 319K!!! Her slides are super detailed, way better than the old ones on the 319K website, and she does a great job of explaining concepts during lecture. Chin obviously works super hard into prepping for each lecture and takes feedback to try and improve them throughout the year. You can tell that she cares a lot about students

Super knowledgeable! She is always looking to improve her teaching and really cares if she is reaching her students. She takes our feedback super seriously and puts lots of effort into making lectures and slides that are engaging and digestible! Super kind in office hours and will totally geek out over anything STEM related with you!

Professor Chin was a great professor for 319K. Her lectures were pretty good and topical, she was super friendly and willing to answer questions, and generally passionate and knowledgeable about the class. 10/10 professor take her if you can.

i literally love lillian chin and i could not get through 319 without em. i had yeraballi but always watched chin's lectures. incredible professor. this class was centralized so there wasn't much she could do to make the class easier or harder but TAKE CHIN IF YOU CAN!!!

analysis.name: Debbie Cifuentes ramirez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: So sweet, but the tests, which there are only 2 that equal 25% of ur grade, are nothing from what we learn. i had a 100% in all the categories in the class, like HW, oral, and participation, but bc of the tests, i got by with an A-. Seriously, the tests are just impossible to study for and basically completel yrandom grammar she never taught us

sweet lady, but very disorganized and poor communicator. didn't grade assignments until the last 2 weeks. class itself is not too hard, but there's no structure, and it gets u for tests. all semester we just yap in class, and then for our 2 tests worth 25% of our grade it's absolutely nothing like what we learned. tests r complete 180

Do NOT take her class. I took it last year and she was genuinely one of the worst professors I have ever had. So much homework and it never gets graded. Had a C for 3+ months in the semester, only because she did not grade 10+ assignments. Then, at the end of the semester, my grade finally moved up to an A when she graded everything. Worst class.
As a prof she's a bit disorganized. There were times where we were thrown off the schedule because of it. Overall though, she's super sweet and genuinely wants you to learn Spanish.

one of the sweetest professors, please take her!! participation is required but we had rly interesting discussions in class and Prof. Cifuentes-Ramirez was very encouraging and patient so don't be afraid to make mistakes in spanish :) other grades are the HWs, exams, speaking assignments, and group presentations but it is very doable to get an A

analysis.name: Erica Ciszek
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It is an easy A with online exams. However, Dr. Ciszek reads off of a script while teaching, and doesn't write their notes on the lecture slides. Instead, you have to rush writing, hopefully without missing anything they say. In addition, class ends at 6:20 on Thursday instead of 6:15 as they start 5 minutes late due to chatting with students.

Not much for this class. Assignments in first half of class are super easy, then go on to campaign critiques. Mandatory attendance for the one lecture a week, one free absence.Four quizzes online throughout the semester, however the cache is that lectures are so boring. Videos are showing during lecture to use up more time, and awkward pauses.

Ciszek is super chill, lectures were very interesting. Attendance is mandatory for the 1 class a week, There is an online lecture video each week outside of class, one assignment or discussion board that doesn't take too long, and there are 4 quizzes total. Very easy. Usually goes 5-10 min over class time, and randomly calls on people in lectures.
Ciszek was great and so understanding. You get out what you put into this class. Would def take ciszek again if i had the opportunity

Dr. Ciszek was amazing! She is so funny and makes lectures feel like a conversation rather than lecture. She tells you what's on her exams, post her power points online so you can actually enjoy and listen to her lectures, and her exams aren't too hard if you study. Attendance required, but you'd want to be there anyway. Take her!

analysis.name: Cindy Meston
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 96 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely loved her and respect her so much. The lectures are very interesting and occasionally gives you bonus points. No homework , each exam weighs 20% but the lowest out of the 5 gets dropped. Very easy class as long as you watch the lecture and read the assigned chapters. I loved this class and literally aspire to be Dr.Meston.

I really enjoyed Dr. Meston's lectures as it was clear she was passionate about the subject and easy to listen to. The lectures were even better in 2x speed and easy to digest. The information isn't for everyone but it was interesting and lots of extra credit plus a pretty straight forward test, no final, and drops lowest test score.

Funniest class I have taken to this day. With that said it is actually kind of difficult so make sure you attend the lectures. If you attend lectures you will not only get EC opportunities but you will also get at least a B. I made the mistake of not going to class for half the semester and it killed me on half the tests.

Super easy free A, but only graded on 5 tests. She provides bonus points opportunity in almost every lecture to bump your grade up 10 points. Attendance not mandatory. Really nice professor who's knowledgable about the class and lectures themselves had interesting topics.

This was one of my favorite classes I've taken at UT! The lectures are super interesting and the required reading is relevant and easy to digest. The tests are not hard and cover exactly what is discussed in lecture. You can also earn bonus points by logging into lectures at the scheduled times. Very engaging and an easy A if you do the work.

analysis.name: Gustavo Cepparo
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 191 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Cepparo is hilarious! I took his class at 8am MWF  and he made it energetic and informative. His notes are organized and briefs you before exams. Expect a rather heavy load of weekly Quest and textbook homework. TA sessions aren't mandatory but you need to go to turn in your homework to be graded. Must work for an A. Most enjoyable class so far.

CEPPARO IS AWESOME!!! If you do and understand his homework, study his online material, go to class, and go to his office hours for questions, you WILL do well.  He is a very generous grader and cares about his students alot.  This is also a fantastic class to take if you must take an 8AM! Very funny! Very entertaining! He made Calculus amazing!

Definitely not an easy class, but Cepparo is a fantastic teacher. His explanations in class were clear, although he did run through material very quickly so it was difficult to keep up at times. There's one book assignment and one quest per week, so workload is a bit heavy. I had only taken Calc AB prior, but I did all the work and made an A.

Cepparo was amazing. I loved every second of his class. He gave a lot of homework, but it really helped me tremendously. I had taken calculus before, so it was pretty easy for me and I made an A on every test. He is very willing to help and loves his students. Take this guy, you won't regret it.

If you screw up just one of his exams, you grade will be affected. So beware! I had 3 tests overall and though I improved from 66% to 96% to 104% (you see how good that improvement is), I could not make an A. :'( Work from the beginning. BTW he stammers on one phrase (always): OK WITH THAT? lol. And he loves coffee.

analysis.name: Erica Cizsek
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: They are such an amazing professor! Super kind and welcoming. They provide super insightful lectures as well. Genuinely learned so much but in a fun and interactive way. Would 100% take again. There are exams and a good amount of writing assignments but they're pretty simple! Attendance is not required 100% of the time, but often.

Cizsek is the sweetest; you can tell they care about their students and teaching the material. This class wasn't difficult at all either. Def don't hesitate to take this class if Cizsek is still the professor!

Although I ended with a C (totally on me because I completely missed a quiz), Professor Cizsek had such great lectures that really helped with understanding the field of advertising and it was a really easy class

Love love loved this class. Super easy with fun lectures and collaborative discussions. Dr.Cizek is clearly passionate about their profession and does their best to ensure their students are being educated about important current issues. Lots of extra credit and exams were stress free with no final
MY FAVORITE TEACHER AT UT!!!! Genuinely cares about her students and the material. Great and engaging lecture! Take her class, you will not regret it!!! Loved every minute of her lectures!

analysis.name: Cindy McCreery
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I promise you need to take this class! It's so fun and interesting! She's very helpful with all your work and always open for questions. She cares so much about all her students and if you just do your work which is pretty easy you will get an A. It's literally impossible to not unless you just don't do the work!

Ask questions anytime Cindy is super chill and is always available and gets back to you, I've never had a teacher/professor care this much about their students :) the work is super easy and fun and it really helped me for my future of wanting to be a writer especially TV writing if that interests you!
This is a great class if you love to write and be creative! This class 100% made me a better writer! Cindy is the NICEST women you will ever meet.
Although there's a lot of participation I feel like this class really created a community for RTF majors and I'm thankful for this class:)

Cindy is a very nice person but there were many things that made the class frustrating. The class was disorganized and assignments could be confusing at times. I felt I was teaching myself most of the time and had to learn how to do something in the span of a week. Also, we don't know what our grades are two weeks before the end of the semester.

analysis.name: Mirela Ciperiani
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Condescending professor. She was/is a mathematical prodigy without humbleness and this didn't translate to excellent teaching. HARSH grader on exams but HW's are always full credit with little feedback. I walked out of the class with a 100 on the final, an A, and a lot of resentment for making algebra not fun. Just save yourself and take Keel.

Lectures are unbelievably dry and suck the life out of the subject that is group theory. Pretty much follows the definition->theorem->proof cycle you would find in any old textbook, except in lecture form. Provides essentially 0 intuition and is pretty much all about deduction and symbolic manipulation. Exam problems sampled from homeworks.

The HW is the exam with the caveat that she expects you to be perfect on the exams. Most of your grade comes from exams but she replaces one and also 2 out of the 11 HWs. Presentations of HW are a big part of this class so expect to present math. She is a phenomenal professor if you expect to take algebraic structures 2 with Sean.

Not the worst but also not great. The homeworks were long and while the tests were based on them, she chooses the hardest/trickiest problems from each assignment, and it feels like there's not enough time to finish the exams. She's not a great lecturer; I just read the textbook or watched YT videos since I got nothing from her lectures.

Super knowledgeable & gives you everything you need to do well. Homework is difficult but exams are pulled from the homework so it's clear what you need to know for exams & exams are easy as a result. Lectures are really informative without being overly dense. Overall a really solid choice for number theory.

analysis.name: Cinzia Russi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Awful professor. She's hysterical and confusing. Makes a fairly easy subject matter very difficult to understand. She also giggles when she gives you bad grades. I would never recommend her to anyone.

Textbook readings can be long. Quizzes were either very easy or very hard. You don't learn much Italian in the course; it's a regular course taught in 70% Italian. Very open to working with the class on what material is difficult and changing the course structure during the semester. Friendly professor, encourages participation.
Lang Truths, Myths, Mysteries was a very interesting class! We covered many different topics and had fun working together in class. Take this class for upper div LAH!

I actually took LAH 352E, Language Myths, Mysteries, and Truths. Great class. Work was straightforward. Class was mostly relaxed group discussion. Dr. Russi was great! Easy grader and class was really interesting. She was really funny and nice!
Very nice, knowledgeable and helpful. Not sure why some other students are whining. I had zero problems with her.

analysis.name: Jessica Ciarla
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great Professor!! Very Knowledgable!  Very fair, if something is unclear she does not penalize you for it. It's nice to hear about her personal experience in the fashion industry as she is very credible having years of experience in New York and owning her bridal shop in Austin. Makes class interesting with relevant fashion clips from youtube.

She understood you're new to the software and will give critiques and guidance if you ask. She doesn't bite. Grades pretty easily just do the work. Class takes a lot of time outside of hybrid meetings.

Very straight-forward classes. Lectures are usually always the same - her giving a powerpoint presentation, with some relevant video clips every few slides. It gets a little boring but she gives you everything you need for the test. VERY friendly and answers all questions. The only thing I didn't like was that class got repetitive.

One of the worst lecturers I have had at UT, un-engaging. Copies her powerpoint slides from the book and read them to us while standing in the same place. Assigns 5 point assignments in class which are a total waste of time. Constantly asks the class inane questions of obvious definitions.

analysis.name: Christian Claudel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor was pretty chill on many assignments, and his discussion times always provided help to work on the codes. I learned how to code in Python fairly easily in class and he was pretty helpful in office hours as well. Unfortunately, his exams shifted to in-person after our TA complained about the use of AI in assignments (excluding final).

The lectures were kinda boring but very helpful with homework and labs I would recommend watching them online at 2x speed. The tests switched from online to paper during the semester but they were still
Pretty easy. He went over the study guide the day before in class and I would recommend you go to that because it was very similar to the test.

Dr. Claudel is a very nice guy. It was my first time learning Python, but it was not as hard as I expected. He asked us for feedback on his lectures and how he could improve them. No attendance grade, but I would go to understand material and ask questions in person. Also it is helpful for the quizzes.

As someone who has never coded before, this class was my biggest nightmare. I learned nothing from it because the labs were so difficult that it felt like you had to have been coding for 3+ years to know what to do. Everything is basically open-note so you can get by if you need to, but I wanted to learn Python and ended up not being able to.

Dr. Claudel is a nice guy who does seem to care about his students and makes himself accessible in many ways, but he's not super great at teaching programming (Python, in my case) to people who have never done it before. The lab TAs were a godsend in this regard. Claudel is pretty funny and at least he made the lectures enjoyable.

analysis.name: Circe Sturm
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Sturm is clearly knowledgeable in her subject. But, she needs to explain things slower and more interestingly, keeping in mind that it's an online class and people can't reach her as easily. She tries to keep people in the loop by engaging in group chats and instapolls. The quizzes are easy.

This is a great course. Dr. Sturm is very organized, and the TAs are helpful. You'll need to study for the three midterms, and there's a project too. Keep up with Instapolls, and you can easily earn an A. The only reason I didn't earn an A is because of the midterms, so watch out!

Lectures are boring --- she just talks in circles and TA's are pretty bad (lacking basic canvas skills). Class is easy, all online prerecorded lectures with occasional instapolls. One project with a 2 page paper. There is extra credit opportunities (~2 points on final grade). Overall --- good class if you just need the credit and an easy A.

Professor Sturm is really nice and takes the time to explain vague concepts thoroughly which shows how genuinely interested she is in her field of work. There isn't too much work in the class right now and you basically only have to keep up with readings. Tests are manageable, but not as easy as you'd expect them to be. All multiple choice tests.

Dr. Strum talks in circles, her lectures tend to be boring and not coherent. They also used recycled lecture segments from a previous semester which was frankly negligent. This class is very content heavy, so only take it if you absolutely need it. One of her textbooks is completely irrelevant to the content of the class, which was vexing.

analysis.name: Cameron  Cler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She had mediocre lectures and loved explaining random Chinese things wrong. Doesn't grade until finals week even though class ends in like October, and even then the grading feels arbitrary. Never gave out a single 100 on an assignment, mostly gives 85s-90s. Attendance is a grade, even if you have an exam that falls during class hours. Mid.

Loved this professor! Even though the class was late in the day, it always flew by because she made the material so engaging. The assignments were straightforward and manageable, and I still walked away learning so much valuable information. Would definitely recommend taking this class with her if you get the chance!

I took Cameron for MKT 174 and she is such an amazing lecturer. She's one of the nicest people I've met at UT, so if you need a 1 hour course take this one!! participation is crucial to passing, but she tries to make each class enjoyable! Loved her!
Very good professor. Explains everything very well, would recommend the class. Also provides very good feedback.

analysis.name: John Clarke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor John Clarke teaches a performance work in his Modern American Art course that contains sexual assault, and he presented it without warning. When I emailed him that I was triggered by this piece, he asked me to tell him in person why it was triggering for me. I declined, and he put the piece on our midterm.

An utterly unpleasant man.  He has no quealms about treating you as though you don't deserve to be in the art history program.  So dictatorial that you wind up not being inspired enough to take anything away from what would otherwise be a compelling and useful class.

I enjoyed the subject matter and was very excited to give my own interpretation guided by the textbooks and readings. Unfortunately Clarke is the kind of professor who prefers that you regurgitate back to him exactly what he has written in his own books and anything that strays from that is considered highly subjective and wrong.

If you're taking this for a VAPA or upper division elective, do something else. He is rude and condescending, and makes little to no accommodations for ANY situation. His sensitive lecture topics (sex, gender, etc) were talked about as if they were a joke. If we didn't remember a specific thing from the reading he'd get angry and say we don't try.

Clarke is such a sweet guy! Not the most tech savvy. Clear lectures that go right along with the exams. Exams aren't hard at all, just need to watch the lectures and memorize the pieces. I never did the readings and got 96+ on all exams. Also some small writing assignments, but they're easy 100s. Go to class to succeed. Would love to take again.

analysis.name: Alexandra Clark
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I loved Dr. Clark's lecturing style and I can say that I learned quite a lot from her! I love that she is passionate about what she teaches and stands for what she believes in. However, I will say that the 3 exams are quite tricky, as they are long free responses. There is a lot of content discussed and no study guide/vague ideas of what to expect.

Dr. Clark is very condescending - when people ask questions in class she acts frustrated and as if the answer should be the most obvious thing in the world. I went to office hours once (Friday 8 AM only) to go over a test and ask for advice and she complained that students "just want to be spoon fed". The TAs were much more helpful.

The 3 exams that make up the majority of your grade require lots of studying, but are doable. She may seem intimidating, but is incredibly engaging and refreshingly honest about her views on what's happening in the US right now in relation to the course content. I learned so much and highly recommend her as a professor.

Dr. Clark's class is very informative. I learned so much about dementia and Alzheimer's. The lectures can be science heavy but she does a great job of explaining it so you shouldn't feel lost. There are 4 free response quizzes that can be a bit tricky so make sure to study ahead. But as long as you put in the work it's totally doable.

I enjoyed Professor Clark's class and learned a lot, and she can answer any question. She does present a lot of information but the way she lectures makes it easier to remember. Quizzes are doable if you keep up with lecture material.

analysis.name: Kevin Clarno
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Clarno is a groovy guy. He is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Concerning the class, if this is your first class on nuclear, it might be rough as there is a learning curve. Exams also are difficult but are graded on a curve so there is less pressure. Reason I am giving a four is because the class was too disorganized. Very swag beard.
Great guy, great class. Study with the slides... Tests are a challenge, but meant to stretch you

analysis.name: Gregory Clark
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I highly recommend taking this course for the UGS requirement. Dr. Clark is super cool and into what he is teaching. The course has some reading reflections, three essays, a group presentation, and an individual presentation. It is very interesting to learn about different plants and what they do. Compared to other UGS's this one is much better.

Dr. Clark is so chill and very understanding! He truly helps every student succeed in his lab, and he doesn't force anybody to do too much work each week! However, the partner system during first semester can get a little frustrating if you're stuck with a bad one, and he doesn't really use canvas, so it is hard to determine your grade!

Awesome professor. So nice and understanding, easy to talk to, cares about your learning while also making sure not to stress you out. His FRI stream is great and provides a great exposure to the basics of research.

Dr. Clark was absolutely amazing! His Hidden Treasures of Plants UGS was really eye-opening and a great learning experience. Discussions were very chill and essay assignments were not too much of a challenge. Dr. Clark was super understanding and spent time learning about his students. I enjoyed his class and learned a lot!

Dr. Clark is THE BEST! Such a sweet guy and is extremely passionate about his research! His lab is interesting but pretty laid back! Not work heavy and he's so forgiving and approachable! LOVE DR.CLARK AND HIS LAB!!!

analysis.name: Cole Holmes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is the easiest BA324 class. If you struggle with public speaking, this is the professor you want. Dr. Holmes is sweet, understanding, and takes a lot of the stress out of the class. He gives less assignments overall than the other professors, however like others have said he grades very last minute and doesn't teach you much.

Prof. Holmes is a very sweet man but does very little teaching. We had only 3 presentations and none were graded (never received any feedback at all on them); if you have presentation anxiety he is the best professor to take. You will not learn anything directly from him, rather everything you learn will be from the intensive capstone project.

Professor Holmes is very caring and understanding. He provides good feedback on the few assignments that we have, but you'll have to wait weeks before you get this feedback which can make the last month of class stressful. Capstone project is majority of your grade so start early.

Professor Holmes is my favorite business professor! He's caring, funny, and super supportive. His assignments aren't hard, but can be time-consuming. He shares amazing stories (and LOVES DIET COKE). If you need help, he's always there for you. His class is fun, engaging, and worth it—definitely TAKE HIM!

Such a sweet and funny professor. BA324 is all about presentations but he gives the least amount of presentations compared to other profs. He does has 2 exams but they are EXTREMELY easy. He takes WAY too long to grade but helps students when they ask for it. He goes off topic most of the time and talks a lot but is so funny.

analysis.name: Cory Reed
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Reed was a phenomenal lecturer. I can seriously say I wasn't ever bored at one of his lectures he made 400 year old book seem interesting. His class is homework heavy tho. Theres an assignment every week and multiple readings throughout out the week as well. His class is manageable as long as you stay on top of the readings.

Professor Reed is a great teacher. He is extremely passionate about this subject. He is a very lenient grader, and he changed the syllabus several times, including take home exams, more allowed absences, extensions, and an opt-out option for the last exam to make it easier on students. I would take his course again, in a heartbeat.

He understands that students are busy and he makes the course structure forgiving. He repeats important concepts multiple times so you're familiar with them by the exam. If you go to class, do the assigned readings, and make an effort, the class is rewarding. He's friendly and passionate about what he teaches.

He's passionate about the material, making him a fantastic lecturer. You can miss three classes, so attendance is crucial. Goes over required reading in class which is extremely helpful. Majority of homework can be completed in class and he's very accessible for office hours. The exams are take-home. It's a pretty easy A if you don't half-ass it.

Probably one of my favorite classes I've taken at UT, just because the content is so interesting and rich. If you attend the lectures in person, you'll have a very smooth time; Prof. Reed gives great explanations of the poems and ballads read in class, and breaks it down into ways that are much easier to understand than what's seen at face value.

analysis.name: Desmond Coles
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: very chill guy. however, lectures can be pretty monotonous and he teaches straight from the textbook. attendance wasn't mandatory for lectures but one quiz in discussion weekly which was pretty manageable. my advice is skip the lectures and learn from the textbook in your own time. tests are easier than hw and have a bonus question.

Chill guy, good teacher. Hw typically takes anywhere between 0.5-3 hrs per week, don't procrastinate. Show up to lectures even if you took AP, b/c theres content not taught in AP thats taught here.(I'm not talking about multivariable). 65% of your grade comes from the exams. Feel free to ask questions, although he can ramble on a bit when answering

My favorite professor during Fall '25. He really knows his subject and can teach it well. He answers questions thoughtfully and explains concepts thoroughly (how particular formulas are derived) so that we understand better. Gave useful homework problems, practice exams, straightforward quizzes/exams, and had a bonus question on exams. 10/10 prof.

Amazing Calc Professor. Homework and quizzes are similar to tests. Tests aren't hard if you truly know the material. Lectures move fast but are insightful. He knows SO much about the field and is genuinely interested. 65% of grade based on tests. Quizzes in discussion. DO THE HOMEWORK! He really emphasizes it for good reason. Amazing professor!

Desmond Coles is an excellent professor with lots of knowledge about his course. It's not absolutely necessary to read the textbook before the lecture, because he will explain EVERYTHING in the lecture. 
However, it is crucial to not skip classes. Also just a chill guy, he's always wearing hats.

TLDR: don't skip class, do half the homework before

analysis.name: Renita Coleman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor is very familiar and passionate about the subject, which makes lessons interesting. The exams make up 60%, but most questions are common sense aside from some hyper-specific examples, which test reviews from professor and TA's mention. Not an extremely easy UGS and had to spend hours studying/doing homework. TA's grade the 6 essays hard.

This class was really easy, most of your grade comes from 3 tests that were all super easy if you went to the discussion test reviews. There were also six one page papers throughout the semester, but were honestly all fun to write (also two got dropped so you only have to do 4). The lectures were probably fun if you are interested in pop culture

Part I. First of all, I hated this class. As a pop culture enthusiast who was raised into this field and developed my identity though it, the curriculum satisfied me and accurately portrayed every single pop culture event which filled me with nostalgia but boredom. Professor Coleman is well-spoken but often stutters and loses her train of thought.

Absolutely loved Dr. Coleman! She's very passionate and funny. This class is very interesting and in my opinion pretty chill. Class is TA heavy, and your grade depends heavily on your TA. Shout out to my TA Carlos Byrd! He was the best, and made me enjoy the class and subject more. Would 100% take again.

Coleman tries her best to set you up for success - she gives you all the materials you need to do well. Who your TA is matters alot - they are the ones giving you reviews before the tests and grading your discussion papers. There are definitely other better UGS courses than this one - don't make this your first choice.

analysis.name: Alan  Covey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Covey is a great, underappreciated professor. His class is interesting, but a little too dull for me as someone who isn't into science. This is a lecture heavy class, there is a book but I never used is and still managed. He gives a GREAT review making the exam easy as expected. This is a class with a lab, helping towards overall grade.

I had Dr. Covey for Cultures in Contact. Good professor, VERY knowledgeable on the topics at hand, and he'll very readily answer any extra questions you may have. But it's a flipped class. It's too easy to just skim through the outside work and zone out in class (attendance measured with Squarecap). Lectures not on test, homeworks only.

I really liked his UGS! His lectures are kinda boring, but then he's really sweet and cares a lot about his students! This class is an easy A-I would just do the questions that he gave us w/ each reading(since the Monte Carlo quizzes are based on that, and you can access your notes). He WANTS you to get an A.

Covey is potentially one of the sweetest teachers at UT. Took this class solely for some needed flags and learned a lot about anthro. TA Blaire was unfortunately unhelpful and graded papers at the last second and harshly. A lot of assigned reading for Monte Carlo quizzes but most readings are short and you're able to use notes on them

Taking this class online was the best thing I can do. I can easily replay his lectures to fill out the given outlines and then do quizzes. Instapolls with every video but easy to complete. Extra credit lab is the best, boosted my grade by 5%.

analysis.name: Thomas Connolly
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Beware of trolls rating this professor; he is not that great. For a Dynamics Physics course, a 95 and above is an A! (For reference, his test average was a 68, and no curve was given). In other words, it's extremely difficult to earn an A in the class. A 90 is a B+! He doesn't even teach well and will not post any notes (so you're on your own).

If you have ADHD prepare to self teach. All he does for lecture is give in class exercises with minimal instruction, let us work on it, then explain the solution. Least engaging lecture I've ever had. Tests (2 mid 1 final) are 25% each, no curve, took over a month to return 1st midterm. +1 to the other recent reviews; don't trust the positive ones

His lecturing style is one of the worst out there. He does not explain things well & relies on his students learning from "in-class exercises." The TAs were also so unhelpful. Most questions were answered as "I don't know, to be honest." The exams were nothing like what we had during quizzes, and they were super late at 8-10 pm on Thursday nights.

Difficult but caring professor. He is very sweet but I found it hard to take what I learnt in the lecture to an exam. I often had to look for other practice problems apart from his own to feel prepared. His extra credit is ~1 % added to your final grade (5 pts bonus for course evals) so dont be counting on it for anything.

95 for an A. The 'curve' you get is 4-8 bonus points added to your lowest exam (which all weigh the same) meaning a 1-2% grade boost. Kind Professor, but avoid. Stopped uploading solutions to his work after a few weeks in. Never have felt so unprepared going into exams, which the worst is NOT dropped despite the 95+ for an A. Non-cumulative final.

analysis.name: Clint Tuttle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 190 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Have you ever watched a Kia or Hyundai commercial and think to yourself "Oh Wow amazing car!" Then after owning it for a few weeks realize a few things? Let me save you some time. Really, would not take again.
Brilliant Entertaining lectures. Horrible, infuriating assignments. 5-mile treadmill-boring articles.

HANDS DOWN one of the best professors at UT. The readings aren't that bad as some make it out to be. Tuttle has a panache for story telling and keeps lectures fresh and exciting. He teaches applications of excel and makes the material easy to understand and keeps you interested. I definitely left Tuttle's class feeling prepared for the real world.

Great guy 10/10. If you get the chance to take professor Tuttle you definitely should! He wants his students to do well. Seriously, he is very fair and helpful with all the material. He knows some students might struggle with excel but trust me when I say he knows you'll use it in the future. You will! Fun class and this is one class you'll want!

Clint Tuttle is a UT LEGEND!!! This guy is freaking awesome and if you don't take him, you're missing out on one of the best classes UT has to offer. You'll hear fantastic stories during class and his presentations is something all professors should learn from. He prepares you for the real world with excel. HW isn't bad and its doable. TAKE HIM!

analysis.name: Craig Linder
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: MANY advised against him, but he really isn't bad. To be honest, I dont think I've ever learned more, (objectives are key for exam), but still his grading is hard. Exams: 1: 83, 2: 84, 3: 81, 4: 84. So in all you can get an A- with 80s, just do every homework (not that many), do every journal entry (easy points), quiz average was about 13/15.

Don't listen to the ratings on here. Just go to class and actually pay attention. I recommend rewatching the lectures and paying attention to the examples. The learning objectives are super helpful and the exams are basically written from them. It is a lot but things make sense if you actually try to understand. He is super nice and I LOVED him.

DONT take if u have another option. kirkpatrick was ok but exams r niche + only 1 exam was curved. linders section is frustrating bc lectures are awk, quizzes are strict, & the exam curve only helped lower scores more & did nothing for higher scores. disc grading is bs since participation doesn't seem to count unless u directly answered a question

Extremely unaccommodating. Missed one of the quizzes due to a medical emergency, which I had multiple doctor's notes and billing receipts from. Linder refused to let me take the quiz 1 day late, so I received a 0. Exam questions are graded on a specific phrases that the questions do not prompt. Does not want his students to succeed.

DONT take if u have another option. kirkpatrick was ok but exams r niche + only 1 exam was curved. linders section is frustrating bc lectures are awk, quizzes are strict, & the exam curve only helped low scores more & did nothing for higher scores. disc grading is bs since participation doesn't seem to count unless u directly answered a question

analysis.name: Kelley Crews
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: do NOT take this class. the assignments are super easy but they are graded incredibly hard by the professor and the TAs. The professor is super judgemental and tries to justify the horrible grades for the easy assignments and also does not have neutral political views, which even if you agree with you still get a bad vibe about her attitude.

This class really just frustrates me. Never give a rubric for our quizzes and don't really know what to expect for them. TAs and professor is really unclear and claim for it to be super easy but the tests get really specific things gone over in lecture.

This class was an EXTREMELY easy A. You just have to show up for the super random attendance checks and write one essay a week (500 words) which is graded so easily I would write the morning they were due and get a 100. However, Dr. Crews is very zany and scatterbrained. She goes off on massive tangents and class can be exhausting to sit through.

The class as a whole was the easiest thing ever. You have to go to class for the random attendance checks and the only other grades are weekly 500 word essays that take like 10 minutes to write. Overall, super easy A. However, I hated Professor Crews with a passion. She is condescending and impresses her beliefs upon students which IS NOT okay.

she missed 2 weeks which made the course very unorganized. your grade literally depends on your TA's grading and its very inconsistent. you never get feedback so you never know what you did wrong. quizzes(4) were short confusing. she dropped the lowest quiz for us but honestly take another class. it wasnt worth it. we watched like 10 movies overall

analysis.name: Michelle Crabtree
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Michelle was great for an entry-level class. I had her 4-6 pm, and for being such a late and long class, she kept us actively engaged. She taught us a lot of dialectical differences and has a lot of experience teaching languages. I struggle a lot in school and she helped me feel more confident.

Prof Crabtree does very well at managing her personal life with her graduate studies and the classes she teaches! She goes above and beyond teaching wise and offers some immersion experiences (ie brought gazpacho to class)! I hate the Spanish dept at UT, but she made this class more than tolerable and goes the extra mile to make up for its faults.

Michelle cares for her students and goes above and beyond to ensure everyone is understanding the content. She answers questions without condescension and enthusiastically. If you have never taken Spanish before, the content will be difficult with any professor, but I wholeheartedly recommend Michelle.

analysis.name: Megan Crowhurst
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This prof isn't the worst but complicated. At first she is nice, but then I realized she uses rhetorical devices to single out people she didn't like. It made it tough to learn anything, trying to constantly sift through her maze of points to figure out what was important or not. Her grading reflects a corporate agenda not correctness. I'd avoid.

She really knew her stuff about everything that she taught, didn't use notes at all. Super interested in the topic, and had a clear and effective learning plan for the class. It was definitely worth the time.

This class is not that hard but is still harder than most other UGS classes. I don't think it's worth it to take this class. Dr. Crowhurst is nice but unclear with her grading scale and lectures are interesting at times (and on zoom) but not enough to outweigh the negatives. If you end up taking the class, make sure you talk in class to get an A.

This class was pretty interesting, Dr. Crowhurst is really passionate about what she is teaching. You do have a term paper and a group presentation, but they aren't really all that bad, you do have a lot of time for them. Overall this class wasn't all that difficult.
She's pretty nice, but honestly, I was bored in the lectures. It's kind of a tedious course, but the material is fairly easy to master. Homework was imo much harder than tests.

analysis.name: Alison Craig
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: funny and overall sweet professor but can be disorganized at times. that issue sort of goes away once you enter the simulation. TAs can be nitpicky with grading but that is usually offset by EC points offered during the simulation; go for a leadership position!

Dr Craig is a GEM. The mock senate simulation may seem daunting but it is actually easy to earn participation points. I had a health crisis and she was very understanding and worked out a way for me to get more credit to make up for what I missed. Okay so she may not be the most organized person lol but she's so funny and fantastic. Take her class!

Lectures first half of semester and then attendance matters for second half (the simulation). Lectures are common sense, and she just rambles, so not really necessary to show up. Simulation is fun and attendance goes toward your participation grade for these days. Extra credit offered. If you don't end this class with an A+, that's your fault.

Dr. Craig is awesome! Her class is taught as a senate simulation, but she takes from her immense knowledge to support students in the class. There are 6 total assignments, one of which is an exam that's based on her lectures - which are funny and helpful. You'll want to attend class, especially in the simulation, but the classes are lots of fun!

Took US Congress with Prof. Craig. Class is largely based off of a senate simulation, where participation is important. She gives lectures that are funny but also can seem somewhat unorganized. There are 6 assignments including 1 exam, all of which are easy to do well on if you pay attention in class. Overall a fun and easy class and professor.

analysis.name: Craig Campbell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class I took isn't on the list here. Dr. Campbell is one of my favorite professors. He cares deeply about the students and the course material. The class was more-discussion based, and he gave really insightful input. There are a lot of readings, but they're manageable, interesting, and very helpful to the big final project. Really cool class.

the professor would also always talk in circles and the pop quizzes were torture because even though I did all the required reading, the questions were always the most obscure random quote from page 3 line 4 from some book about some white guy studying people of color and then going and publishing a book about it for more white people to read

Professor Campbell is a wonderful and smart professor.  His lectures are pretty fun, he likes using technology.  Be prepared to talk a lot, he encourages students to be active talkers.  Be prepared to spent around $100 in his "the photographic image class" you will need to print a lot.  Grades are based on 2 presentations, 7 projects, participation

Honestly, I found his lectures to be boring. He would read material straight from the textbook. The videos that he played were cool, though. Attendance was mandatory due to the in-person quizzes. The discussion section was the only interesting part of the class, and my TA was more engaging than this professor.

Professor Campbell's ANT302 class was not difficult. He is super chill and a really cool professor, but his lectures are very wordy and theoretical. Someone said the same thing below but if you're not on the same wavelength as him, lectures are a bit hard to follow sometimes. Interesting class

analysis.name: Rowena Crabbe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor, she is extremely thorough with lectures and truly cares about the subject. HOWEVER, I would not recommend this as a UGS course simply because it requires SO MUCH WORK and you are better off in an easier one. We had reflections due weekly, all requiring a ton of reading (mainly academic articles that were hard to understand).

I LOVE DR. CRABBE!!! Yes, there is some reading and weekly reflections. However, Dr. Crabbe does her best to make it accesible and there's plenty of time to complete. She is genuinely so knowledgeable, and you'll leave with such a rich understanding and curiosity of marketing. TAKE THIS CLASS- you won't regret it.

Dr. Crabbe is an excellent professor, she explains things in such a clear way and makes you feel like your opinion matters. This isn't a blow off UGS, but still light work. It was genuinely one of my favorite courses this year because the content you learn and talk about matters. Highly recommend

Dr. Crabbe's Influence of Marketing in Society course was one of the most thought-provoking, enlightening, and engaging classes I've taken at UT. Each lecture functions as a time to discuss readings, and participation is a big part of your grade, but Dr. Crabbe makes it easy to do so! The amount of reading also lightens up throughout the semester.

Dr. Crabbe was the best professor I could've asked for. Her assignments were challenging but impactful, especially with the amount of time to submit each paper. It may feel like a lot of writing and reading at times, but her care and knowledge for what it's like to be a student makes her 1 of 1. Would definitely recommend, just be ready to read!

analysis.name: Cristine Legare
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The lectures are an open discussion with the class; there are no lecture slides. The lectures did not have relevance to the exam, we had to learn everything on our own. There are a total of 6 essay exams and a final essay exam all in person without notes. There would randomly be group projects that were not on the syllabus. Class was not organized.

There are 6 exams 3-4 questions each: 1 pg essay per. Questions release 2-3 days before. Exam time was shortened from 90 to 75 mins 
This class killed any interest in the subject. The textbook is disorganized, the professor doesn't lecture, and exams are impossible to write to the prof's standards for all 4 questions in the given time.

Lectures are almost completely unrelated to exams, but attendance is mandatory. She never gave a rubric for essay exams, and for our 15-page term paper, the format requirements (changed margins and we all lost 1-2 pages) were changed a week before the due date. Nice woman and seemed to care about the course topic, just a little lazy unfortunately.

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Legare is a very nice person and she's very highly educated in her field, however attendance was mandatory so if you took one day off your grade would go down, she threw random assignments at us then later told us it was for extra credit, and the TA grades the exams harshly. Very insightful class but not the best I'd say.

Do not take this class. 6 exams, and you will literally never get comments on your exams or how to improve on your essays.  You wont even get your last exam grade back until you are already taking the next exam.  TA is a horrible and harsh grader for no reason.  You are never told what they are expecting for the exams so it is impossible to do well

analysis.name: Cristina Maymí
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: of course, spanish at UT is going to be a heavy course load. maymi makes it to where you feel supported throughout the course. took her over summer and during that my father passed away. she made it to where she was flexible with not only my work during that time but always checked in to make sure my mental was good as well. take her if you can!

I cannot express enough gratitude for Señora Maymí. I took SPN 610 last semester (not listed here), and her class was super engaging. Thanks to her support and recommendation letter, I got to study abroad in Spain and traveled around Europe. She's an amazing professor who continues to support her students even after the semester ends.

She's literally the sweetest professor ever! She genuinely wants you to learn Spanish, not just pass. Yeah, the class is a LOT of work, but she's incredibly supportive, and by the end, you'll actually know Spanish. I had a tough time toward the end of the semester, but was able to pull through and pass. We seriously need more profs like her. 10/10.

This professor was kind and you could tell really wanted to see her students succeed. She was flexible with late assignments and very understanding. This class was hard, but she made it easy because she's an amazing professor. This course load is heavy, but again, she was so helpful.

analysis.name: Ann Cvetkovich
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Material and readings 4 me were very interesting so long as u care about the topics. At times lectures felt somewhat contrived, but overall they were engaging and interesting. Essays are graded somewhat harshly but the feedback provided is helpful. I wouldn't say the class is an "free" A, but if u have a passion for LGBTQ+ issues it's a great class

She wasn't a very good lecturer, so the class would just be her talking nonstop about random things, and it was super boring. She was very rude and got mad easily. Don't even try emailing her, she NEVER answers. Her TA Gabriel was very harsh in grading. It seemed like they both didn't like each other & didn't want to be there. Syllabus unclear.

Dr. Cvetkovich is very passionate about her class but it doesn't necessarily translate into having an interesting class. The graduate TA, Gabriel, is a very harsh grader with vague rubrics so it's slightly hard to make an A. The field trips are interesting but a little irrelevant to the class. The readings are long & slightly boring & repetitive.

The content was interesting, but the lectures did seem to drag on, and the TA is not very nice. The grading was a bit harsh, depending on whether you got the TA or the professor as your grader. I would recommend taking this class if you have a genuine interest in the material rather than just for the credit.

Dr. Ann is an excellent professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable in her field and provides great feedback on assignments. Many experiential learning opportunities, which is very enjoyable. She appreciates honest participation and encourages questions. Course load is easy to manage, would recommend for UGS!

analysis.name: Robert Crosnoe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pretty easy and something you can put on the side. Discussion post every week and a short quiz over the lecture (3-5 questions that can range from 5-15minutes). A couple of papers, but the lectures are enjoyable to watch, and you can find them very relatable in your day-to-day life.

Crosnoe is the GOAT. Super sweet, pretty funny, and actually wants to get to know his students despite being online. Essays are so light. Quizzes get a little challenging at times, but it's nothing crazy. Biggest advice: go to his office hours! We talked about Hobbes for like 10 minutes and it was great! + he'll help you out w/ your grade if you go

Professor Crosnoe is a nice guy and I enjoyed talking to him one-on-one. My only issue is that I found it pretty difficult for me to focus in class during the lectures (which were live streamed). There is quite a bit of reading as well as quizzes and discussions for almost every class, but nothing too hard. Not a bad class overall :)

Sweet guy. 3 big papers due throughout the semester plus quizzes at the beginning of every class, instapolls, and chats for participation. The papers are pretty easy honestly you don't really need to pay attention to be able to do them and they don't grade super hard. You have to go in person once for participation credit. Didn't need the textbook.

The class itself is completely online, there are quizzes and participation discussions every class but very easy. He also gives instapolls during class, but not for a grade, just to see if you are paying attention. There are three main assignments during the curriculum, but he grades them very easily. Overall, the guy cares about your well-being.

analysis.name: Douglas Cushing
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cushing is difficult to work with and creates a stressful classroom environment. He is quick to raise academic integrity concerns and refer you to SCAI without clearly communicating reasoning or providing sufficient context. If you take this class, be extremely cautious, and keep detailed records of everything you submit.

Dr. Cushing is very enthusiastic about this course and cares a lot about students- he makes lots of fun extra-credit opportunities through the semester. His lectures move quickly and cover a lot so take notes and do the heading ahead of time to not get lost. Tests are open note and the study guides are really helpful.

He's ridiculously smart and very knowledgeable on like everything history related. He's big on participation and discussions for his smaller classes. My course had a lot of readings and writing but check the syllabus cuz that not true for all of his classes. A good professor but his lectures are very wordy.

Not many assignments, but the ones that we had were not too easy, and not graded too easily either. 2 exams. Weekly HW "quizzes", but aren't bad. Lectures are really long, and he does not stop talking throughout. Meet once a week w/ TA, which was nice to get to talk to people about the class. Overall, not super hard, but it is a lot of content.

Decent VAPA. Yes, some assignments can be annoying if you're just looking to get your VAPA out of the way and don't care for art history, but quizzes/tests are easy—this class is a GPA booster (not honor-locked as of this semester). He's a genuine and knowledgeable professor, and TAs are understanding. Fast-paced lectures, not required though.

analysis.name: James Curley
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 98 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Although the lectures cumulatively are quite long and drag at times, he thoroughly explains each concept to ensure comprehension. Ive never had such a thorough professor tbh. I had no background in stats/coding, yet I didn't find the material too difficult due to the profundity with which he explained it. He's also super likable, imo.

Each week you have multiple videos to help you with an open book untimed quiz to do. This class will only take up 1 day in your week. He gives out tons of extra credit for small things. I thought learning statistics would be hard, but this class made is so manageable. Great class, very organized, and great professor and lecture videos.

this class will take up about one full day of your week for lecture content and test. only one test a week typically 15-20 questions open notes. Curley is definitely a s sweet guy and would recommend. he went out of his way to make sure we were set up for the class extra credit was also given throughout the semester.

Dr. Curley was wonderful! Highly recommend going to OH; he gives full explanations if you get stuck. It's all quizzes, but they're untimed & pretty straightforward. I personally found the material super easy, but there's usually replacement grades if needed. Textbook isn't needed but a good resource with Ctrl+F. Overall, a lowkey class & simple A!

Loved Dr. Curley! Anyone who says otherwise is lying to you!! He's super helpful + his TAs, and even though the class is online, he is very helpful when it comes to asking him questions. His class was pretty chill, basically just a quiz every week & no tests!! Loved his class, just familiarize yourself with R & R Studio! Lots of resources too!

analysis.name: Henry Curtis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I honestly think for his first time teaching it really wasn't too bad. He was kind of rude and sassy at times and the course is strictly based off of tests. The tests were worded weirdly, and though he says that attendance was required, he took it ONCE. He would go off into tangents and I would get lost, so this course is pretty much self taught.

Attendance was mandatory but never taken except on TXOU weekend. Lectures were dull, off topic, and he often sat on his phone during group work. Exams had bad multiple-choice but okay short answers. He tries to make an intro class harder than it needs to be and said, "philosophy is as hard as chemical engineering". Overall a childish professor.

This class is very interesting if you are interested in thinking about how certain political/social problems in today's world work and how different ethical theories can be applied to them. There are about 3 weekly readings. There are 3 tests and they aren't too difficult as long as you understand the readings and attend lectures.

Extremely chill, accessible outside of class, very accommodating and did a fairly decent job at explaining readings. Lectures could get a little dry. He never actually took attendance tho and it was often difficult to participate because he sometimes goes off on tangents. Do the readings, sit front row and go to office hours.

I really enjoyed having Henry as a professor. His lectures were very funny, and his office hours were quite helpful. There was a decent amount of reading, but it was never impossible to manage. Our grade was made up of 3 exams and participation, which causes some pressure, but if you attend every lecture and do the readings you'll succeed.

analysis.name: Joe Cutbirth
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Really enjoyed lying and deception with Cutbirth. Class consists of weekly quizzes over the reading and 3 easy interview projects. Material itself is really interesting and Cutbirth allows for a lot of discussion (though not required). Attendance isn't tracked but he is a knowledgeable guy with a lot of cool experience so it's worth going.

A lot of writing (no exams) and a group project at the end. Not hard and a lot of flexibility with the "hybrid." The professor went out of his way to take some unconventional approaches with readings and "leaders," and that was cool. He's good to meet up with in office hours, too.

Worst class I've taken at this University. He makes the weekly quizzes very deceptive and tricky. Lectures are vague. Honestly I didn't know how to win and make a good grade in this class. I did all the readings and went to all the classes and couldn't make a good grade.

Super nice guy very straight forward. Take him literally when he tells you how things are done. He isn't very flexible on make-ups and excused absences. Has a great career with a lot of practical experience. See him in his office. He likes knowing who you are and what your interests are. And he will go out of his way to help if you're struggling.

I took both classes. Pretty informal but his standards are high. Quizzes  mini-exams with stuff from books but not lectures. He posts slides BEFORE the lectures, lets you drop two quiz grades and gives a good midterm and final review. Go to his office hours, but beware he can be a little chatty. Fake News was my favorite course yet at UT.

analysis.name: Milica Cudina
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Cudina is an amazing professor! She is very caring for her students and her lectures are very comprehensive. Her notes are also very easy to read and are posted after each lecture on her website. Her tests can be a bit tricky but very doable. She also offered extra credit this semester and the assignment was very interesting. Would take again!

One of the nicest professors that I've ever taken. Super nice with everyone and helpful beyond measure,extremely conciderative as well. The class context is very difficult though If you really want to understand the class as she sort of expects you to have a general understanding beforehand, but getting a high grade isn't hard

The class covered some good content, and the majority of our grade was made up of the 3 midterms and optional final. She provides practice tests that give you a clear indication of what to expect for the actual exams..being able to solve those is a good indicator for how well you will do on the actual exams. The homework is challenging however.
Lectures were hard to follow, homework was really difficult, projects took a while, and exams were hard to prepare for. Still, she is the sweetest person on the planet.

I took her for M 378K and M 362K, but same rating for both. Very caring and friendly professor! M 362K is good Exam P prep, too. But do note that you will need to put a lot more time into the homework assignments. Not a free A, but you learn a lot even if you walk out with an A-. P.S. Free fruit snacks at her office hours :3

analysis.name: Molly Cummings
