analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Discussion section attendance mandatory (otherwise, lectures are optional). Botero and Cummings were both great lecturers, although only Botero provided study guides for the exams. The TA, Brittany, was very helpful throughout the course. Tests comprise ~80% of final grade. Exams mostly short-answer and fill-in-the-blank, class avg mid- to high-B.

I do not usually review, but she was the rudest person ever for no reason. This class was SO MUCH HARDER than it had to be. Attendance was optional but not rlly. Maybe people would come in person if she wasnt so mean and passive aggressive about it and cold calling on students who look confused. She didn't accept my accommodations?? Is that legal?

Dr. Cummings is so nice and always in good spirits. I took the class online bc covid so it may have been easier than normal. Tests were open note so I barely studied and did well. 1/4 of grade is a group research project where we were not given a rubric. There was a presentation and then a paper. I despise both research and writing but was fine

I love animal behavior but Dr. Hutchins/Dr.Cummings made it extremely difficult. their tests were way too broad and detail-heavy with some of the things never even mentioned in lecture. They don't even provide practice problems or even a study guide. Also complains about people not attending lecture when they are so uninteractive. Do better.

She seems to be a well-respected expert in the fish behavior world. Her lectures aren't confusing but they are dense with content, which can be hard for non-neuro majors. The content she emphasized the most in lecture was not tested on the exam, rather it was on minor/less-focused details. She does not provide practice problems nor practice exams.

analysis.name: Erin Cunningham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Is overall a very skilled and caring teacher. I'm not a fan of sculpture, but I enjoyed learning new techniques and hearing her opinions in crit. Her class requires participation, but has a chill atmosphere and she'll check in on you to see if she can help with anything. Would definitely recommend.

Core class taken for studio art major, no way around it, but I appreciate Erin. She's pretty chill and even when I thought a student was being very disrespectful towards her she just laughed and went along with it. I personally don't like sculpture too much but I still found enjoyment in the projects and her critique for everyone thoughtful.

Erin is the best! I took her Sculpture for Nonmajors class. There were 3 projects (found-object, wood, and metal), and Erin really wanted to help us make pieces that we liked. Overall, a very fun, engaging, and informative class. I would recommend it to anyone.

analysis.name: Cynthia Penwell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great prof with field experience, but totally disorganized. Extensive weekly papers and a ton of readings she never touches on during lectures. She does mix students up A LOT and does not seem to know who is who. Besides that, she is an OG who also works in the field while teaching and is a brutally honest person, which is rare, and I appreciate.

Professor Penwell is ok. You will have weekly reflections due on Sundays, which you can begin writing only at the end of the week because you need the entire week's lectures to complete it. Rubrics aren't always clear. Shes definitely knowledgeable in her field, but just beware of the many writing assignments youll do compared to other professors.

Long weekly papers with no rubric and harsh grading. Only 2 allowed absences. She is not understanding yet is literally a SW professor. She mixes up students' names of the same race. She is so hard to work with. By far my most time consuming, repetitive class. DISORGANIZED! You will have to suffer for an A. DO NOT BE FOOLED BY THE HIGH RATING!

She's very respected and knows what she's talking about because she is so experienced in the social work field. She's very funny and kind. She is willing to work with those who have personal issues, and the class is mostly based on papers and a group project as well as attendance. LOVED her! One of the best professors I've had.

Penwell is a great, very caring, compassionate professor. I recommend taking her, she is truly interested in her students. Class does have a lot of tedious assignments, though, but I do learn a lot. Weekly papers, service learning requirement, and a big dyad project, which was interesting and you learn a lot, but you roleplay in front of the class.

analysis.name: Cynthia Marentes
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor is highly critical of students. While she gives feedback on all presentations (there are multiple), she always finds things to deduct points for. Her critique is subjective, even if you argue your points, she is unlikely to give you your points back. You will not receive a 100 on any presentation. Just take it online.

I took Prof. Marentes for Professional Comm. Studies in the spring semester of 2024 and she was amazing! There are quizzes after each chapter that are open notes, lots of presentations, and class participations. This class definitely helped me improve my presentation and communication skills. I thoroughly enjoyed her class and would take it again!
This class was interesting, no assignments were hard BUT she did grade hard.....

analysis.name: Cynthia Labrake
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 129 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Basically, if you do homework on Canvas and go to class, this class isn't that hard. There is online polling that happens during class, but you can do that at home if you need to. Because of this, technically you don't need to go to class but I would suggest it. She's a pretty good teacher, even with the 200+ students class.

The structure of the course was changed this year to 8 exams, which causes you to spend more time studying throughout the entire semester. There is work for essentially every class. Labrake herself is quite scattered, requiring you to learn outside of class. However, her and especially Albert's reviews are worth going to and will help you on exams.

LaBrake is one of the best chem professors in the department. Her lectures are super engaging and she knows what she's talking about. She goes a little fast so you really have to do the homework ahead of time, otherwise you won't understand what's going on. She has a few options for bonus points on tests, so look out for those opportunities.

To even call her a professor I've had is a bit much since she used videos over a year old full of errors recorded at odd hours and videos she liked from youtube that replaced her lectures. I feel she tries to claim this is part of 'self-directed learning', but I feel there's a difference between encouraging learning and not teaching.

I learn by seeing the problem done step by step and explained why things are a certain way, but she does the problem on her own and I never know what I am doing. The textbook to me was not helpful at all. Goes too fast on the powerpoint and barley goes on a topic when all of a sudden she's on another.

analysis.name: Todd Curtis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 337 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: This class got so much harder this semester. Long tophat homeworks, insane amount of reading, lectures are rushed, and exams worth 70% of your grade that are graded extremely harshly by TA's. Way too much work and stress for a VAPA. Very hard to get an A.

I agree that Dr. Curtis is very knowledgeable about mythology but the readings are just a killing. I stopped reading all together and just took detailed notes of his lectures, I mean word for word of what he was saying. He gives assignments with all possible questions and I would just memorize the answers and my essays. Too much work for LAC credit

He recently changed the format of the class. You will have to memorize 200-300 words for each exam. Exams are every other Monday, so your Sundays will have to be dedicated to studying. There's so much homework that is lengthy and difficult, and his powerpoints are useless. I have a 3.9 GPA and this is the hardest, worst class I have taken at UT.

Good class to meet a flag if you need one! 4 tests for 80% and cumulative tophat for 80% of the final grade. Tests (which were directly from worksheets he posts for every lecture) consist of MC (20%), short answer (30%), and one essay (50%). Attendance isn't mandatory but he goes into detail in the lecture that you wouldn't get if you skipped.

Everything is based on the lectures, so if you don't go you're going to fail regardless of whether you read the textbook or not. The TA was beyond obnoxious and rude - thought she knew everything. I had high hopes for Curtis, but he wasn't very responsive nor did he seem to care about his students grades.

analysis.name: Cynthia Talbot
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Talbot is a terrible teacher. Graded one of my assignments without her laid out rubric and instead by how much she liked the paper. The tests and quizzes have no relation to what you learn in class and requires extra prep for tests. If you're looking for an easy A, this isn't it. Too many assignments . She was often unsure on her history info

Dr. Talbot is a very good professor, the history course of the premodern world is very interesting, tests are in essay form, and both the professor and TA give good feedback. But reading, attending class, and paying attention to class and test preparation are very useful and important. Overall, very good professor.

Dr. Talbot is kind, intelligent, and she really cares about her students. She posts readings that will help you better understand, in-class review sessions before exams, extra office hours around exams, and she always helps out the best she can. Very fair. Great professor. I recommend.

analysis.name: Natalie Czimskey
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I LOVED taking Dr.Czimskey's class. She also has the "Longhorn Friday" where, if ALL class wears burnt orange on Friday, she will bring either treats next class or add extra points. She will also allow you to give burnt orange items to classmates before class. She is very funny during lecture and you have access to all ppt. on Canva.WILL take again

She is amazing as always, phonetics content is very overwhelming at first but makes sure her students fully grasp the info. Her and her TA are very easy to reach outside of class and will help you in anyways they can. She makes sure we get the printed out version of the lectures and I think it helps a lot more than typing it out on a computer!

sweetest professor ever! I look forward to her classes every week. Easy to get in contact with, inclusive with all students, explains material in a way that's easy to understand. Love going to office hours and just chatting with her! Would definitely take any and all of her classes again.

EXTREMELY caring and accessible prof. Attendance isn't mandatory. All tests are online and not monitored (she respects our privacy and trusts students not to cheat). I am not an SLHS major, but she made the class fun. Also, an optional final to replace the lowest test grade. Only con is that there's very few assignments outside of the tests.

Great option to take as a science core class, even if you aren't an SLH major. Dr. Czimskey is funny, engaging, and is truly passionate about her field. Make sure to take notes in class as the slides don't cover everything you need to know. Very helpful in office hours if any guidance is needed.

analysis.name: Devin Stauffer
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: OK, so Dr. Stauffer is a really interesting, fun, intelligent professor. He is a fair grader, expects a lot of his students, but provides ample opportunities to make a good grade. He does stutter a bit, which can be annoying at times. Side note: If Mr. Weasley and Chandler Bing had a love-child, that child would look just like Dr. Stauffer.

he's so funny and super cool. just very lecture heavy, just make sure to read. he gives pop quizzes but he lets you know when the quizzes will be before he gives them. he doesnt ask for participation because a lot of people always talk. take him, hes cool

Be prepared to buy lots of books and read before every single class. The readings were a little hard on their own but with the lectures, they became a little fun! Prof. Stauffer was an amazing lecturer and tried to make it easy to understand. Consisted of 2 papers and pop quizzes. Also offered a lot of extra credit which was super appreciated.

Stauffer is one of the best political theory professors here. He explains complex topics simply & provides many opportunities for grade improvement like quizzes, optional papers & SI sessions (much appreciated as political theory classes are tough). Even with large class sizes, he tries to learn everyone's names. I cannot recommend him enough!

He teaches about political theorists, and his style of teaching allows for those theorists to be more accessible for an average government student. The tests are in-class essays and he will usually offer two prompts. One that is reciting the stances of the writers and then an opportunity to outline an interpretation of the text.

analysis.name: Devangi Parikh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 133 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Parikh does not present the material in a way that is understandable. She does not explain things well and does not answer questions well. She also gives us important content in the lecture before the test, provides no practice problems/ practice exams before and then asks us a difficult question about a concept just taught. Would not take again.

She's too smart for her own good, explains concepts abstractly then speeds through the 1-2 examples done in lecture as if we should know it already. Have to master content in 1-3 days for the weekly quizzes. "Practice test" is useless and homework includes untaught material. While grading is lenient and she's nice, the course has its flaws.

terrible professor please try to get a different professor if possible just awfully structured class with below mediocre teaching

EDIT: final was terrible 0 resources to help prepare

Parikh is genuinely a sweet professor if you know her fr. She seems scary but she's actually chill. Long lectures, lots of material, make sure to lock in. Participation grade based on videos and attendance. Study A LOT every day and prep for dreadful weekly quizzes. TAs are goated they lowkenuinely carried my grade.

She doesn't really prepare you for the tests, she puts topics barely covered in the class and expects students to magically be able to answer the questions, And starts whining in class when students do bad on a test she didn't prepare us for

analysis.name: Deepa Thomas
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures help a ton to learn the concepts with a ton of slides, but you won't do well on the exams without completing the weekly Quest homework. I thought that Professor Thomas was very well-versed on the content and explained concepts very well. Checked understanding with instapolls so that you could see if you knew the concept. Overhated tbh

Didn't buy the textbook for this course and I was fine.  The lectures consisted of the prof reading from a note page so I never went.  Exams are online, taken at home, and open everything (notes, class materials, internet) so it wasn't too challenging but I don't think I got a good grasp of some content as a result of Dr. Thomas' teaching style.

Lectures and discussions were required but completely useless. She was really charismatic, but really did not help with actual graded things. Exams were 2/3 hw, 1/3 new stuff and the new stuff was always too hard. Failing averages on 2/3 midterms + the final with only multiple choice tests that offer no partial credit. She is a strict no curver.

Dr thomas was great. Her exams are literally HW problems + 1 or 2 conceptual questions, not hard if you study. She's nice and idk why people are complaining, I didn't have prior knowledge of physics and did fine. Practice hws and pay attention during her test review session. Discussion is useless but you only need to participate once. Great class.

DO NOT TAKE HER!!! Her accent is so strong and I would go to class and I literally could not understand a single thing she was saying. There are instapolls in class but she kind of stopped doing them because no one shows up to class. She often gets confused when working out problems in class. I tried teaching myself, but still makes no sense.

analysis.name: Dirk Mateer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Yeah this guy is the goat. If you show up to class and review the practice questions before exams I genuinely don't see how you'd get below an A. If you get a B or below in the class, it speaks volumes to you more than anything(coming from a 3.4 STEM major). Best lecturer I've had so far.

He makes his lectures fun and engaging, really made learning economics enjoyable. This is not an easy A you definitely have to put in the effort and study a lot to do well on exams. He provides practice questions for each chapter that are very similar to the ones on the tests, which helps a lot. Just study the practice questions and you will pass.

So fun and easily manageable while taking calc 1. There are lectures 2 a week, and they're really interesting. You read 1 chapter a week and do in-Quizitive every Tuesday by 8 pm. He does do in-class Kahoot's and Think-Pair-Shares for participation points, but we have 3 weeks left of classes, and almost everyone already has enough points.

I was dreading taking an economics class—I was a mostly straight A student in high school, but nearly failed macro. I took micro with Dr. Mateer, and honestly, it was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. He makes lectures fun and engaging with games and activities that demonstrate key economics concepts. I highly recommend! Take this class!

Dirk is the best professor I've had. Fantastic lecturer and a super forgiving grading system (everyone should get A's as long as they show up and try). Don't need to study too much for tests and very engaging in class as he gives out candy for participation & money for kahoot wins. Only downside to this glorious man is his nephew Mateer (OU's QB).

analysis.name: Dima Shamoun
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The exams cover a lot of material and the questions tend to be a lot more difficult then those on the homework. Even if you don't think the questions are difficult, it will be hard to complete all of the questions in the time frame since you aren't allowed to use a calculator. She does realize it's a difficult class so she grades on a rank scale.
Comically bad at teaching and comically unorganized. Avoid at all costs.

Do yourself a favor and avoid this class at all costs! coming from someone that cares about school and grades this class has quite literally ruined my GPA. The tests make up pretty much all the grades and are pretty much set up to fail you. The Homeworks are Difficult and the TA's are NOT willing to help and are completely different to the lectures

Please avoid this class at ALL COSTS. Coming from someone who cares about school and grades, I still found this class EXTREMELY difficult. If you have the option to take another professor use that to your advantage!!. This class very test heavy and the test have open ended questions which affects your grade immensely, and its set up to fail you.

This professor assigns a lot of homeworks, does not explain the material well and doesnt provide extra examples when students arent getting the concepts. Her tests are extremely difficult, and youre not allowed to use a calculator. So for the first exam youll find yourself having to calculate the midpoint formula BY HAND. Avoid at all costs.

analysis.name: daniel dillon
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very interesting class to take. Class discussions were very engaging and it is a class I looked forward to attending every week. You will need to read, but it is manageable. For the final project, you have a lot of freedom, which is nice. My only comment is that you need to study a lot for the midterm because grading can be harsh. Totally recommend

daniel was a great professor! the class itself, full transparency, it doesn't entirely fall in line with my belief system, however, he was very inviting, and it is truly a safe space to have a voice. as long as you did all that was required, i find it harder to fail than pass; i genuinely never stressed. be respectful, enjoy, and get a good giggle!

The professor lacked the professionalism and composure I would hope for in the way discussions were led. I feel like the lectures were helpful to understanding the material at the beginning of the course, but slowly moved away from meaningful discussion over time.

The class was fantastic! The lectures were super interesting and I really appreciated the way Dr dillon approached topics and he was funny. But the midterm was graded really harsh everything else is graded on completion so that's good.

The best SOC class I've taken! Prof. dillon is funny, engaging, caring, and taught me so much. Readings were amazing. Midterm is a test + essay (you get a day to do it), relatively easy. He makes it so you don't have to do the final but it's a creative project so I enjoyed it. I'll miss this class and I hope to take another with him in the future!

analysis.name: David DiCarlo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is not a very good professor. He does not have any industry experience and his background is just physics and water. I don't get why UT Austin keeps hiring inexperienced professors being so close to Houston. His lecture notes and writing are a mess. He makes us show memes every class, because of how boring it gets!

Is it fun? No, its thermo. DiCarlo makes it as enjoyable as thermo could possibly be though, and makes an effort to know all the students. Topics are not digestible just through lectures, and required lots of reviewing notes, textbooks, and office hours (always very approachable). Test heavy, but if you understand concepts, they aren't that bad.
Best class I've ever taken. People say it's hard, but it's so light if you just lock in. 10/10 would take again, all thanks to Professor DiCarlo

He is very disorganized and sloppy. He makes many mistakes. He is very hard to understand. No one understood what he was saying. The only thing good about him is that he had a good sense of humor, other than that, he is a terrible prof. I wouldn't recommend anyone taking a class with him.

Professor DiCarlo makes coming to class fun he stops the lectures halfway through class so students can stand up and tell dad jokes, a much needed break from a 1.5 hour lecture of heavy material. He cares about each student and makes an effort to learn everyones name and interests. Thermo is a hard subject but he keeps you invested and tests easy.

analysis.name: Todd Ditmire
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ditmire is clearly a very talented physicist, but he falls short when it comes to actually teaching students. He moves VERY quickly through his notes. His notes are terribly organized which makes it even harder to keep up with him. He does not give enough time on instapolls and closes them abruptly. You will have to learn on your own.

There are no lecture slides or recordings - he derives equations on a chalkboard the whole time. If you fall behind in this class, it is almost impossible to catch up because you don't even know what topics are being covered (again, no slides). All assignments and tests are online, un-proctored, but still very difficult. Final is 45% of your grade.

DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY. should retire atp, no one would miss him here. don't ask questions because he'll look at you like you're challenged. also changed tests from take home to in class, tests are 26 questions long, final is 45% of the grade. just evil work all throughout. also he's from prague (he'll make sure you know this)

Great guy, less so of a professor, but if having a professor interested in his work pulls you in as well you'd do perfect. Caution though as final is worth 50% of grade and guessing on his exams is next to impossible.

One of the worst professor in UT, he did a terrible job to explain the material and the tests are hard. Final exam take 50% of the whole grade. I won't take him if I have to retake engineer physics one more time.

analysis.name: Isil Dillig
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Isil's a terribly professor overall, but she's great as a person. She also gives out candies in class. Well, honestly, her lectures and TAs were both pretty terribly when I took the course, so I hope you at least get decent TAs. The key to doing well in the class is to get the textbook (pdf available), read it, practice the problems before lecture.

The class is very well prepared, it has very good slides. The presentation is extremely clear. If you ever read Isil's paper, you will know why. Even if there are things unclear, if someone asks, Isil would like to explain in more detail.  No project at all. Light homework, but there are exams. Workload OK.  BTW, I took the class three years back.

There's a lot of material. Though Isil explains it well, it's covered too quickly during class. I recommend going to class, reviewing notes afterwards, doing the homework, and looking in the textbook for extra problems to practice for the challenging tests. Just doing what's required may not be enough if you want to excel. Practice is key to an A.

We had weekly quizzes instead of psets and they can't put problems which require lots of thinking on the quizzes, unfortunately making the class very mechanical. Dr. Dillig goes very fast in lecture, but she's willing to stop and explain if needed (and she brings candy!). Curve is also very generous; I wouldn't stress over exam grades.

Dr. Dillig is not a good professor. She lectures way too quickly, is barely accessible outside of class, and mostly dismisses student questions. She also assigns HW due the day before the test, even though the material is assessed on a later exam. Despite the generous curve, wouldn't recommend taking her classes.

analysis.name: C Tyler Dick
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed the class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it will count towards your final grade. He was very good at ensuring all students could determine the civil engineering sub-discipline that best fit their interests throughout the class. He is very patient and has a nice personality. I enjoyed the guest lectures thoroughly and the class was easy.

Dr. Dick is a very nice guy. Helped students learn about different disciplines in civil engineering and brought in other profs for guest lectures. There is a lab, but it is not hard as long as you work with your group and listen to the TA's and Dr. Dick's instructions. Emphasis on nice guy, he was probably one of the chillest profs ive had.

Attendance isnt mandatory but he does in-class assignments every class day that counts towards final grade. The labs are easy but the TA's are kind of tough graders for the lab reports. I highly recommend you take ARE217 before this class because you will need to know basics of AutoCAD for some of the projects.

Your grade is basically dependent on your group project! He is very passionate about what he does and encourages students to find their area of interest as well. He is always open to criticism and has a few assignments asking us for our opinions on the class and civil engineering as a whole.

An excellent lecturer who consistently provides valuable feedback to students on projects and helps them develop software skills in MicroStation. Course materials are slides. He is incredibly patient, guiding students through step-by-step calculations in class. If you stay engaged and follow along, you'll definitely succeed.

analysis.name: Diane Rhodes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Had 327/334 w/her. Cons: Often shows disregard for students that aren't liberal, made evident by political commentary. At times, passive aggressive in response. Little to no feedback. Pros: Accessible by email and after class. Accepted late work and gave a few xtra credit opportunities.

One of my favorite professors I've had. She's passionate about her work and is very open to listening to her students talk about any subject and will keep it going. She makes sure we participate but doesn't make us feel pressured to. Easy grader and easy going. Make sure to read so that you can participate.

I took two courses with Professor Rhodes this semester, SW334 and SW327, and she was amazing in both. She is very caring and flexible, which I appreciate. I enjoyed her insight and hearing about her experiences as a social worker. She is also crazy funny. Wish I could take more courses with her because I feel she has so much wisdom to share.

Rhodes was a decent professor but the classes were boring and not engaging. The asynchronous setting was not helpful for this, but all we did was watch videos and go over slides that were already posted in canvas. The assignments weren't very helpful for learning the material and weren't related to the lectures. Paper was easy.

Dr. Rhodes is amazing, she is so charismatic and funny and honest. Classes with her are really fun and full of really great discussion. She is very laid back and understanding. I'm taking Foundations of Social Justice with her; 3 papers and a take home final. A lot of reading but it's all very interesting. Super kind and accessible. Adore her!!!

analysis.name: Dhiraj Murthy
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great course & fantastic professor! He cares and is truly invested. All students should take his class because data privacy is becoming so important. Recommend getting txtbk online, hw is easy if you go to lab, and tests are tricky if you don't do optional quizzes. ATTENDANCE MANDATORY and can help push your grade if needed.

Every week we had to read about 30-50 pages of the textbook and take a quiz. There were two exams which covered very knit-picky details from the textbook so you had to take very good notes and study well to do okay. Professor was available. Wasn't prepared to have to do so much work for a class outside of my major.

Professor wanted students to recite textbook info through quizzes rather than learn course concepts and hardly provided genuine engagement. For this online course, he didn't provide video lectures or assignments outside of what came with the book ($135 and required). The course covered basic computer concepts and was not what was advertised.

analysis.name: Dragan Djurdjanovic
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Djurdjanovic makes this class very accessible to someone with no background in programming. The class starts out quite slow, but about halfway through the semester difficulty skyrockets and you'll need to put in 10 hours of homework/labs a week.

It isn't hard, though—and extra credit makes the class an easy A.

Lectures really only explained the theory of what you do, not actually coding it, which made the homework tedious and reliant on self-teaching. The homework/lab assignments are fine, just long in the middle units of the course. Take-home tests are a blessing, though, so keep up with the class, and an A is very possible.

Phenomenal professor with some of the best lectures I've ever seen at UT. He is truly passionate about numerical methods and isn't afraid to show that. It's a shame that his TAs are among the harshest graders I have ever witnessed. One of his TAs reeked of sanctimony whenever she graded my assignments (ex. losing 5+ pts for wrong plot color/marker)

Dr. Djurdjanovic was incredibly helpful in and out of class. He answered questions well, and provided a lot of assistance understanding the material. He also offered a ton of extra credit. The material isn't very difficult, and all formulas are outlined clearly in the lecture notes posted to canvas. If you're stuck, go to office hours.
He likes to go on about his own research, but you can tell he loves the subject. He cares a lot about his students, especially if you go to office hours. Take him if you can

analysis.name: Lauren Dobbs
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Dobbs was probably my favorite professor that I've had in the Neuro department so far. She makes lectures super interesting and the material easy to understand! Exams are challenging, but not unreasonably so, and she always includes extra credit points at the end of each exam. Highly recommend taking her class.
I LOVED DOBBS!! The course is fantastic, but there is a ton of content. I thought the tests were pretty fair, but I'd highly recommend reading through the textbook and paying attention in lecture!
Loved it, made me love neuro more

Really sweet lady, but the extremely dense lectures are not recorded. Difficult exams. Study wiith friends to prepare for exams because you might miss some information (since lectures are not recorded) that may be tested on the exam. TA's grade a bit harshly on homeworks, so make sure you really understand the papers. Do NOT cram for the final.

Class was easy as long as you didn't cram. What helped me ace every exam was going through lectures and reading the book to help answer the study guides she gave us. The study guides were pretty straight-forward and similar to the information she tests on. I made the info into anki flashcards and that's what worked best. An A is very doable.

analysis.name: Donna Kornhaber
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Y'all this woman is my goat. I had her for LAH 350: Best Pictures (which wasn't an option on RMP oops) and it was my favorite class I've ever taken. She knows everything about film formalism and I respect her so much. Just do the assignments and stay engaged in class and she'll love you. I can't hype her up enough I loveeeee her.

Dr. Kornhaber is amazing!! She is the most kind and flexible professor I've ever had. Every opinion, insight, or thought is welcome in her classroom and she never makes a student feel stupid. The content is amazing and has changed how I watch movies for the better. Highly recommend to take her, she is beyond great!

Dr. Kornhaber's class is interesting and teaches you a lot about film. The course load seems daunting with all of the books and films you are assigned, but you can get away with just writing about films. I would recommend watching the films (which are all classics anyway) and just spark-noting the readings. The discussions are boring but required.

The class can be very interesting or boring but shes very nice and really wants you to learn the material. You do not have to do too much work on the essays and she gives you plenty of options to write on so you aren't limited.  The class was fun and very interesting. Make sure to use the university writing center. It helps a ton in this class.

Very fun class! Watching movies as homework was great. Except when you watch movies in class you might fall asleep. She is very flexible with watching the movies and reading the books because she understands we have other classes. Grading depends mostly on TAs however, but still an easy A.

analysis.name: Donnie Sackey
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Sackey lectures, TA's grade. His lectures are very interesting, random, and engaging. Just engage with him during lecture to make him feel a little more love. He is a great source of advice when doing the actual assignments for the class, but make sure to give him time to respond. He also had a great dynamic with Dr. Laude in joint lectures.

Dr. Sackey is the best! I've taken him for a few classes and he is a very understanding professor who likes to push his students to perform WITHOUT hurting their grade. I wish all my professors were like him.

Topic: Rhetoric & Data Visualization | Excellent (and hilarious) professor! I'd recommend this to any STEM major. You'll not just learn to write but make great PowerPoints. Btw, don't be scared by "98 = A". Like 75% of the grade is participation *and* there's enough extra credit opportunities to bring that down to a de facto 94.
very funny and pretty nice! sometimes he can be blunt but i think its more of his sense of humor ... dont take him too seriously lol

Professor Sackey is one of the best professors I had at UT so far. He always gives extensive feedback, makes lectures super interesting, and has a lot of office hours outside of class. He's kind, caring, helpful, and hilarious. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches! Would love to take a class with him again.

analysis.name: Stephen Donald
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Attend lectures and take detailed notes, and you will succeed in this class. Exams are doable if you study, and Professor Donald provides past exams. Homeworks are doable and done with Stata. One of the best professors in the department. Funny, kind, understanding, and intelligent.

There is lecture and lab which are graded separately. Prof Donald is very funny and always willing to talk to students. There are quizzes on some days but 2 or so are dropped & weekly homework which are graded on completion. Only 1 midterm and then final. Just study and you'll do fine for them. You will not pass if you do not do good in the lab.

He's a pretty fun and chill guy. Lectures are lowkey boring and slow but its also the nature of the course. Class is def not hard to get a good grade in (hw is on completion, some quizzes, and exams are curved). lots of practice for exams too. He's really funny without realizing it.
lots of hw but class was doable if you understand it. the hw is kinda confusing at first but it gets better. prof is nice and understanding.
Professor Donald makes Econometrics interesting. The grading is more than fair as he grades on a curve and the exams are straightforward.

analysis.name: Dongmei Chen
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures were very difficult to understand and not very helpful for studying. Lecture notes are just random screenshots from textbooks without any explanation. 85% of your grade is from tests. Did not explain concepts very well but was a generally reasonable grader. would try to find another professor if you want to learn controls though.
Lectures were detailed and example heavy. Very nice person who truly cares about students' learning and well-being. DSC is hard, but she makes it reasonable.
Very difficult class.  Definitely need to take a controls class prior to this class.  Nice teacher, hard to understand material.  Was pushed hard and learned a lot.

analysis.name: Emily Drumsta
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
I took Drumsta for ARA 611C, which wasn't an option on RMP.
She is an amazing professor! Class is always fun engaging. Other Arabic professors are just as kind and friendly, but Drumsta's class feels more interactive. Less rote memorization, more conversational learning. Her grading for ARA is not tough. Do the work, go to class, and you'll learn!

I took this class for my UGS, and I should have just waited another semester.  She did not keep students engaged or interested. Although I received an A-, I had to attend multiple extra office hours, which you shouldn't have to do to earn an A- in your UGS. Four in-class essays make up your entire course grade, with zero room for error or makeup.

I really wouldn't recommend taking this professor. A UGS shouldn't be as difficult as a STEM class, yet somehow it was (coming from a person who has only had A's and A-'s.) There was no reason at all to assign so many readings, and she isn't flexible at all. Avoid if you can.

Prof Drumsta claimed to be there for us and help with grades but us the toughest grader I've ever had. Consistently gave out C's on essays that take the entirety of your grade. A C is a 55 for this class which means it should not be possible to get a consistent C on every exam while changing how I'm approaching them. DO NOT TAKE HER

Extremely strict and a tough grader. Class seems manageable but she changes the grades very last minute causing significant grade drops. Participation worth 20% and no remorse shown for students that show up late. Rarely gives out 100s even when deserved. Takes points off for "grade-grubbing" leaving students hopeless. Save yourself the headache.

analysis.name: David Laude
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 466 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Easiest chem professor!! An A is easy as long as you really learn the 20 question types that he provides for every exam! The quizzes in almost every class period really count a lot towards your grade so they will help a lot if you do good on them, which is manageable because he gives quiz reviews for each one.

I am seeing a lot of reviews that talk a bit down on Dr. Laude with most of them saying that he is an easy A and he does not actually teach anything, which is because he runs a reverse classroom. Many of the people writing these reviews are privileged to have a professor like Dr. Laude as he really helps students transition to college chemistry.

There are LOTS of ways to make an A in this class. His grading scheme is pretty easy, but as a teacher, I don't think he's that great. His lectures can be very confusing and the tests are difficult. If you took AP Chem in HS and did well, I recommend his class, but otherwise (if you have little chem background), I would find a different teacher.

Strange teaching style where you have to learn the content mostly by yourself before class (which takes a longgg time), but Dr.Laude gives LOTS of great advice on self-studying and provides the best chem materials ever! So A's are easy to get as long as you follow his suggestions. 
Take this class if you wanna learn how to study and get an A.

Dr. Laude is no doubt an intelligent man and dedicated professor. You can exempt the final if you do moderatley well on his tests, complete the modules, AND DO WELL ON QUIZZES. You're essentially guaranteed an A if you can get into his class. He emphasizes big picture topics and leaves you to learn the rest but provides so many TA and office hours.

analysis.name: Andrew Bako
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Take a class taught by him if you like wasting your time and money and enjoy being perpetually confused. He doesn't make sense when he talks and expected an unreasonable amount of work. Don't take any class taught by him, one of the worst architecture profs ever. How does he keep getting hired, do schools check student reviews ever? Waste of time!!

At front the workload is not insane it is the way its presented and worded that makes it unbearable, repeating the same terms over and over and over as if we would just understand if repeated once more. Incredibly confusing, burn out before midreview season, never had in-studio reviews, 1st time I gen considered dropping out, must stay locked in

Absolutely terrible. Hands down, Bako is the worst professor I have had at UT! He is so incompetent! Who hired him? Shame on UT Austin. All the reviews are accurate. He gave bizarre, unclear assignments and asked for a stupid load of work. He was rude and unsupportive. I am pretty sure this class ruined my GPA and chances of getting internship.

This professor will give you the most intense design semester of your life. I would say Andrew or Andy was too intense with his students and expected unobtainable perfection from every student. Somehow our year made him proud, but a lot of the students are mentally burnt out after the semester.

analysis.name: Eric Drott
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class has a few essays, but I feel like they are all doable if you go to office hours/ask the TA/Dr. Drott questions! You should take advantage of their feedback, as Dr. Drott is very particular about his grading (esp for essays). However, it is very doable to get an A on essays and FRQ quizzes. Dr. Drott overall just wants you to succeed!

Good UGS if you put the effort in, helps to have an interest in music. Sort of a picky grader, so ask for feedback before turning in papers. Three 2-3 pg papers, 2 quizzes w/ 4 open-ended questions on concepts (only 1 quiz counted!), final project. Minimal participation required, attendance is graded (although they do not care if you are late)

Didn't pay attention in a single lecture (attendance is mandatory & apart of your grade) and got an A. Essays are pretty hefty and he's a very picky grader. Overall easy but the essays sneak up on you if you don't start soon enough. Wouldn't do if you hate writing.

Very particular on grading for essays but provides clear and insightful feedback. Interest in music and/or politics helps in being engaged by lectures but Drott is a great lecturer. Big assignments can sneak up but overall an interesting and worthwhile course.

I've been genuinely interested in music since I've played instruments for most of my life, but the class really wasn't what I was expecting in aligning with my interests. It was a lot more conceptual. The grading I felt was pretty harsh, but very clear feedback, though, so you can fix it for the next assignment.

analysis.name: Andrew Loveridge
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 108 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: As head instructor, this course is honestly a disgrace to what UT represents. The lab instructions are vague, and one's grade is dependent on the TA. The lab practical is an absolute joke, with such limited time to do 3 experiments in 75 minutes- with the amount of calculations you need to do. While I got an A, this class nearly gave me a stroke.

Loveridge is genuinely just an outstanding professor. Ignore the other reviews for the lab sections. Those are TA dependent. When talking about Loveridge himself, his lectures are excellent, he cares about his students, and he goes to extra lengths to ensure we succeed. Thermodynamics can be difficult but he made it approachable! Highly recommend.

Worst class ever. You have to take it as a pre-med. The grade depends on the TA. The instructions are super vague, and you get points taken off for criteria you didn't know existed. Least favorite class I've taken at UT by far.

Never met the guy he j oversees the course but all the TAs r useless; NEVER RESPOND TO ED DISCUSSION OR EMAILS when students bring up many issues; lack of communication is crazy and is the most disorganized course I have ever taken at UT with the most indifferent TAs; lab notes r annoying

Physics 1 lab is probably the easiest stem class I've taken. Experiments and reports are simple, I guess it depends in you TA but mine was fantastic. Lab practical isn't bad as long as you study. It's a good amount of work for 1 credit but it is what it is.

analysis.name: Zena Drakou
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I think these reviews are a bit harsh. Database is an easy and manageable course if you just studied and tried on the exams (I would barely attend class and study a few days before the test). However, the course can be ambiguous and disorganized, which is why I think ppl are frustrated. It's not a "free" A, but with minimal effort you will do well.

Zena Drakous is genuinely the worst professors I've had at UT. Her course is incredibly disorganized, exams weigh so much but only consist of few questions with incredibly vague instruction, but are graded extremely harshly. This is the worst classes I've taken--it's making me question the quality of the MIS/ BAX program here at UT. DON'T TAKE ZENA

The other reviews are pretty clear. She's kind, but the class has no structure. Slides don't match the textbook, which doesn't match the activities or homework. Expectation is that you know how to code, because time isn't given in class for it. Exams are cumulative and coding heavy. Be prepared to spend time outside of class studying and coding.

Zena is nice but I didn't find her lectures helpful. Vague "headcount" attendance?? Tests are tricky, read test questions carefully & know the code from the KCs + HW. This class is basically self taught from the textbook so actually read it and take notes yourself. If you want an A, take textbook notes each week instead of cramming like me lol

This class was hard. I think Zena is getting more hate than she deserves, because the class was hard regardless of the professor. Like most people taking this class, I did not actually try on hws and just coasted through the semester using gpt. When it comes time to take the test, you'll regret that I promise. Just read the textbook! Lectures suck
